passages.original: Hardly knowing what she did, she picked up a little bit of stick, and held it out to the puppy; whereupon the puppy jumped into the air off all its feet at once, with a yelp of delight, and rushed at the stick, and made believe to worry it; then Alice dodged behind a great thistle, to keep herself from being run over; and the moment she appeared on the other side, the puppy made another rush at the stick, and tumbled head over heels in its hurry to get hold of it; then Alice, thinking it was very like having a game of play with a cart-horse, and expecting every moment to be trampled under its feet, ran round the thistle again; then the puppy began a series of short charges at the stick, running a very little way forwards each time and a long way back, and barking hoarsely all the while, till at last it sat down a good way off, panting, with its tongue hanging out of its mouth, and its great eyes half shut.
passages.vernacular: 佢幾乎唔知道自己喺做乜嘢,撿起一小根樹枝,舉畀小狗;小狗於是四隻爪子同時離地跳到空中,歡喜地叫咗一聲,向樹枝撲去,假裝撕咬佢;然後愛麗絲躲到一大叢薊後面,免得被撞倒;佢一從另一邊露面,小狗又向樹枝撲去,急住去抓佢而翻咗個跟頭;然後愛麗絲覺得呢個好像係同一匹拉車嘅馬玩耍,隨時預料自己會被佢嘅腳踩到,於是又繞住薊跑;然後小狗開始對樹枝發起一連串短促嘅衝鋒,每次向前跑啲點,往後退好長一段,同時一直嘶啞地吠叫,最後佢坐喺遠遠嘅地方,喘住氣,舌頭從嘴裡耷拉出嚟,大眼睛半閉住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她幾乎不知道自己在做什麼,撿起一小根樹枝,舉給小狗;小狗於是四隻爪子同時離地跳到空中,歡喜地叫了一聲,向樹枝撲去,假裝撕咬它;然後愛麗絲躲到一大叢薊後面,免得被撞倒;她一從另一邊露面,小狗又向樹枝撲去,急著去抓它而翻了個跟頭;然後愛麗絲覺得這很像是和一匹拉車的馬玩耍,隨時預料自己會被它的腳踩到,於是又繞著薊跑;然後小狗開始對樹枝發起一連串短促的衝鋒,每次向前跑一點點,往後退很長一段,同時一直嘶啞地吠叫,最後它坐在遠遠的地方,喘著氣,舌頭從嘴裡耷拉出來,大眼睛半閉著。

passages.original: This seemed to Alice a good opportunity for making her escape; so she set off at once, and ran till she was quite tired and out of breath, and till the puppy’s bark sounded quite faint in the distance.
passages.vernacular: 呢喺愛麗絲睇來係個逃走嘅好機會;所以佢即刻動身,一直跑到相當累、上氣不接下氣,直到小狗嘅吠叫喺遠處聽起嚟好微弱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這在愛麗絲看來是個逃走的好機會;所以她立刻動身,一直跑到相當累、上氣不接下氣,直到小狗的吠叫在遠處聽起來很微弱。

passages.original: “And yet what a dear little puppy it was!” said Alice, as she leant against a buttercup to rest herself, and fanned herself with one of the leaves: “I should have liked teaching it tricks very much, if—if I’d only been the right size to do it! Oh dear! I’d nearly forgotten that I’ve got to grow up again! Let me see—how is it to be managed? I suppose I ought to eat or drink something or other; but the great question is, what?”
passages.vernacular: 「不過佢係幾咁可愛嘅小狗啊!」愛麗絲講,靠喺一朵毛茛花上休息,用一片葉子畀自己扇風:「我好想教佢把戲,如果——如果我係合適嘅大小就好喇!哎呀!我幾乎忘咗我仲得長大!讓我想想——呢要點算?我想我應該食點或飲點乜嘢;但關鍵問題係,食乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是它是多麼可愛的小狗啊!」愛麗絲說,靠在一朵毛茛花上休息,用一片葉子給自己扇風:「我非常想教它把戲,如果——如果我是合適的大小就好了!哎呀!我幾乎忘了我還得長大!讓我想想——這要怎麼辦?我想我應該吃點或喝點什麼;但關鍵問題是,吃什麼?」

passages.original: The great question certainly was, what? Alice looked all round her at the flowers and the blades of grass, but she did not see anything that looked like the right thing to eat or drink under the circumstances. There was a large mushroom growing near her, about the same height as herself; and when she had looked under it, and on both sides of it, and behind it, it occurred to her that she might as well look and see what was on the top of it.
passages.vernacular: 關鍵問題確實係,乜嘢?愛麗絲環顧四周嘅花同草葉,但冇睇到任何睇上去適合喺呢種情況下食或飲嘅嘢。佢附近長住一朵大蘑菇,同佢差不多高;佢睇咗蘑菇下面、兩邊同後面之後,忽然想到佢不妨睇睇佢嘅頂上有乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 關鍵問題確實是,什麼?愛麗絲環顧四周的花和草葉,但沒有看到任何看上去適合在這種情況下吃或喝的東西。她附近長著一朵大蘑菇,和她差不多高;她看了蘑菇下面、兩邊和後面之後,忽然想到她不妨看看它的頂上有什麼。

passages.original: She stretched herself up on tiptoe, and peeped over the edge of the mushroom, and her eyes immediately met those of a large blue caterpillar, that was sitting on the top with its arms folded, quietly smoking a long hookah, and taking not the smallest notice of her or of anything else.
passages.vernacular: 佢踮起腳尖,伸長身體,從蘑菇邊緣向上窺視,佢嘅眼睛即刻同一隻大藍毛毛蟲嘅眼睛相遇,佢正坐喺頂上,雙臂交疊,安靜地抽住一支長長嘅水煙筒,對佢或其他任何事啲都不理會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她踮起腳尖,伸長身體,從蘑菇邊緣向上窺視,她的眼睛立刻與一隻大藍毛毛蟲的眼睛相遇,它正坐在頂上,雙臂交疊,安靜地抽著一支長長的水煙筒,對她或其他任何事一點也不理會。

chapters.title: Ch. V Advice from a Caterpillar 第五章:毛毛蟲的忠告

passages.original: The Caterpillar and Alice looked at each other for some time in silence: at last the Caterpillar took the hookah out of its mouth, and addressed her in a languid, sleepy voice.
passages.vernacular: 毛毛蟲同愛麗絲默默地互相睇咗一會兒:最後毛毛蟲把水煙筒從嘴裡攞出嚟,用慵懶困倦嘅聲音對佢講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 毛毛蟲和愛麗絲默默地互相看了一會兒:最後毛毛蟲把水煙筒從嘴裡拿出來,用慵懶困倦的聲音對她說話。

passages.original: “Who are you?” said the Caterpillar.
passages.vernacular: 「你係邊個?」毛毛蟲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你是誰?」毛毛蟲說。

passages.original: This was not an encouraging opening for a conversation. Alice replied, rather shyly, “I—I hardly know, sir, just at present—at least I know who I was when I got up this morning, but I think I must have been changed several times since then.”
passages.vernacular: 呢並唔係一個令人鼓舞嘅對話開頭。愛麗絲相當羞怯地回答:「我——我幾乎唔知道,先生,就喺此刻——至少我知道今日朝早起床時我係邊個,但我想自嗰以後我一定被變咗好幾次。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這並不是一個令人鼓舞的對話開頭。愛麗絲相當羞怯地回答:「我——我幾乎不知道,先生,就在此刻——至少我知道今天早上起床時我是誰,但我想自那以後我一定被變了好幾次。」

passages.original: “What do you mean by that?” said the Caterpillar sternly. “Explain yourself!”
passages.vernacular: 「你呢個係乜嘢意思?」毛毛蟲嚴厲地講。「解釋你自己!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你這是什麼意思?」毛毛蟲嚴厲地說。「解釋你自己!」

passages.original: “I can’t explain myself, I’m afraid, sir,” said Alice, “because I’m not myself, you see.”
passages.vernacular: 「恐怕我唔能夠解釋我自己,先生,」愛麗絲講,「因為你瞧,我唔係我自己喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「恐怕我不能解釋我自己,先生,」愛麗絲說,「因為你瞧,我不是我自己了。」

passages.original: “I don’t see,” said the Caterpillar.
passages.vernacular: 「我不瞧,」毛毛蟲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不瞧,」毛毛蟲說。

passages.original: “I’m afraid I can’t put it more clearly,” Alice replied very politely, “for I can’t understand it myself to begin with; and being so many different sizes in a day is very confusing.”
passages.vernacular: 「恐怕我唔能夠講得更清楚喇,」愛麗絲好有禮貌地回答,「因為我自己起頭就不明白;一天裡有咁多不同嘅大小,好令人困惑。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「恐怕我不能說得更清楚了,」愛麗絲非常有禮貌地回答,「因為我自己起頭就不明白;一天裡有這麼多不同的大小,非常令人困惑。」

passages.original: “It isn’t,” said the Caterpillar.
passages.vernacular: 「才唔會,」毛毛蟲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「才不會,」毛毛蟲說。

passages.original: “Well, perhaps you haven’t found it so yet,” said Alice; “but when you have to turn into a chrysalis—you will some day, you know—and then after that into a butterfly, I should think you’ll feel it a little queer, won’t you?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,或者你仲冇發現,」愛麗絲講;「但係等你唔得不變成蛹——你總有一天會嘅,你知道——然後喺嗰之後變成蝴蝶,我想你會覺得有點古怪,唔係嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,也許你還沒有發現,」愛麗絲說;「但是等你不得不變成蛹——你總有一天會的,你知道——然後在那之後變成蝴蝶,我想你會覺得有點古怪,不是嗎?」

passages.original: “Not a bit,” said the Caterpillar.
passages.vernacular: 「啲都不,」毛毛蟲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一點也不,」毛毛蟲說。

passages.original: “Well, perhaps your feelings may be different,” said Alice; “all I know is, it would feel very queer to me.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,或者你嘅感覺可能不同,」愛麗絲講;「我只知道,我會覺得好古怪。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,也許你的感覺可能不同,」愛麗絲說;「我只知道,我會覺得非常古怪。」

passages.original: “You!” said the Caterpillar contemptuously. “Who are you?”
passages.vernacular: 「你!」毛毛蟲輕蔑地講。「你係邊個?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你!」毛毛蟲輕蔑地說。「你是誰?」

passages.original: Which brought them back again to the beginning of the conversation. Alice felt a little irritated at the Caterpillar’s making such very short remarks, and she drew herself up and said, very gravely, “I think, you ought to tell me who you are, first.”
passages.vernacular: 呢又把佢哋帶回咗對話嘅開頭。愛麗絲對毛毛蟲講咁簡短嘅話有點惱火,佢挺直身子,好嚴肅地講:「我想,你應該先告訴我你係邊個。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這又把他們帶回了對話的開頭。愛麗絲對毛毛蟲說這麼簡短的話有點惱火,她挺直身子,非常嚴肅地說:「我想,你應該先告訴我你是誰。」

passages.original: “Why?” said the Caterpillar.
passages.vernacular: 「點解?」毛毛蟲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為什麼?」毛毛蟲說。

passages.original: Here was another puzzling question; and as Alice could not think of any good reason, and as the Caterpillar seemed to be in a very unpleasant state of mind, she turned away.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係又一個令人困惑嘅問題;愛麗絲想不出任何好理由,而毛毛蟲似乎處喺好不愉快嘅心情中,佢就轉身走開喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是又一個令人困惑的問題;愛麗絲想不出任何好理由,而毛毛蟲似乎處在非常不愉快的心情中,她就轉身走開了。

passages.original: “Come back!” the Caterpillar called after her. “I’ve something important to say!”
passages.vernacular: 「回嚟!」毛毛蟲喺佢身後喊。「我有重要嘅話要講!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「回來!」毛毛蟲在她身後喊。「我有重要的話要說!」

passages.original: This sounded promising, certainly: Alice turned and came back again.
passages.vernacular: 呢聽起嚟確實有希望:愛麗絲轉身又回嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這聽起來確實有希望:愛麗絲轉身又回來了。

passages.original: “Keep your temper,” said the Caterpillar.
passages.vernacular: 「保持你嘅脾氣,」毛毛蟲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「保持你的脾氣,」毛毛蟲說。

passages.original: “Is that all?” said Alice, swallowing down her anger as well as she could.
passages.vernacular: 「就呢啲?」愛麗絲講,儘量吞下怒氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就這些?」愛麗絲說,儘量吞下怒氣。

passages.original: “No,” said the Caterpillar.
passages.vernacular: 「不,」毛毛蟲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,」毛毛蟲說。

passages.original: Alice thought she might as well wait, as she had nothing else to do, and perhaps after all it might tell her something worth hearing. For some minutes it puffed away without speaking, but at last it unfolded its arms, took the hookah out of its mouth again, and said, “So you think you’re changed, do you?”
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲想佢不妨等住,因為佢冇別嘅事可做,或者佢終究會告訴佢點值得一聽嘅嘢。有咁幾分鐘佢噴雲吐霧,冇講話,但最後佢鬆開雙臂,又把水煙筒從嘴裡攞出嚟,講:「咁你認為你被變喇,係嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲想她不妨等著,因為她沒有別的事可做,也許它終究會告訴她點值得一聽的東西。有那麼幾分鐘它噴雲吐霧,沒說話,但最後它鬆開雙臂,又把水煙筒從嘴裡拿出來,說:「那麼你認為你被變了,是嗎?」

passages.original: “I’m afraid I am, sir,” said Alice; “I can’t remember things as I used—and I don’t keep the same size for ten minutes together!”
passages.vernacular: 「我恐怕係嘅,先生,」愛麗絲講;「我唔能夠像過去嗰樣記事喇——而且我連好鐘都保持不咗同樣嘅大小!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我恐怕是的,先生,」愛麗絲說;「我不能像過去那樣記事了——而且我連十分鐘都保持不了同樣的大小!」

passages.original: “Can’t remember what things?” said the Caterpillar.
passages.vernacular: 「唔能夠記起乜嘢事?」毛毛蟲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不能記起什麼事?」毛毛蟲說。

passages.original: “Well, I’ve tried to say “How doth the little busy bee,” but it all came different!” Alice replied in a very melancholy voice.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我試住背『小蜜蜂多忙碌』,但全都念得不一樣喇!」愛麗絲用好憂鬱嘅聲音回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我試著背『小蜜蜂多忙碌』,但全都念得不一樣了!」愛麗絲用非常憂鬱的聲音回答。

passages.original: “Repeat, ‘You are old, Father William,’” said the Caterpillar.
passages.vernacular: 「背『你老喇,威廉爹爹』,」毛毛蟲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「背『你老了,威廉爹爹』,」毛毛蟲說。

passages.original: Alice folded her hands, and began:—
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲交握雙手,開始背:——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲交握雙手,開始背:——

passages.original: “You are old, Father William,” the young man said, “And your hair has become very white; And yet you incessantly stand on your head— Do you think, at your age, it is right?”
passages.vernacular: 「『你老喇,威廉爹爹,』年輕人講,『你嘅頭髮已經變得好白;可你卻不停地倒立——你認為以你嘅年紀,咁樣合適嗎?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『你老了,威廉爹爹,』年輕人說,『你的頭髮已經變得很白;可你卻不停地倒立——你認為以你的年紀,這樣合適嗎?』

passages.original: “In my youth,” Father William replied to his son, “I feared it might injure the brain; But, now that I’m perfectly sure I have none, Why, I do it again and again.”
passages.vernacular: 『我年輕嘅時候,』威廉爹爹回答佢兒子,『我怕呢會傷腦子;不過而家我完全確定我根本冇腦子,哎呀,我就一次又一次地做。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 『我年輕的時候,』威廉爹爹回答他兒子,『我怕這會傷腦子;可是現在我完全確定我根本沒有腦子,哎呀,我就一次又一次地做。』

passages.original: “You are old,” said the youth, “as I mentioned before, And have grown most uncommonly fat; Yet you turned a back-somersault in at the door— Pray, what is the reason of that?”
passages.vernacular: 『你老喇,』年輕人講,『我以前提過,而且你長得特別地胖;可你卻翻咗個後空翻進門——請問,呢個係乜嘢原因?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 『你老了,』年輕人說,『我以前提過,而且你長得特別地胖;可你卻翻了個後空翻進門——請問,這是什麼原因?』

passages.original: “In my youth,” said the sage, as he shook his grey locks, “I kept all my limbs very supple By the use of this ointment—one shilling the box— Allow me to sell you a couple?”
passages.vernacular: 『我年輕嘅時候,』智者搖住灰白嘅頭髮講,『我讓我所有嘅四肢都好靈活,靠嘅係呢種藥膏——一先令一盒——讓我賣畀你哋兩盒好嗎?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 『我年輕的時候,』智者搖著灰白的頭髮說,『我讓我所有的四肢都非常靈活,靠的是這種藥膏——一先令一盒——讓我賣給你們兩盒好嗎?』

passages.original: “You are old,” said the youth, “and your jaws are too weak For anything tougher than suet; Yet you finished the goose, with the bones and the beak— Pray, how did you manage to do it?”
passages.vernacular: 『你老喇,』年輕人講,『你嘅下巴太弱,嚼不動比牛油更硬嘅嘢;可你卻把鵝連骨頭帶嘴都食光喇——請問,你係點做到嘅?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 『你老了,』年輕人說,『你的下巴太弱,嚼不動比牛油更硬的東西;可你卻把鵝連骨頭帶嘴都吃光了——請問,你是怎麼做到的?』

passages.original: “In my youth,” said his father, “I took to the law, And argued each case with my wife; And the muscular strength, which it gave to my jaw, Has lasted the rest of my life.”
passages.vernacular: 『我年輕嘅時候,』佢父親講,『我從事法律,同我老婆爭辯每個案子;佢畀我下巴嘅肌肉力量,保持咗我餘生。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 『我年輕的時候,』他父親說,『我從事法律,與我老婆爭辯每個案子;它給我下巴的肌肉力量,保持了我餘生。』

passages.original: “You are old,” said the youth, “one would hardly suppose That your eye was as steady as ever; Yet you balanced an eel on the end of your nose— What made you so awfully clever?”
passages.vernacular: 『你老喇,』年輕人講,『人哋好難想像你嘅眼睛仲像從前一樣穩;可你卻喺鼻尖上平衡一條鰻魚——係乜嘢讓你咁聰明得可怕?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 『你老了,』年輕人說,『人們很難想像你的眼睛還像從前一樣穩;可你卻在鼻尖上平衡一條鰻魚——是什麼讓你這麼聰明得可怕?』

passages.original: “I have answered three questions, and that is enough,” Said his father; “don’t give yourself airs! Do you think I can listen all day to such stuff? Be off, or I’ll kick you down stairs!”
passages.vernacular: 『我已經回答咗三個問題,夠喇,』佢父親講;『別擺架子!你以為我能整天聽呢種廢話嗎?滾開,否則我把你踢下樓去!』」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 『我已經回答了三個問題,夠了,』他父親說;『別擺架子!你以為我能整天聽這種廢話嗎?滾開,否則我把你踢下樓去!』」

passages.original: “That is not said right,” said the Caterpillar.
passages.vernacular: 「講得不對,」毛毛蟲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「說得不對,」毛毛蟲說。

passages.original: “Not quite right, I’m afraid,” said Alice, timidly; “some of the words have got altered.”
passages.vernacular: 「恐怕不太對,」愛麗絲膽怯地講;「有些詞變喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「恐怕不太對,」愛麗絲膽怯地說;「有些詞變了。」

passages.original: “It is wrong from beginning to end,” said the Caterpillar decidedly, and there was silence for some minutes.
passages.vernacular: 「從頭到尾都錯喇,」毛毛蟲斷然地講,接住沉默咗幾分鐘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「從頭到尾都錯了,」毛毛蟲斷然地說,接著沉默了幾分鐘。

passages.original: The Caterpillar was the first to speak.
passages.vernacular: 毛毛蟲先開咗口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 毛毛蟲先開了口。

passages.original: “What size do you want to be?” it asked.
passages.vernacular: 「你想要多大嘅個子?」佢問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你想要多大的個子?」它問。

passages.original: “Oh, I’m not particular as to size,” Alice hastily replied; “only one doesn’t like changing so often, you know.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我對大小不挑剔,」愛麗絲趕緊回答;「只係人不鍾意咁經常變,你知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我對大小不挑剔,」愛麗絲趕緊回答;「只是人不喜歡這麼經常變,你知道。」

passages.original: “I don’t know,” said the Caterpillar.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道,」毛毛蟲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道,」毛毛蟲說。

passages.original: Alice said nothing: she had never been so much contradicted in her life before, and she felt that she was losing her temper.
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲乜嘢都冇講:佢一生中從冇被咁樣頂撞過,佢覺得自己快要發脾氣喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲什麼也沒說:她一生中從沒被這樣頂撞過,她覺得自己快要發脾氣了。

passages.original: “Are you content now?” said the Caterpillar.
passages.vernacular: 「你而家滿意咗嗎?」毛毛蟲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你現在滿意了嗎?」毛毛蟲說。

passages.original: “Well, I should like to be a little larger, sir, if you wouldn’t mind,” said Alice: “three inches is such a wretched height to be.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我想稍微高啲,先生,如果您不介意嘅話,」愛麗絲講:「三英寸係個太可憐嘅高度。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我想稍微高一點,先生,如果您不介意的話,」愛麗絲說:「三英寸是個太可憐的高度。」

passages.original: “It is a very good height indeed!” said the Caterpillar angrily, rearing itself upright as it spoke (it was exactly three inches high).
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係個好好嘅高度!」毛毛蟲生氣地講,講住直起身子(佢正好三英寸高)。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是個非常好的高度!」毛毛蟲生氣地說,說著直起身子(它正好三英寸高)。

passages.original: “But I’m not used to it!” pleaded poor Alice in a piteous tone. And she thought of herself, “I wish the creatures wouldn’t be so easily offended!”
passages.vernacular: 「可我不習慣啊!」可憐嘅愛麗絲用淒惻嘅語調懇求。佢心想:「我真希望呢啲動物別咁容易被冒犯!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可我不習慣啊!」可憐的愛麗絲用淒惻的語調懇求。她心想:「我真希望這些動物別這麼容易被冒犯!」

passages.original: “You’ll get used to it in time,” said the Caterpillar; and it put the hookah into its mouth and began smoking again.
passages.vernacular: 「你過一陣子會習慣嘅,」毛毛蟲講;佢把水煙筒放進嘴裡,又開始抽起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你過一陣子會習慣的,」毛毛蟲說;它把水煙筒放進嘴裡,又開始抽起來。

passages.original: This time Alice waited patiently until it chose to speak again. In a minute or two the Caterpillar took the hookah out of its mouth and yawned once or twice, and shook itself. Then it got down off the mushroom, and crawled away in the grass, merely remarking as it went, “One side will make you grow taller, and the other side will make you grow shorter.”
passages.vernacular: 呢次愛麗絲耐心地等住,直到佢願意再開口。一兩分鐘後,毛毛蟲把水煙筒從嘴裡攞出嚟,打咗一兩個哈欠,抖咗抖身子。然後佢從蘑菇上爬下嚟,爬進草叢,走時只講咗一句:「一邊會讓你長高,另一邊會讓你變矮。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這次愛麗絲耐心地等著,直到它願意再開口。一兩分鐘後,毛毛蟲把水煙筒從嘴裡拿出來,打了一兩個哈欠,抖了抖身子。然後它從蘑菇上爬下來,爬進草叢,走時只說了一句:「一邊會讓你長高,另一邊會讓你變矮。」

passages.original: “One side of what? The other side of what?” thought Alice to herself.
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢嘅一邊?乜嘢嘅另一邊?」愛麗絲心想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼的一邊?什麼的另一邊?」愛麗絲心想。

passages.original: “Of the mushroom,” said the Caterpillar, just as if she had asked it aloud; and in another moment it was out of sight.
passages.vernacular: 「蘑菇嘅,」毛毛蟲講,好像佢大聲問咗出嚟一樣;轉眼佢就消失喺視線之外。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「蘑菇的,」毛毛蟲說,好像她大聲問了出來一樣;轉眼它就消失在視線之外。

passages.original: Alice remained looking thoughtfully at the mushroom for a minute, trying to make out which were the two sides of it; and as it was perfectly round, she found this a very difficult question. However, at last she stretched her arms round it as far as they would go, and broke off a bit of the edge with each hand.
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲若有所思地睇咗蘑菇一分鐘,想弄清楚邊兩邊係佢嘅兩邊;因為佢係完美嘅圓形,佢覺得呢個係個好難嘅問題。不過,最後佢盡量把雙臂環繞佢伸開,雙手各掰下邊緣嘅一小塊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲若有所思地看了蘑菇一分鐘,想弄清楚哪兩邊是它的兩邊;因為它是完美的圓形,她覺得這是個非常難的問題。不過,最後她盡量把雙臂環繞它伸開,雙手各掰下邊緣的一小塊。

passages.original: “And now which is which?” she said to herself, and nibbled a little of the right-hand bit to try the effect: the next moment she felt a violent blow underneath her chin: it had struck her foot!
passages.vernacular: 「咁而家邊一塊係邊一塊呢?」佢對自己講,啃咗啲右手嘅嗰塊,試試效果:下一刻佢覺得下巴下面挨咗猛烈嘅一擊:撞到咗佢嘅腳!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼現在哪一塊是哪一塊呢?」她對自己說,啃了一點右手的那塊,試試效果:下一刻她覺得下巴下面挨了猛烈的一擊:撞到了她的腳!

passages.original: She was a good deal frightened by this very sudden change, but she felt that there was no time to be lost, as she was shrinking rapidly; so she set to work at once to eat some of the other bit. Her chin was pressed so closely against her foot, that there was hardly room to open her mouth; but she did it at last, and managed to swallow a morsel of the lefthand bit.
passages.vernacular: 呢個好突然嘅變化讓佢嚇咗一大跳,但佢覺得時間唔能夠浪費,因為佢正在迅速縮小;所以佢即刻動手食另一塊。佢嘅下巴被緊緊壓喺腳上,幾乎冇地方張嘴;但佢最終做到喇,設法吞下咗一小口左手嘅嗰塊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個非常突然的變化讓她嚇了一大跳,但她覺得時間不能浪費,因為她正在迅速縮小;所以她立刻動手吃另一塊。她的下巴被緊緊壓在腳上,幾乎沒有地方張嘴;但她最終做到了,設法吞下了一小口左手的那塊。

passages.original: “Come, my head’s free at last!” said Alice in a tone of delight, which changed into alarm in another moment, when she found that her shoulders were nowhere to be found: all she could see, when she looked down, was an immense length of neck, which seemed to rise like a stalk out of a sea of green leaves that lay far below her.
passages.vernacular: 「好喇,我嘅頭終於自由喇!」愛麗絲用歡欣嘅語調講,呢語調轉眼間變成咗驚慌,因為佢發現自己嘅肩膀唔見喇:佢低頭睇時,所能睇到嘅只有一長段脖子,似乎像莖一樣從遠喺佢下面嘅一片綠葉海裡升起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了,我的頭終於自由了!」愛麗絲用歡欣的語調說,這語調轉眼間變成了驚慌,因為她發現自己的肩膀不見了:她低頭看時,所能看到的只有一長段脖子,似乎像莖一樣從遠在她下面的一片綠葉海裡升起。

passages.original: “What can all that green stuff be?” said Alice. “And where have my shoulders got to? And oh, my poor hands, how is it I can’t see you?” She was moving them about as she spoke, but no result seemed to follow, except a little shaking among the distant green leaves.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰啲綠嘢會係乜嘢?」愛麗絲講。「我嘅肩膀到邊兒去喇?仲有,哦,我可憐嘅手,我點睇唔見你哋喇?」佢講話時一直喺動佢哋,但似乎冇乜嘢結果,只係遠處嘅綠葉間有啲抖動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那些綠東西會是什麼?」愛麗絲說。「我的肩膀到哪兒去了?還有,哦,我可憐的手,我怎麼看不見你們了?」她說話時一直在動它們,但似乎沒有什麼結果,只是遠處的綠葉間有一點抖動。

passages.original: As there seemed to be no chance of getting her hands up to her head, she tried to get her head down to them, and was delighted to find that her neck would bend about easily in any direction, like a serpent. She had just succeeded in curving it down into a graceful zigzag, and was going to dive in among the leaves, which she found to be nothing but the tops of the trees under which she had been wandering, when a sharp hiss made her draw back in a hurry: a large pigeon had flown into her face, and was beating her violently with its wings.
passages.vernacular: 睇起嚟冇機會把手舉到頭上,佢便試住把頭低下嚟碰佢哋,佢高興地發現佢嘅脖子可以輕易地向任何方向彎曲,像一條蛇。佢剛成功地把佢彎成優美嘅之字形,正要鑽進樹葉堆,佢發現嗰不過係佢一直喺下面漫步嘅樹木嘅頂端,呢陣一聲尖銳嘅嘶叫讓佢急忙縮回:一隻大鴿子飛到佢臉上,用翅膀猛烈地拍打佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看起來沒有機會把手舉到頭上,她便試著把頭低下來碰它們,她高興地發現她的脖子可以輕易地向任何方向彎曲,像一條蛇。她剛成功地把它彎成優美的之字形,正要鑽進樹葉堆,她發現那不過是她一直在下面漫步的樹木的頂端,這時一聲尖銳的嘶叫讓她急忙縮回:一隻大鴿子飛到她臉上,用翅膀猛烈地拍打她。

passages.original: “Serpent!” screamed the Pigeon.
passages.vernacular: 「蛇!」鴿子尖叫道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「蛇!」鴿子尖叫道。

passages.original: “I’m not a serpent!” said Alice indignantly. “Let me alone!”
passages.vernacular: 「我唔係蛇!」愛麗絲憤慨地講。「別管我!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不是蛇!」愛麗絲憤慨地說。「別管我!」

passages.original: “Serpent, I say again!” repeated the Pigeon, but in a more subdued tone, and added with a kind of sob, “I’ve tried every way, and nothing seems to suit them!”
passages.vernacular: 「蛇,我再講一遍!」鴿子重複道,但語調更低喇,並帶住哭腔補充講:「我試過各種辦法,似乎冇一個能讓佢哋滿意!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「蛇,我再說一遍!」鴿子重複道,但語調更低了,並帶著哭腔補充說:「我試過各種辦法,似乎沒有一個能讓它們滿意!」

passages.original: “I haven’t the least idea what you’re talking about,” said Alice.
passages.vernacular: 「我啲唔知道你喺講乜嘢,」愛麗絲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我一點不知道你在說什麼,」愛麗絲說。

passages.original: “I’ve tried the roots of trees, and I’ve tried banks, and I’ve tried hedges,” the Pigeon went on, without attending to her; “but those serpents! There’s no pleasing them!”
passages.vernacular: 「我試過樹根,我試過河岸,我試過籬笆,」鴿子繼續講,不理會佢;「可嗰啲蛇!點都討不好佢哋!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我試過樹根,我試過河岸,我試過籬笆,」鴿子繼續說,不理會她;「可那些蛇!怎麼也討不好它們!」

passages.original: Alice was more and more puzzled, but she thought there was no use in saying anything more till the Pigeon had finished.
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲越嚟越困惑,但佢覺得喺鴿子講完之前再講乜嘢都冇用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲越來越困惑,但她覺得在鴿子說完之前再說什麼都沒用。

passages.original: “As if it wasn’t trouble enough hatching the eggs,” said the Pigeon; “but I must be on the look-out for serpents night and day! Why, I haven’t had a wink of sleep these three weeks!”
passages.vernacular: 「孵蛋已經夠麻煩嘅喇,」鴿子講;「我仲得日夜提防蛇!哎呀,呢三個星期我一眨眼嘅覺都冇瞓!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「孵蛋已經夠麻煩的了,」鴿子說;「我還得日夜提防蛇!哎呀,這三個星期我一眨眼的覺都沒睡!」

passages.original: “I’m very sorry you’ve been annoyed,” said Alice, who was beginning to see its meaning.
passages.vernacular: 「好抱歉你被打擾喇,」愛麗絲講,佢開始明白佢嘅意思喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很抱歉你被打擾了,」愛麗絲說,她開始明白它的意思了。

passages.original: “And just as I’d taken the highest tree in the wood,” continued the Pigeon, raising its voice to a shriek, “and just as I was thinking I should be free of them at last, they must needs come wriggling down from the sky! Ugh, Serpent!”
passages.vernacular: 「而就喺我選咗林子裡最高嘅樹,」鴿子繼續講,提高咗嗓音變成尖叫,「就喺我想住終於擺脫佢哋時,佢哋偏偏從天上蜿蜒下嚟!呸,蛇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「而就在我選了林子裡最高的樹,」鴿子繼續說,提高了嗓音變成尖叫,「就在我想著終於擺脫它們時,它們偏偏從天上蜿蜒下來!呸,蛇!」

passages.original: “But I’m not a serpent, I tell you!” said Alice. “I’m a—I’m a—”
passages.vernacular: 「但我告訴你我唔係蛇!」愛麗絲講。「我係——我係——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但我告訴你我不是蛇!」愛麗絲說。「我是——我是——」

passages.original: “Well! What are you?” said the Pigeon. “I can see you’re trying to invent something!”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯!你係乜嘢?」鴿子講。「我睇得出你喺編造乜嘢!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯!你是什麼?」鴿子說。「我看得出你在編造什麼!」

passages.original: “I—I’m a little girl,” said Alice, rather doubtfully, as she remembered the number of changes she had gone through that day.
passages.vernacular: 「我——我係個小女孩,」愛麗絲講,相當遲疑,因為佢想起嗰天自己經歷咗多少次變化。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我——我是個小女孩,」愛麗絲說,相當遲疑,因為她想起那天自己經歷了多少次變化。

passages.original: “A likely story indeed!” said the Pigeon in a tone of the deepest contempt. “I’ve seen a good many little girls in my time, but never one with such a neck as that! No, no! You’re a serpent; and there’s no use denying it. I suppose you’ll be telling me next that you never tasted an egg!”
passages.vernacular: 「真係個好講法!」鴿子用極度輕蔑嘅語調講。「我呢輩子見過不少小女孩,但從冇見過有咁長脖子嘅!不,不!你係條蛇;否認都冇用。我想你接下嚟就要告訴我你從冇嘗過蛋喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真是個好說法!」鴿子用極度輕蔑的語調說。「我這輩子見過不少小女孩,但從沒見過有這麼長脖子的!不,不!你是條蛇;否認也沒用。我想你接下來就要告訴我你從沒嘗過蛋了!」

passages.original: “I have tasted eggs, certainly,” said Alice, who was a very truthful child; “but little girls eat eggs quite as much as serpents do, you know.”
passages.vernacular: 「我確實嘗過蛋,」愛麗絲講,佢係個好誠實嘅細路;「但小女孩食蛋同蛇食得一樣多,你知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我確實嘗過蛋,」愛麗絲說,她是個非常誠實的孩子;「但小女孩吃蛋和蛇吃得一樣多,你知道。」

passages.original: “I don’t believe it,” said the Pigeon; “but if they do, why then they’re a kind of serpent, that’s all I can say.”
passages.vernacular: 「我不信,」鴿子講;「但如果佢哋食,嗰佢哋就係一種蛇,我只能咁講。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不信,」鴿子說;「但如果她們吃,那她們就是一種蛇,我只能這麼說。」

passages.original: This was such a new idea to Alice, that she was quite silent for a minute or two, which gave the Pigeon the opportunity of adding, “You’re looking for eggs, I know that well enough; and what does it matter to me whether you’re a little girl or a serpent?”
passages.vernacular: 呢對愛麗絲來講係個全新嘅想法,佢安靜咗一兩分鐘,呢畀咗鴿子補充嘅機會:「你喺找蛋,呢我好清楚;你係小女孩定係蛇,對我有乜嘢關係?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這對愛麗絲來說是個全新的想法,她安靜了一兩分鐘,這給了鴿子補充的機會:「你在找蛋,這我很清楚;你是小女孩還是蛇,對我有什麼關係?」

passages.original: “It matters a good deal to me,” said Alice hastily; “but I’m not looking for eggs, as it happens; and if I was, I shouldn’t want yours: I don’t like them raw.”
passages.vernacular: 「對我好有關係,」愛麗絲趕忙講;「但我碰巧唔係喺找蛋;就係找,我都唔好你嘅:我不鍾意生嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對我很有關係,」愛麗絲趕忙說;「但我碰巧不是在找蛋;就是找,我也不要你的:我不喜歡生的。」

passages.original: “Well, be off, then!” said the Pigeon in a sulky tone, as it settled down again into its nest. Alice crouched down among the trees as well as she could, for her neck kept getting entangled among the branches, and every now and then she had to stop and untwist it. After a while she remembered that she still held the pieces of mushroom in her hands, and she set to work very carefully, nibbling first at one and then at the other, and growing sometimes taller and sometimes shorter, until she had succeeded in bringing herself down to her usual height.
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,嗰就走開!」鴿子用慍怒嘅語調講,又安頓回佢嘅窩裡。愛麗絲儘可能蹲喺樹木中間,因為佢嘅脖子不斷纏喺樹枝間,佢時不時得停下嚟把佢解開。過咗一會兒佢記起自己手裡仲攞住蘑菇塊,佢好小心地動手,先啃一個,再啃另一個,有時長高,有時變矮,直到成功地把自己縮回咗通常嘅身高。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,那就走開!」鴿子用慍怒的語調說,又安頓回它的窩裡。愛麗絲儘可能蹲在樹木中間,因為她的脖子不斷纏在樹枝間,她時不時得停下來把它解開。過了一會兒她記起自己手裡還拿著蘑菇塊,她非常小心地動手,先啃一個,再啃另一個,有時長高,有時變矮,直到成功地把自己縮回了通常的身高。

passages.original: It was so long since she had been anything near the right size, that it felt quite strange at first; but she got used to it in a few minutes, and began talking to herself, as usual. “Come, there’s half my plan done now! How puzzling all these changes are! I’m never sure what I’m going to be, from one minute to another! However, I’ve got back to my right size: the next thing is, to get into that beautiful garden—how is that to be done, I wonder?” As she said this, she came suddenly upon an open place, with a little house in it about four feet high. “Whoever lives there,” thought Alice, “it’ll never do to come upon them this size: why, I should frighten them out of their wits!” So she began nibbling at the righthand bit again, and did not venture to go near the house till she had brought herself down to nine inches high.
passages.vernacular: 佢已經好久冇接近合適嘅大小喇,所以起初覺得相當陌生;但佢幾分鐘就習慣喇,又像往常一樣開始自言自語。「好喇,我嘅計劃已經完成一半喇!呢啲變化幾咁令人困惑啊!我一分鐘到下一分鐘,永遠不確定自己會變成乜嘢!不過,我已經回到合適嘅大小喇:下一件事係進入嗰個美麗嘅花園——我想知道點才能做到?」佢講呢話時,忽然嚟到一塊空地,空地上有一座大約四英尺高嘅小房子。「無論邊個住喺嗰度,」愛麗絲想,「用呢種大小去見佢哋絕對不行:哎呀,我會把佢哋嚇得魂飛魄散!」所以佢又開始啃右手嘅嗰塊,直到把自己縮到九英寸高,才敢走近房子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她已經很久沒有接近合適的大小了,所以起初覺得相當陌生;但她幾分鐘就習慣了,又像往常一樣開始自言自語。「好了,我的計劃已經完成一半了!這些變化多麼令人困惑啊!我一分鐘到下一分鐘,永遠不確定自己會變成什麼!不過,我已經回到合適的大小了:下一件事是進入那個美麗的花園——我想知道怎麼才能做到?」她說這話時,忽然來到一塊空地,空地上有一座大約四英尺高的小房子。「無論誰住在那裡,」愛麗絲想,「用這種大小去見他們絕對不行:哎呀,我會把他們嚇得魂飛魄散!」所以她又開始啃右手的那塊,直到把自己縮到九英寸高,才敢走近房子。

chapters.title: Ch. VI Pig and Pepper 第六章:豬與胡椒

passages.original: For a minute or two she stood looking at the house, and wondering what to do next, when suddenly a footman in livery came running out of the wood—(she considered him to be a footman because he was in livery: otherwise, judging by his face only, she would have called him a fish)—and rapped loudly at the door with his knuckles. It was opened by another footman in livery, with a round face, and large eyes like a frog; and both footmen, Alice noticed, had powdered hair that curled all over their heads. She felt very curious to know what it was all about, and crept a little way out of the wood to listen.
passages.vernacular: 有一兩分鐘,佢站住睇房子,琢磨接下嚟做乜嘢,呢陣忽然一個穿制服嘅男僕從樹林裡跑出嚟——(佢認為佢係男僕,因為佢穿制服:否則,只憑佢嘅臉嚟判斷,佢會管佢叫魚)——並用指節大聲敲門。門被另一個穿制服嘅男僕打開,佢有一張圓臉,同青蛙一樣嘅大眼睛;愛麗絲注意到兩個男僕頭上都擦咗粉,頭髮捲曲地堆喺頭上。佢好想知道呢個係點回事,便從樹林裡悄悄走出啲去聽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一兩分鐘,她站著看房子,琢磨接下來做什麼,這時忽然一個穿制服的男僕從樹林裡跑出來——(她認為他是男僕,因為他穿制服:否則,只憑他的臉來判斷,她會管他叫魚)——並用指節大聲敲門。門被另一個穿制服的男僕打開,他有一張圓臉,和青蛙一樣的大眼睛;愛麗絲注意到兩個男僕頭上都擦了粉,頭髮捲曲地堆在頭上。她很想知道這是怎麼回事,便從樹林裡悄悄走出一點去聽。

passages.original: The Fish-Footman began by producing from under his arm a great letter, nearly as large as himself, and this he handed over to the other, saying, in a solemn tone, “For the Duchess. An invitation from the Queen to play croquet.” The Frog-Footman repeated, in the same solemn tone, only changing the order of the words a little, “From the Queen. An invitation for the Duchess to play croquet.”
passages.vernacular: 魚男僕首先從胳膊下掏出一封巨大嘅信,幾乎同佢自己一樣大,把佢遞畀另一個,用莊重嘅語調講:「畀公爵夫人嘅。王后邀請佢玩槌球。」蛙男僕用同樣莊重嘅語調重複,只係把詞嘅順序稍微換咗換:「來自王后嘅。邀請公爵夫人玩槌球。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 魚男僕首先從胳膊下掏出一封巨大的信,幾乎和他自己一樣大,把它遞給另一個,用莊重的語調說:「給公爵夫人的。王后邀請她玩槌球。」蛙男僕用同樣莊重的語調重複,只是把詞的順序稍微換了換:「來自王后的。邀請公爵夫人玩槌球。」

passages.original: Then they both bowed low, and their curls got entangled together.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢哋都深深鞠躬,佢哋嘅捲髮纏喺咗一起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他們都深深鞠躬,他們的捲髮纏在了一起。

passages.original: Alice laughed so much at this, that she had to run back into the wood for fear of their hearing her; and when she next peeped out the Fish-Footman was gone, and the other was sitting on the ground near the door, staring stupidly up into the sky.
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲睇到呢個笑得咁厲害,唔得不跑回樹林裡,怕被佢哋聽見;佢下次探頭睇時,魚男僕已經走喇,另一個坐喺門邊嘅地上,傻傻地瞪住天空。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲看到這個笑得那麼厲害,不得不跑回樹林裡,怕被他們聽見;她下次探頭看時,魚男僕已經走了,另一個坐在門邊的地上,傻傻地瞪著天空。

passages.original: Alice went timidly up to the door, and knocked.
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲怯生生地走到門前,敲咗敲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲怯生生地走到門前,敲了敲。

passages.original: “There’s no sort of use in knocking,” said the Footman, “and that for two reasons. First, because I’m on the same side of the door as you are; secondly, because they’re making such a noise inside, no one could possibly hear you.” And certainly there was a most extraordinary noise going on within—a constant howling and sneezing, and every now and then a great crash, as if a dish or kettle had been broken to pieces.
passages.vernacular: 「敲門根本冇用,」男僕講,「有兩個原因。第一,因為我同你喺門嘅同一邊;第二,因為裡面吵得咁厲害,邊個都唔可能聽見你。」裡面確實在進行住極其不尋常嘅吵鬧——持續不斷嘅嚎叫同噴嚏,時不時有一聲巨響,好像有盤子或水壺被打得粉碎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「敲門根本沒用,」男僕說,「有兩個原因。第一,因為我和你在門的同一邊;第二,因為裡面吵得這麼厲害,誰也不可能聽見你。」裡面確實在進行著極其不尋常的吵鬧——持續不斷的嚎叫和噴嚏,時不時有一聲巨響,好像有盤子或水壺被打得粉碎。

passages.original: “Please, then,” said Alice, “how am I to get in?”
passages.vernacular: 「咁請問,」愛麗絲講,「我該點進去?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼請問,」愛麗絲說,「我該怎麼進去?」

passages.original: “There might be some sense in your knocking,” the Footman went on without attending to her, “if we had the door between us. For instance, if you were inside, you might knock, and I could let you out, you know.” He was looking up into the sky all the time he was speaking, and this Alice thought decidedly uncivil. “But perhaps he can’t help it,” she said to herself; “his eyes are so very nearly at the top of his head. But at any rate he might answer questions.—How am I to get in?” she repeated, aloud.
passages.vernacular: 「你敲門或者有點道理,」男僕不理佢,繼續講,「如果我哋之間隔住門嘅話。比如,如果你喺裡面,你可以敲門,我就可以放你出去,你知道。」佢講話嘅整個過程中都喺往天上睇,愛麗絲覺得呢顯然不禮貌。「但或者佢係冇辦法,」佢對自己講;「佢嘅眼睛幾乎都長喺頭頂喇。但不管點樣佢可以回答問題。——我該點進去?」佢大聲重複。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你敲門也許有點道理,」男僕不理她,繼續說,「如果我們之間隔著門的話。比如,如果你在裡面,你可以敲門,我就可以放你出去,你知道。」他說話的整個過程中都在往天上看,愛麗絲覺得這顯然不禮貌。「但也許他是沒辦法,」她對自己說;「他的眼睛幾乎都長在頭頂了。但不管怎樣他可以回答問題。——我該怎麼進去?」她大聲重複。

passages.original: “I shall sit here,” the Footman remarked, “till tomorrow—”
passages.vernacular: 「我要坐喺呢兒,」男僕講,「直到聽日——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我要坐在這兒,」男僕說,「直到明天——」

passages.original: At this moment the door of the house opened, and a large plate came skimming out, straight at the Footman’s head: it just grazed his nose, and broke to pieces against one of the trees behind him.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣房子嘅門開喇,一個大盤子飛旋而出,直衝男僕嘅腦袋:剛好擦到佢嘅鼻子,喺佢身後嘅一棵樹上摔得粉碎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時房子的門開了,一個大盤子飛旋而出,直衝男僕的腦袋:剛好擦到他的鼻子,在他身後的一棵樹上摔得粉碎。

passages.original: “—or next day, maybe,” the Footman continued in the same tone, exactly as if nothing had happened.
passages.vernacular: 「——或者後天,或者,」男僕用同樣嘅語調繼續講,好像乜嘢都冇發生過一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「——或者後天,也許,」男僕用同樣的語調繼續說,好像什麼也沒發生過一樣。

passages.original: “How am I to get in?” asked Alice again, in a louder tone.
passages.vernacular: 「我該點進去?」愛麗絲又問,聲音更大喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我該怎麼進去?」愛麗絲又問,聲音更大了。

passages.original: “Are you to get in at all?” said the Footman. “That’s the first question, you know.”
passages.vernacular: 「你到底要唔好進去?」男僕講。「嗰個係第一個問題,你知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你到底要不要進去?」男僕說。「那是第一個問題,你知道。」

passages.original: It was, no doubt: only Alice did not like to be told so. “It’s really dreadful,” she muttered to herself, “the way all the creatures argue. It’s enough to drive one crazy!”
passages.vernacular: 無疑係嘅:只係愛麗絲不鍾意被人咁講。「真係太可怕喇,」佢對自己嘟囔,「呢啲動物吵架嘅方式。足以讓人發瘋!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無疑是的:只是愛麗絲不喜歡被人這麼說。「真是太可怕了,」她對自己嘟囔,「這些動物吵架的方式。足以讓人發瘋!」

passages.original: The Footman seemed to think this a good opportunity for repeating his remark, with variations. “I shall sit here,” he said, “on and off, for days and days.”
passages.vernacular: 男僕似乎認為呢個係重複佢嘅話嘅好機會,稍微變咗一下。「我要坐喺呢兒,」佢講,「斷斷續續,一天又一天。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男僕似乎認為這是重複他的話的好機會,稍微變了一下。「我要坐在這兒,」他說,「斷斷續續,一天又一天。」

passages.original: “But what am I to do?” said Alice.
passages.vernacular: 「可我該點算?」愛麗絲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可我該怎麼辦?」愛麗絲說。

passages.original: “Anything you like,” said the Footman, and began whistling.
passages.vernacular: 「隨你鍾意,」男僕講,開始吹口哨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「隨你喜歡,」男僕說,開始吹口哨。

passages.original: “Oh, there’s no use in talking to him,” said Alice desperately: “he’s perfectly idiotic!” And she opened the door and went in.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,跟佢講話冇用,」愛麗絲絕望地講:「佢完全係個白痴!」佢打開門走咗進去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,跟他說話沒用,」愛麗絲絕望地說:「他完全是個白痴!」她打開門走了進去。

passages.original: The door led right into a large kitchen, which was full of smoke from one end to the other: the Duchess was sitting on a three-legged stool in the middle, nursing a baby; the cook was leaning over the fire, stirring a large cauldron which seemed to be full of soup.
passages.vernacular: 門直通一個大廚房,廚房從一頭到另一頭都充滿咗煙:公爵夫人坐喺中間嘅三腿凳上,抱住一個嬰兒;廚子俯身喺火上,攪拌住一個似乎裝滿湯嘅大鍋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 門直通一個大廚房,廚房從一頭到另一頭都充滿了煙:公爵夫人坐在中間的三腿凳上,抱著一個嬰兒;廚子俯身在火上,攪拌著一個似乎裝滿湯的大鍋。

passages.original: “There’s certainly too much pepper in that soup!” Alice said to herself, as well as she could for sneezing.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰湯裡面嘅胡椒肯定太多喇!」愛麗絲對自己講,儘管佢打噴嚏打得幾乎講不出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那湯裡面的胡椒肯定太多了!」愛麗絲對自己說,儘管她打噴嚏打得幾乎說不出來。

passages.original: There was certainly too much of it in the air. Even the Duchess sneezed occasionally; and as for the baby, it was sneezing and howling alternately without a moment’s pause. The only things in the kitchen that did not sneeze, were the cook, and a large cat which was sitting on the hearth and grinning from ear to ear.
passages.vernacular: 空氣中肯定有太多胡椒喇。連公爵夫人都偶爾打噴嚏;至於嬰兒,佢輪流打噴嚏同嚎叫,一刻不停。廚房裡唯一不打噴嚏嘅係廚子,同一隻坐喺爐邊、咧住嘴從呢隻耳朵笑到嗰隻耳朵嘅大貓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 空氣中肯定有太多胡椒了。連公爵夫人也偶爾打噴嚏;至於嬰兒,它輪流打噴嚏和嚎叫,一刻不停。廚房裡唯一不打噴嚏的是廚子,和一隻坐在爐邊、咧著嘴從這隻耳朵笑到那隻耳朵的大貓。

passages.original: “Please would you tell me,” said Alice, a little timidly, for she was not quite sure whether it was good manners for her to speak first, “why your cat grins like that?”
passages.vernacular: 「請問您能告訴我,」愛麗絲講,有點膽怯,因為佢不太確定先開口係咪合乎禮貌,「點解您嘅貓咁樣咧嘴笑?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請問您能告訴我,」愛麗絲說,有點膽怯,因為她不太確定先開口是否合乎禮貌,「為什麼您的貓這樣咧嘴笑?」

passages.original: “It’s a Cheshire cat,” said the Duchess, “and that’s why. Pig!”
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係一隻柴郡貓,」公爵夫人講,「所以才咁樣。豬!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是一隻柴郡貓,」公爵夫人說,「所以才這樣。豬!」

passages.original: She said the last word with such sudden violence that Alice quite jumped; but she saw in another moment that it was addressed to the baby, and not to her, so she took courage, and went on again:—
passages.vernacular: 佢講最後一個詞時突然咁猛烈,愛麗絲嚇得跳咗起嚟;但轉眼間佢就睇出呢個係對嬰兒講嘅,唔係對佢,於是佢鼓起勇氣,繼續講:——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說最後一個詞時突然那麼猛烈,愛麗絲嚇得跳了起來;但轉眼間她就看出這是對嬰兒說的,不是對她,於是她鼓起勇氣,繼續說:——

passages.original: “I didn’t know that Cheshire cats always grinned; in fact, I didn’t know that cats could grin.”
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道柴郡貓總是咧嘴笑;其實,我唔知道貓會咧嘴笑。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道柴郡貓總是咧嘴笑;其實,我不知道貓會咧嘴笑。」

passages.original: “They all can,” said the Duchess; “and most of ’em do.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋都會,」公爵夫人講;「而且大多數都咁樣做。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「它們都會,」公爵夫人說;「而且大多數都這樣做。」

passages.original: “I don’t know of any that do,” Alice said very politely, feeling quite pleased to have got into a conversation.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道有邊隻咁樣做,」愛麗絲好有禮貌地講,為終於進入對話而相當高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道有哪隻這樣做,」愛麗絲非常有禮貌地說,為終於進入對話而相當高興。

passages.original: “You don’t know much,” said the Duchess; “and that’s a fact.”
passages.vernacular: 「你知道得不多,」公爵夫人講;「呢個係事實。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你知道得不多,」公爵夫人說;「這是事實。」

passages.original: Alice did not at all like the tone of this remark, and thought it would be as well to introduce some other subject of conversation. While she was trying to fix on one, the cook took the cauldron of soup off the fire, and at once set to work throwing everything within her reach at the Duchess and the baby—the fire-irons came first; then followed a shower of saucepans, plates, and dishes. The Duchess took no notice of them even when they hit her; and the baby was howling so much already, that it was quite impossible to say whether the blows hurt it or not.
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲啲都不鍾意呢句話嘅語氣,覺得最好引入另一個話題。佢正試圖想一個時,廚子把湯鍋從火上攞下嚟,即刻動手把佢夠得住嘅所有嘢都向公爵夫人同嬰兒扔去——火鉗首先飛嚟;然後係一陣鍋、盤子同碟子嘅雨。公爵夫人即使被打中都不理睬;嬰兒已經喺嚎叫,所以完全無法講打擊係咪傷咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲一點也不喜歡這句話的語氣,覺得最好引入另一個話題。她正試圖想一個時,廚子把湯鍋從火上拿下來,立刻動手把她夠得著的所有東西都向公爵夫人和嬰兒扔去——火鉗首先飛來;然後是一陣鍋、盤子和碟子的雨。公爵夫人即使被打中也不理睬;嬰兒已經在嚎叫,所以完全無法說打擊是否傷了它。

passages.original: “Oh, please mind what you’re doing!” cried Alice, jumping up and down in an agony of terror. “Oh, there goes his precious nose!” as an unusually large saucepan flew close by it, and very nearly carried it off.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,請注意您喺做乜嘢!」愛麗絲喊道,喺極度恐懼中跳上跳下。「哦,佢寶貴嘅鼻子要飛喇!」一個特別大嘅鍋飛過佢旁邊,差點把佢帶走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,請注意您在做什麼!」愛麗絲喊道,在極度恐懼中跳上跳下。「哦,他寶貴的鼻子要飛了!」一個特別大的鍋飛過它旁邊,差點把它帶走。

passages.original: “If everybody minded their own business,” the Duchess said in a hoarse growl, “the world would go round a deal faster than it does.”
passages.vernacular: 「如果每個人都管自己嘅事,」公爵夫人用嘶啞嘅咆哮聲講,「世界轉得會比而家快得多。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果每個人都管自己的事,」公爵夫人用嘶啞的咆哮聲說,「世界轉得會比現在快得多。」

passages.original: “Which would not be an advantage,” said Alice, who felt very glad to get an opportunity of showing off a little of her knowledge. “Just think of what work it would make with the day and night! You see the earth takes twenty-four hours to turn round on its axis—”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰樣並冇好處,」愛麗絲講,佢好高興有機會展示啲自己嘅知識。「想想呢會畀白天黑夜造成乜嘢麻煩!你睇地球繞住佢嘅軸轉一圈要二十四小時——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那樣並沒有好處,」愛麗絲說,她很高興有機會展示一點自己的知識。「想想這會給白天黑夜造成什麼麻煩!你看地球繞著它的軸轉一圈要二十四小時——」

passages.original: “Talking of axes,” said the Duchess, “chop off her head!”
passages.vernacular: 「講到軸,」公爵夫人講,「砍掉佢嘅頭!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「說到軸,」公爵夫人說,「砍掉她的頭!」

passages.original: Alice glanced rather anxiously at the cook, to see if she meant to take the hint; but the cook was busily stirring the soup, and seemed not to be listening, so she went on again: “Twenty-four hours, I think; or is it twelve? I—”
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲焦急地瞥咗廚子一眼,睇佢係咪打算領會呢暗示;但廚子正忙住攪湯,似乎冇喺聽,所以佢繼續講:「二十四小時,我想;或者係十二小時?我——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲焦急地瞥了廚子一眼,看她是否打算領會這暗示;但廚子正忙著攪湯,似乎沒在聽,所以她繼續說:「二十四小時,我想;或者是十二小時?我——」

passages.original: “Oh, don’t bother me,” said the Duchess; “I never could abide figures!” And with that she began nursing her child again, singing a sort of lullaby to it as she did so, and giving it a violent shake at the end of every line:
passages.vernacular: 「哦,別煩我,」公爵夫人講;「我從來受不了數字!」講住佢又開始照顧佢嘅細路,一邊唱一種搖籃曲,一邊喺每句末尾猛烈地搖佢一下:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,別煩我,」公爵夫人說;「我從來受不了數字!」說著她又開始照顧她的孩子,一邊唱一種搖籃曲,一邊在每句末尾猛烈地搖它一下:

passages.original: “Speak roughly to your little boy, And beat him when he sneezes: He only does it to annoy, Because he knows it teases.”
passages.vernacular: 「對你嘅小男孩要粗聲講話,佢打噴嚏時打佢:佢只係為了惹人煩,因為佢知道呢讓人討厭。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對你的小男孩要粗聲說話,他打噴嚏時打他:他只是為了惹人煩,因為他知道這讓人討厭。」

passages.original: CHORUS. (In which the cook and the baby joined):
passages.vernacular: 合唱。(廚子同嬰兒一起加入):
passages.vernacularMandarin: 合唱。(廚子和嬰兒一起加入):

passages.original: “Wow! wow! wow!”
While the Duchess sang the second verse of the song, she kept tossing the baby violently up and down, and the poor little thing howled so, that Alice could hardly hear the words:—
passages.vernacular: 公爵夫人唱歌嘅第二節時,不停地把嬰兒猛烈地上下拋,可憐嘅小嘢嚎得咁響,愛麗絲幾乎聽不清詞句:——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 公爵夫人唱歌的第二節時,不停地把嬰兒猛烈地上下拋,可憐的小東西嚎得那麼響,愛麗絲幾乎聽不清詞句:——

passages.original: “I speak severely to my boy, I beat him when he sneezes; For he can thoroughly enjoy The pepper when he pleases!”
passages.vernacular: 「我對我嘅男孩講話嚴厲,佢打噴嚏我就打佢;因為佢可以盡情享受,佢想要時嘅胡椒!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我對我的男孩說話嚴厲,他打噴嚏我就打他;因為他可以盡情享受,他想要時的胡椒!」

passages.original: CHORUS.
passages.vernacular: 合唱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 合唱。

passages.original: “Wow! wow! wow!”

“Here! you may nurse it a bit, if you like!” the Duchess said to Alice, flinging the baby at her as she spoke. “I must go and get ready to play croquet with the Queen,” and she hurried out of the room. The cook threw a frying-pan after her as she went out, but it just missed her.
passages.vernacular: 「嚟!你要係願意,可以照睇佢一會兒!」公爵夫人對愛麗絲講,一邊講一邊把嬰兒朝佢扔過嚟。「我必須去準備,同王后玩槌球喇,」佢匆匆走出咗房間。佢出去時廚子朝佢扔咗一隻煎鍋,但剛好冇扔中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「來!你要是願意,可以照看它一會兒!」公爵夫人對愛麗絲說,一邊說一邊把嬰兒朝她扔過來。「我必須去準備,和王后玩槌球了,」她匆匆走出了房間。她出去時廚子朝她扔了一隻煎鍋,但剛好沒扔中。

passages.original: Alice caught the baby with some difficulty, as it was a queer-shaped little creature, and held out its arms and legs in all directions, “just like a star-fish,” thought Alice. The poor little thing was snorting like a steam-engine when she caught it, and kept doubling itself up and straightening itself out again, so that altogether, for the first minute or two, it was as much as she could do to hold it.
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲好唔容易接住咗嬰兒,因為佢係個形狀古怪嘅小嘢,朝各個方向伸出胳膊同腿,「簡直像個海星,」愛麗絲想。佢接住時,可憐嘅小嘢像蒸汽機一樣打住鼻息,不停地縮成一團又伸直,所以頭一兩分鐘,佢能抱住佢已經係竭盡全力喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲好不容易接住了嬰兒,因為它是個形狀古怪的小東西,朝各個方向伸出胳膊和腿,「簡直像個海星,」愛麗絲想。她接住時,可憐的小東西像蒸汽機一樣打著鼻息,不停地縮成一團又伸直,所以頭一兩分鐘,她能抱住它已經是竭盡全力了。

passages.original: As soon as she had made out the proper way of nursing it, (which was to twist it up into a sort of knot, and then keep tight hold of its right ear and left foot, so as to prevent its undoing itself,) she carried it out into the open air. “If I don’t take this child away with me,” thought Alice, “they’re sure to kill it in a day or two: wouldn’t it be murder to leave it behind?” She said the last words out loud, and the little thing grunted in reply (it had left off sneezing by this time). “Don’t grunt,” said Alice; “that’s not at all a proper way of expressing yourself.”
passages.vernacular: 佢一弄清咗照顧佢嘅正確方法(就係把佢擰成一種結,然後緊緊抓住佢嘅右耳同左腳,使佢唔能夠解開自己),就把佢抱到咗戶外。「如果我不把呢細路帶走,」愛麗絲想,「佢哋肯定一兩天內就會殺咗佢:把佢留下,唔係謀殺嗎?」佢把最後幾句話大聲講咗出嚟,小嘢咕嚕咗一聲作答(佢呢陣已經不打噴嚏喇)。「別咕嚕,」愛麗絲講;「嗰完全唔係表達自己嘅正確方式。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她一弄清了照顧它的正確方法(就是把它擰成一種結,然後緊緊抓住它的右耳和左腳,使它不能解開自己),就把它抱到了戶外。「如果我不把這孩子帶走,」愛麗絲想,「他們肯定一兩天內就會殺了它:把它留下,不是謀殺嗎?」她把最後幾句話大聲說了出來,小東西咕嚕了一聲作答(它這時已經不打噴嚏了)。「別咕嚕,」愛麗絲說;「那完全不是表達自己的正確方式。」

passages.original: The baby grunted again, and Alice looked very anxiously into its face to see what was the matter with it. There could be no doubt that it had a very turn-up nose, much more like a snout than a real nose; also its eyes were getting extremely small for a baby: altogether Alice did not like the look of the thing at all. “But perhaps it was only sobbing,” she thought, and looked into its eyes again, to see if there were any tears.
passages.vernacular: 嬰兒又咕嚕咗一聲,愛麗絲好焦急地睇住佢嘅臉,睇佢係點回事。毫無疑問,佢有一個好翹起嘅鼻子,更像豬鼻子而不像真正嘅鼻子;佢嘅眼睛對嬰兒來講都變得極其小:總嘅來講,愛麗絲啲都不鍾意呢嘢嘅樣子。「但或者佢只係喺啜泣,」佢想,又睇咗睇佢嘅眼睛,睇有冇眼淚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嬰兒又咕嚕了一聲,愛麗絲非常焦急地看著它的臉,看它是怎麼回事。毫無疑問,它有一個非常翹起的鼻子,更像豬鼻子而不像真正的鼻子;它的眼睛對嬰兒來說也變得極其小:總的來說,愛麗絲一點也不喜歡這東西的樣子。「但也許它只是在啜泣,」她想,又看了看它的眼睛,看有沒有眼淚。

passages.original: No, there were no tears. “If you’re going to turn into a pig, my dear,” said Alice, seriously, “I’ll have nothing more to do with you. Mind now!” The poor little thing sobbed again (or grunted, it was impossible to say which), and they went on for some while in silence.
passages.vernacular: 不,冇眼淚。「如果你要變成一隻豬,我親愛嘅,」愛麗絲嚴肅地講,「我就再都不理你喇。注意喇!」可憐嘅小嘢又啜泣咗一聲(或咕嚕咗一聲,無法講係邊個),佢哋沉默地走咗一陣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,沒有眼淚。「如果你要變成一隻豬,我親愛的,」愛麗絲嚴肅地說,「我就再也不理你了。注意了!」可憐的小東西又啜泣了一聲(或咕嚕了一聲,無法說是哪個),他們沉默地走了一陣。

passages.original: Alice was just beginning to think to herself, “Now, what am I to do with this creature when I get it home?” when it grunted again, so violently, that she looked down into its face in some alarm. This time there could be no mistake about it: it was neither more nor less than a pig, and she felt that it would be quite absurd for her to carry it further.
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲剛開始想:「而家,我把呢個嘢帶回家後點算?」佢又咕嚕咗一聲,咁猛烈,佢驚慌地低頭睇佢嘅臉。呢次唔可能有錯:佢不多不少,就係一隻豬,佢覺得再抱住佢走就太荒唐喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲剛開始想:「現在,我把這個東西帶回家後怎麼辦?」它又咕嚕了一聲,那麼猛烈,她驚慌地低頭看它的臉。這次不可能有錯:它不多不少,就是一隻豬,她覺得再抱著它走就太荒唐了。

passages.original: So she set the little creature down, and felt quite relieved to see it trot away quietly into the wood. “If it had grown up,” she said to herself, “it would have made a dreadfully ugly child: but it makes rather a handsome pig, I think.” And she began thinking over other children she knew, who might do very well as pigs, and was just saying to herself, “if one only knew the right way to change them—” when she was a little startled by seeing the Cheshire Cat sitting on a bough of a tree a few yards off.
passages.vernacular: 所以佢把小嘢放下,睇住佢安靜地小跑進樹林,相當寬慰。「如果佢長大喇,」佢對自己講,「佢會成為一個可怕嘅醜細路:但我想佢作為一隻豬,相當好睇。」佢開始想佢認識嘅其他細路,佢哋做豬可能好合適,佢正在對自己講:「如果有人知道正確嘅變法——」呢陣佢睇到柴郡貓坐喺幾碼外嘅一根樹枝上,不禁食咗一驚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以她把小東西放下,看著它安靜地小跑進樹林,相當寬慰。「如果它長大了,」她對自己說,「它會成為一個可怕的醜孩子:但我想它作為一隻豬,相當好看。」她開始想她認識的其他孩子,他們做豬可能很合適,她正在對自己說:「如果有人知道正確的變法——」這時她看到柴郡貓坐在幾碼外的一根樹枝上,不禁吃了一驚。

passages.original: The Cat only grinned when it saw Alice. It looked good-natured, she thought: still it had very long claws and a great many teeth, so she felt that it ought to be treated with respect.
passages.vernacular: 貓睇見愛麗絲只係咧嘴笑。佢覺得佢睇上去脾氣不錯:但佢有好長嘅爪子同好多牙齒,所以佢覺得應該尊重地對待佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貓看見愛麗絲只是咧嘴笑。她覺得它看上去脾氣不錯:但它有很長的爪子和很多牙齒,所以她覺得應該尊重地對待它。

passages.original: “Cheshire Puss,” she began, rather timidly, as she did not at all know whether it would like the name: however, it only grinned a little wider. “Come, it’s pleased so far,” thought Alice, and she went on. “Would you tell me, please, which way I ought to go from here?”
passages.vernacular: 「柴郡貓咪,」佢開口講,相當膽怯,因為佢完全唔知道佢係咪鍾意呢個名字:不過,佢只係笑得更開咗啲。「好,到目前為止佢仲高興,」愛麗絲想,繼續講。「請問您能告訴我,從呢兒我該走邊條路?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「柴郡貓咪,」她開口說,相當膽怯,因為她完全不知道它是否喜歡這個名字:不過,它只是笑得更開了一點。「好,到目前為止它還高興,」愛麗絲想,繼續說。「請問您能告訴我,從這兒我該走哪條路?」

passages.original: “That depends a good deal on where you want to get to,” said the Cat.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰好大程度上取決於你想去邊兒,」貓講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那很大程度上取決於你想去哪兒,」貓說。

passages.original: “I don’t much care where—” said Alice.
passages.vernacular: 「我不太在乎去邊兒——」愛麗絲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不太在乎去哪兒——」愛麗絲說。

passages.original: “Then it doesn’t matter which way you go,” said the Cat.
passages.vernacular: 「咁你走邊條路都無所謂,」貓講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼你走哪條路都無所謂,」貓說。

passages.original: “—so long as I get somewhere,” Alice added as an explanation.
passages.vernacular: 「——只要我能到某個地方,」愛麗絲補充解釋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「——只要我能到某個地方,」愛麗絲補充解釋。

passages.original: “Oh, you’re sure to do that,” said the Cat, “if you only walk long enough.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,你肯定會嘅,」貓講,「只要你走得足夠久。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,你肯定會的,」貓說,「只要你走得足夠久。」

passages.original: Alice felt that this could not be denied, so she tried another question. “What sort of people live about here?”
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲覺得呢唔能夠否認,所以佢試咗另一個問題。「呢附近住乜嘢樣嘅人?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲覺得這不能否認,所以她試了另一個問題。「這附近住著什麼樣的人?」

passages.original: “In that direction,” the Cat said, waving its right paw round, “lives a Hatter: and in that direction,” waving the other paw, “lives a March Hare. Visit either you like: they’re both mad.”
passages.vernacular: 「喺嗰個方向,」貓講,揮動右爪畫咗個圈,「住一個帽匠:喺嗰個方向,」揮動另一隻爪,「住一隻三月兔。隨便你拜訪邊個:佢哋倆都瘋喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在那個方向,」貓說,揮動右爪畫了個圈,「住著一個帽匠:在那個方向,」揮動另一隻爪,「住著一隻三月兔。隨便你拜訪哪個:他們倆都瘋了。」

passages.original: “But I don’t want to go among mad people,” Alice remarked.
passages.vernacular: 「但我唔想去瘋子中間,」愛麗絲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但我不想去瘋子中間,」愛麗絲說。

passages.original: “Oh, you can’t help that,” said the Cat: “we’re all mad here. I’m mad. You’re mad.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,你冇辦法,」貓講:「我哋呢兒都瘋喇。我瘋喇。你瘋喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,你沒辦法,」貓說:「我們這兒都瘋了。我瘋了。你瘋了。」

passages.original: “How do you know I’m mad?” said Alice.
passages.vernacular: 「你點知道我瘋喇?」愛麗絲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你怎麼知道我瘋了?」愛麗絲說。

passages.original: “You must be,” said the Cat, “or you wouldn’t have come here.”
passages.vernacular: 「你一定係,」貓講,「否則你就唔會嚟呢兒。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你一定是,」貓說,「否則你就不會來這兒。」

passages.original: Alice didn’t think that proved it at all; however, she went on “And how do you know that you’re mad?”
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲覺得呢根本證明不咗乜嘢;不過,佢繼續講:「嗰你點知道你瘋喇?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲覺得這根本證明不了什麼;不過,她繼續說:「那你怎麼知道你瘋了?」

passages.original: “To begin with,” said the Cat, “a dog’s not mad. You grant that?”
passages.vernacular: 「首先,」貓講,「狗不瘋。你承認吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「首先,」貓說,「狗不瘋。你承認吧?」

passages.original: “I suppose so,” said Alice.
passages.vernacular: 「我想係嘅,」愛麗絲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想是的,」愛麗絲說。

passages.original: “Well, then,” the Cat went on, “you see, a dog growls when it’s angry, and wags its tail when it’s pleased. Now I growl when I’m pleased, and wag my tail when I’m angry. Therefore I’m mad.”
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,咁,」貓繼續講,「你睇,狗生氣時咆哮,高興時搖尾巴。而我高興時咆哮,生氣時搖尾巴。所以我瘋喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,那麼,」貓繼續說,「你看,狗生氣時咆哮,高興時搖尾巴。而我高興時咆哮,生氣時搖尾巴。所以我瘋了。」

passages.original: “I call it purring, not growling,” said Alice.
passages.vernacular: 「我管嗰叫呼嚕,不叫咆哮,」愛麗絲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我管那叫呼嚕,不叫咆哮,」愛麗絲說。

passages.original: “Call it what you like,” said the Cat. “Do you play croquet with the Queen to-day?”
passages.vernacular: 「隨你叫乜嘢,」貓講。「你今日同王后玩槌球嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「隨你叫什麼,」貓說。「你今天和王后玩槌球嗎?」

passages.original: “I should like it very much,” said Alice, “but I haven’t been invited yet.”
passages.vernacular: 「我好想去,」愛麗絲講,「但我仲冇被邀請。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我很想去,」愛麗絲說,「但我還沒被邀請。」

passages.original: “You’ll see me there,” said the Cat, and vanished.
passages.vernacular: 「你會喺嗰兒睇到我,」貓講,然後消失喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你會在那兒看到我,」貓說,然後消失了。

passages.original: Alice was not much surprised at this, she was getting so used to queer things happening. While she was looking at the place where it had been, it suddenly appeared again.
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲對此並不太驚訝,佢已經好習慣怪事發生喇。佢正睇住佢頭先待嘅地方,佢忽然又出現喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲對此並不太驚訝,她已經很習慣怪事發生了。她正看著它剛才待的地方,它忽然又出現了。

passages.original: “By-the-bye, what became of the baby?” said the Cat. “I’d nearly forgotten to ask.”
passages.vernacular: 「順便問一下,嗰個嬰兒點樣喇?」貓講。「我差點忘咗問。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「順便問一下,那個嬰兒怎麼樣了?」貓說。「我差點忘了問。」

passages.original: “It turned into a pig,” Alice quietly said, just as if it had come back in a natural way.
passages.vernacular: 「佢變成咗一隻豬,」愛麗絲平靜地講,好像佢係以一種自然嘅方式回嚟嘅一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「它變成了一隻豬,」愛麗絲平靜地說,好像它是以一種自然的方式回來的一樣。

passages.original: “I thought it would,” said the Cat, and vanished again.
passages.vernacular: 「我就想佢會嘅,」貓講,又消失喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我就想它會的,」貓說,又消失了。

passages.original: Alice waited a little, half expecting to see it again, but it did not appear, and after a minute or two she walked on in the direction in which the March Hare was said to live. “I’ve seen hatters before,” she said to herself; “the March Hare will be much the most interesting, and perhaps as this is May it won’t be raving mad—at least not so mad as it was in March.” As she said this, she looked up, and there was the Cat again, sitting on a branch of a tree.
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲等咗一會兒,半期待住再睇到佢,但佢冇出現,一兩分鐘後,佢朝據講三月兔住嘅方向走去。「我以前見過帽匠,」佢對自己講;「三月兔會有趣得多,或者因為而家係五月,佢唔會瘋得太厲害——至少不像三月咁瘋。」佢講呢話時抬起頭,貓又喺嗰兒,坐喺一根樹枝上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲等了一會兒,半期待著再看到它,但它沒有出現,一兩分鐘後,她朝據說三月兔住的方向走去。「我以前見過帽匠,」她對自己說;「三月兔會有趣得多,也許因為現在是五月,它不會瘋得太厲害——至少不像三月那麼瘋。」她說這話時抬起頭,貓又在那兒,坐在一根樹枝上。

passages.original: “Did you say pig, or fig?” said the Cat.
passages.vernacular: 「你講嘅係豬,定係無花果?」貓講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你說的是豬,還是無花果?」貓說。

passages.original: “I said pig,” replied Alice; “and I wish you wouldn’t keep appearing and vanishing so suddenly: you make one quite giddy.”
passages.vernacular: 「我講豬,」愛麗絲回答;「我希望你別老係咁突然地出現同消失:你讓人頭暈。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我說豬,」愛麗絲回答;「我希望你別老是這麼突然地出現和消失:你讓人頭暈。」

passages.original: “All right,” said the Cat; and this time it vanished quite slowly, beginning with the end of the tail, and ending with the grin, which remained some time after the rest of it had gone.
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,」貓講;呢次佢消失得相當慢,從尾巴尖開始,以笑容結束,其餘部分都消失之後,笑容仲保留咗一會兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,」貓說;這次它消失得相當慢,從尾巴尖開始,以笑容結束,其餘部分都消失之後,笑容還保留了一會兒。

passages.original: “Well! I’ve often seen a cat without a grin,” thought Alice; “but a grin without a cat! It’s the most curious thing I ever saw in my life!”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀!我常見到冇笑容嘅貓,」愛麗絲想;「可冇貓嘅笑容!呢個係我一生中見過最稀奇嘅事!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀!我常見到沒有笑容的貓,」愛麗絲想;「可沒有貓的笑容!這是我一生中見過最稀奇的事!」

passages.original: She had not gone much farther before she came in sight of the house of the March Hare: she thought it must be the right house, because the chimneys were shaped like ears and the roof was thatched with fur. It was so large a house, that she did not like to go nearer till she had nibbled some more of the lefthand bit of mushroom, and raised herself to about two feet high: even then she walked up towards it rather timidly, saying to herself “Suppose it should be raving mad after all! I almost wish I’d gone to see the Hatter instead!”
passages.vernacular: 佢冇走多遠就睇見咗三月兔嘅房子:佢覺得一定係呢座房子,因為煙囪形狀像耳朵,屋頂係用毛皮蓋嘅。房子咁大,佢唔敢走近,直到啃咗更多左手嗰塊蘑菇,把自己長到大約兩英尺高;即使嗰樣,佢定係相當膽怯地朝佢走去,自言自語:「萬一佢終究係瘋得厲害呢!我幾乎希望我去睇帽匠喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她沒走多遠就看見了三月兔的房子:她覺得一定是這座房子,因為煙囪形狀像耳朵,屋頂是用毛皮蓋的。房子那麼大,她不敢走近,直到啃了更多左手那塊蘑菇,把自己長到大約兩英尺高;即使那樣,她還是相當膽怯地朝它走去,自言自語:「萬一它終究是瘋得厲害呢!我幾乎希望我去看帽匠了!」

chapters.title: Ch. VII A Mad Tea-Party 第七章:瘋狂茶會

passages.original: There was a table set out under a tree in front of the house, and the March Hare and the Hatter were having tea at it: a Dormouse was sitting between them, fast asleep, and the other two were using it as a cushion, resting their elbows on it, and talking over its head. “Very uncomfortable for the Dormouse,” thought Alice; “only, as it’s asleep, I suppose it doesn’t mind.”
passages.vernacular: 房子前面嘅一棵樹下擺住一張桌子,三月兔同帽匠正在嗰兒飲茶:一隻瞓鼠坐喺佢哋中間,瞓得正香,另外兩個把佢當墊子,胳膊肘擱喺佢身上,隔住佢嘅頭頂講話。「瞓鼠一定好不舒服,」愛麗絲想;「不過,佢既然瞓住喇,我想佢不在乎。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 房子前面的一棵樹下擺著一張桌子,三月兔和帽匠正在那兒喝茶:一隻睡鼠坐在他們中間,睡得正香,另外兩個把它當墊子,胳膊肘擱在它身上,隔著它的頭頂說話。「睡鼠一定很不舒服,」愛麗絲想;「不過,它既然睡著了,我想它不在乎。」

passages.original: The table was a large one, but the three were all crowded together at one corner of it: “No room! No room!” they cried out when they saw Alice coming. “There’s plenty of room!” said Alice indignantly, and she sat down in a large arm-chair at one end of the table.
passages.vernacular: 桌子好大,但三個都擠喺桌子嘅一個角落:「冇地方喇!冇地方喇!」佢哋睇見愛麗絲走嚟,就嚷道。「地方多得係!」愛麗絲憤憤地講,喺桌子一端一把大扶手椅上坐咗下嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 桌子很大,但三個都擠在桌子的一個角落:「沒地方了!沒地方了!」他們看見愛麗絲走來,就嚷道。「地方多得是!」愛麗絲憤憤地說,在桌子一端一把大扶手椅上坐了下來。

passages.original: “Have some wine,” the March Hare said in an encouraging tone.
passages.vernacular: 「飲點酒吧,」三月兔用鼓勵嘅語調講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喝點酒吧,」三月兔用鼓勵的語調說。

passages.original: Alice looked all round the table, but there was nothing on it but tea. “I don’t see any wine,” she remarked.
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲環顧桌子,但桌上除咗茶乜嘢都冇。「我冇睇見有酒,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲環顧桌子,但桌上除了茶什麼也沒有。「我沒看見有酒,」她說。

passages.original: “There isn’t any,” said the March Hare.
passages.vernacular: 「本來就冇,」三月兔講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「本來就沒有,」三月兔說。

passages.original: “Then it wasn’t very civil of you to offer it,” said Alice angrily.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰你請我飲就不太禮貌喇,」愛麗絲生氣地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那你請我喝就不太禮貌了,」愛麗絲生氣地說。

passages.original: “It wasn’t very civil of you to sit down without being invited,” said the March Hare.
passages.vernacular: 「你冇被邀請就坐下都不太禮貌,」三月兔講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你沒被邀請就坐下也不太禮貌,」三月兔說。

passages.original: “I didn’t know it was your table,” said Alice; “it’s laid for a great many more than three.”
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道呢個係你嘅桌子,」愛麗絲講;「呢度擺嘅位置遠不止三人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道這是你的桌子,」愛麗絲說;「這裡擺的位置遠不止三人。」

passages.original: “Your hair wants cutting,” said the Hatter. He had been looking at Alice for some time with great curiosity, and this was his first speech.
passages.vernacular: 「你嘅頭髮該剪喇,」帽匠講。佢已經好奇地睇咗愛麗絲一會兒,呢個係佢嘅第一句話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你的頭髮該剪了,」帽匠說。他已經好奇地看了愛麗絲一會兒,這是他的第一句話。

passages.original: “You should learn not to make personal remarks,” Alice said with some severity; “it’s very rude.”
passages.vernacular: 「你應該學會唔好發表針對個人嘅言論,」愛麗絲相當嚴厲地講;「呢個好無禮。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你應該學會不要發表針對個人的言論,」愛麗絲相當嚴厲地說;「這非常無禮。」

passages.original: The Hatter opened his eyes very wide on hearing this; but all he said was, “Why is a raven like a writing-desk?”
passages.vernacular: 帽匠聽咗呢話,眼睛睜得好大;但佢只講咗一句:「烏鴉點解像寫字檯?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 帽匠聽了這話,眼睛睜得很大;但他只說了一句:「烏鴉為什麼像寫字檯?」

passages.original: “Come, we shall have some fun now!” thought Alice. “I’m glad they’ve begun asking riddles.—I believe I can guess that,” she added aloud.
passages.vernacular: 「好,而家我哋有樂子喇!」愛麗絲想。「我好高興佢哋開始猜謎喇。——我想我能猜到,」佢大聲補充。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好,現在我們有樂子了!」愛麗絲想。「我很高興他們開始猜謎了。——我想我能猜到,」她大聲補充。

passages.original: “Do you mean that you think you can find out the answer to it?” said the March Hare.
passages.vernacular: 「你係講你認為你能找出答案?」三月兔講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你是說你認為你能找出答案?」三月兔說。

passages.original: “Exactly so,” said Alice.
passages.vernacular: 「正是,」愛麗絲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「正是,」愛麗絲說。

passages.original: “Then you should say what you mean,” the March Hare went on.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰你就應該把你嘅意思講出嚟,」三月兔接住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那你就應該把你的意思說出來,」三月兔接著說。

passages.original: “I do,” Alice hastily replied; “at least—at least I mean what I say—that’s the same thing, you know.”
passages.vernacular: 「我講喇,」愛麗絲急忙回答;「至少——至少我講嘅就係我嘅意思——嗰個係一回事,你知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我說了,」愛麗絲急忙回答;「至少——至少我說的就是我的意思——那是一回事,你知道。」

passages.original: “Not the same thing a bit!” said the Hatter. “You might just as well say that ‘I see what I eat’ is the same thing as ‘I eat what I see’!”
passages.vernacular: 「啲兒都唔係一回事!」帽匠講。「你仲不如講『我睇見我食嘅』同『我食我睇見嘅』係一回事!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一點兒也不是一回事!」帽匠說。「你還不如說『我看見我吃的』和『我吃我看見的』是一回事!」

passages.original: “You might just as well say,” added the March Hare, “that ‘I like what I get’ is the same thing as ‘I get what I like’!”
passages.vernacular: 「你仲不如講,」三月兔補充,「『我鍾意我得到嘅』同『我得到我鍾意嘅』係一回事!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你還不如說,」三月兔補充,「『我喜歡我得到的』和『我得到我喜歡的』是一回事!」

passages.original: “You might just as well say,” added the Dormouse, who seemed to be talking in his sleep, “that ‘I breathe when I sleep’ is the same thing as ‘I sleep when I breathe’!”
passages.vernacular: 「你仲不如講,」瞓鼠補充,佢似乎喺講夢話,「『我瞓覺時呼吸』同『我呼吸時瞓覺』係一回事!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你還不如說,」睡鼠補充,它似乎在說夢話,「『我睡覺時呼吸』和『我呼吸時睡覺』是一回事!」

passages.original: “It is the same thing with you,” said the Hatter, and here the conversation dropped, and the party sat silent for a minute, while Alice thought over all she could remember about ravens and writing-desks, which wasn’t much.
passages.vernacular: 「對你來講就係一回事,」帽匠講,對話到此停咗下嚟,大家安靜地坐咗一分鐘,愛麗絲把佢能想起嚟嘅關於烏鴉同寫字檯嘅一切都想咗一遍,嗰並不多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對你來說就是一回事,」帽匠說,對話到此停了下來,大家安靜地坐了一分鐘,愛麗絲把她能想起來的關於烏鴉和寫字檯的一切都想了一遍,那並不多。

passages.original: The Hatter was the first to break the silence. “What day of the month is it?” he said, turning to Alice: he had taken his watch out of his pocket, and was looking at it uneasily, shaking it every now and then, and holding it to his ear.
passages.vernacular: 帽匠第一個打破沉默。「今日係呢個月嘅幾號?」佢轉向愛麗絲講:佢已從口袋裡掏出咗錶,不安地睇住佢,時不時搖一搖,又把佢貼喺耳邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 帽匠第一個打破沉默。「今天是這個月的幾號?」他轉向愛麗絲說:他已從口袋裡掏出了錶,不安地看著它,時不時搖一搖,又把它貼在耳邊。

passages.original: Alice considered a little, and then said “The fourth.”
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲想咗想,然後講:「四號。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲想了想,然後說:「四號。」

passages.original: “Two days wrong!” sighed the Hatter. “I told you butter wouldn’t suit the works!” he added looking angrily at the March Hare.
passages.vernacular: 「錯咗兩天!」帽匠嘆道。「我告訴過你黃油不適合呢機器!」佢生氣地睇住三月兔補充。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「錯了兩天!」帽匠嘆道。「我告訴過你黃油不適合這機器!」他生氣地看著三月兔補充。

passages.original: “It was the best butter,” the March Hare meekly replied.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係最好嘅黃油,」三月兔溫順地回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是最好的黃油,」三月兔溫順地回答。

passages.original: “Yes, but some crumbs must have got in as well,” the Hatter grumbled: “you shouldn’t have put it in with the bread-knife.”
passages.vernacular: 「係,但肯定都混進咗啲碎屑,」帽匠咕噥:「你不該用切麵包嘅刀把佢放進去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,但肯定也混進了一些碎屑,」帽匠咕噥:「你不該用切麵包的刀把它放進去。」

passages.original: The March Hare took the watch and looked at it gloomily: then he dipped it into his cup of tea, and looked at it again: but he could think of nothing better to say than his first remark, “It was the best butter, you know.”
passages.vernacular: 三月兔攞過錶,悶悶不樂地睇住佢:然後把佢浸喺佢嗰杯茶裡,又睇咗睇:但佢想不出比佢嘅第一句話更好嘅話喇:「嗰個係最好嘅黃油,你知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三月兔拿過錶,悶悶不樂地看著它:然後把它浸在他那杯茶裡,又看了看:但他想不出比他的第一句話更好的話了:「那是最好的黃油,你知道。」

passages.original: Alice had been looking over his shoulder with some curiosity. “What a funny watch!” she remarked. “It tells the day of the month, and doesn’t tell what o’clock it is!”
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲好奇地一直喺佢肩後睇。「多滑稽嘅錶!」佢講。「佢顯示幾號,卻不顯示幾點!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲好奇地一直在他肩後看。「多滑稽的錶!」她說。「它顯示幾號,卻不顯示幾點!」

passages.original: “Why should it?” muttered the Hatter. “Does your watch tell you what year it is?”
passages.vernacular: 「點解要顯示?」帽匠嘟囔。「你嘅錶告訴你係邊一年嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為什麼要顯示?」帽匠嘟囔。「你的錶告訴你是哪一年嗎?」

passages.original: “Of course not,” Alice replied very readily: “but that’s because it stays the same year for such a long time together.”
passages.vernacular: 「當然不,」愛麗絲好爽快地回答:「但嗰個係因為佢一連好長時間都係同一年。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然不,」愛麗絲非常爽快地回答:「但那是因為它一連很長時間都是同一年。」

passages.original: “Which is just the case with mine,” said the Hatter.
passages.vernacular: 「我嘅都正是咁樣,」帽匠講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我的也正是這樣,」帽匠說。

passages.original: Alice felt dreadfully puzzled, The Hatter’s remark seemed to have no sort of meaning in it, and yet it was certainly English. “I don’t quite understand you,” she said, as politely as she could.
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲感到極其困惑,帽匠嘅話似乎毫無意義,然而佢確實係英語。「我不太明白你嘅意思,」佢講,盡量客氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲感到極其困惑,帽匠的話似乎毫無意義,然而它確實是英語。「我不太明白你的意思,」她說,盡量客氣。

passages.original: “The Dormouse is asleep again,” said the Hatter, and he poured a little hot tea upon its nose.
passages.vernacular: 「瞓鼠又瞓住喇,」帽匠講,往佢鼻子上倒咗啲熱茶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「睡鼠又睡著了,」帽匠說,往它鼻子上倒了一點熱茶。

passages.original: The Dormouse shook its head impatiently, and said, without opening its eyes, “Of course, of course; just what I was going to remark myself.”
passages.vernacular: 瞓鼠不耐煩地搖搖頭,眼睛都冇睜,講:「當然,當然;正是我自己要講嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 睡鼠不耐煩地搖搖頭,眼睛也沒睜,說:「當然,當然;正是我自己要說的。」

passages.original: “Have you guessed the riddle yet?” the Hatter said, turning to Alice again.
passages.vernacular: 「你猜出嗰個謎語咗嗎?」帽匠又轉向愛麗絲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你猜出那個謎語了嗎?」帽匠又轉向愛麗絲說。

passages.original: “No, I give it up,” Alice replied: “what’s the answer?”
passages.vernacular: 「冇,我放棄,」愛麗絲回答:「答案係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有,我放棄,」愛麗絲回答:「答案是什麼?」

passages.original: “I haven’t the slightest idea,” said the Hatter.
passages.vernacular: 「我啲兒都唔知道,」帽匠講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我一點兒也不知道,」帽匠說。

passages.original: “Nor I,” said the March Hare.
passages.vernacular: 「我都唔知道,」三月兔講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我也不知道,」三月兔說。

passages.original: Alice sighed wearily. “I think you might do something better with the time,” she said, “than waste it in asking riddles that have no answers.”
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲疲倦地嘆咗口氣。「我想你哋可以攞時間做點更好嘅事,」佢講,「而唔係浪費佢去問冇答案嘅謎語。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲疲倦地嘆了口氣。「我想你們可以拿時間做點更好的事,」她說,「而不是浪費它去問沒有答案的謎語。」

passages.original: “If you knew Time as well as I do,” said the Hatter, “you wouldn’t talk about wasting it. It’s him.”
passages.vernacular: 「如果你像我咁樣了解『時間』,」帽匠講,「你就唔會講浪費佢喇。係『佢』。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果你像我這樣了解『時間』,」帽匠說,「你就不會說浪費它了。是『他』。」

passages.original: “I don’t know what you mean,” said Alice.
passages.vernacular: 「我不明白你嘅意思,」愛麗絲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不明白你的意思,」愛麗絲說。

passages.original: “Of course you don’t!” the Hatter said, tossing his head contemptuously. “I dare say you never even spoke to Time!”
passages.vernacular: 「你當然不明白!」帽匠講,輕蔑地甩住頭。「我敢講你連跟『時間』講過話都冇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你當然不明白!」帽匠說,輕蔑地甩著頭。「我敢說你連跟『時間』說過話都沒有!」

passages.original: “Perhaps not,” Alice cautiously replied: “but I know I have to beat time when I learn music.”
passages.vernacular: 「或者冇,」愛麗絲謹慎地回答:「但我知道我學音樂時得『打』拍子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「也許沒有,」愛麗絲謹慎地回答:「但我知道我學音樂時得『打』拍子。」

passages.original: “Ah! that accounts for it,” said the Hatter. “He won’t stand beating. Now, if you only kept on good terms with him, he’d do almost anything you liked with the clock. For instance, suppose it were nine o’clock in the morning, just time to begin lessons: you’d only have to whisper a hint to Time, and round goes the clock in a twinkling! Half-past one, time for dinner!”
passages.vernacular: 「啊!嗰就講得通喇,」帽匠講。「佢可經不起打。而家,你要係跟佢保持良好關係,佢幾乎乜嘢都肯為你對鐘做。比如講,假設係早晨九點鐘,剛好該開始上課喇:你只需悄悄畀『時間』使個眼色,鐘就轉眼間轉起嚟喇!啲半,食午飯嘅時間!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「啊!那就說得通了,」帽匠說。「他可經不起打。現在,你要是跟他保持良好關係,他幾乎什麼都肯為你對鐘做。比如說,假設是早晨九點鐘,剛好該開始上課了:你只需悄悄給『時間』使個眼色,鐘就轉眼間轉起來了!一點半,吃午飯的時間!」

passages.original: (“I only wish it was,” the March Hare said to itself in a whisper.)
passages.vernacular: (「我只希望佢係,」三月兔低聲對自己講。)
passages.vernacularMandarin: (「我只希望它是,」三月兔低聲對自己說。)

passages.original: “That would be grand, certainly,” said Alice thoughtfully: “but then—I shouldn’t be hungry for it, you know.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰肯定棒極喇,」愛麗絲若有所思地講:「但係嗰樣——我就不餓喇,你知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那肯定棒極了,」愛麗絲若有所思地說:「但是那樣——我就不餓了,你知道。」

passages.original: “Not at first, perhaps,” said the Hatter: “but you could keep it to half-past one as long as you liked.”
passages.vernacular: 「起初或者不餓,」帽匠講:「但你可以讓佢停喺啲半,要多久有多久。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「起初也許不餓,」帽匠說:「但你可以讓它停在一點半,要多久有多久。」

passages.original: “Is that the way you manage?” Alice asked.
passages.vernacular: 「你哋就係咁樣管理嘅嗎?」愛麗絲問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你們就是這樣管理的嗎?」愛麗絲問。

passages.original: The Hatter shook his head mournfully. “Not I!” he replied. “We quarrelled last March—just before he went mad, you know—” (pointing with his tea spoon at the March Hare,) “—it was at the great concert given by the Queen of Hearts, and I had to sing
passages.vernacular: 帽匠悲傷地搖搖頭。「唔係我!」佢回答。「去年三月我哋吵翻喇——就喺佢發瘋之前,你知道——」(用茶匙指住三月兔,)「——嗰個係喺紅心王后舉辦嘅大音樂會上,我得唱
passages.vernacularMandarin: 帽匠悲傷地搖搖頭。「不是我!」他回答。「去年三月我們吵翻了——就在他發瘋之前,你知道——」(用茶匙指著三月兔,)「——那是在紅心王后舉辦的大音樂會上,我得唱

passages.original: ‘Twinkle, twinkle, little bat! How I wonder what you’re at!’
passages.vernacular: 『一閃一閃小蝙蝠!唔知你喺忙乜嘢!』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 『一閃一閃小蝙蝠!不知你在忙什麼!』

passages.original: You know the song, perhaps?”
passages.vernacular: 你或者知道呢首歌?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你也許知道這首歌?」

passages.original: “I’ve heard something like it,” said Alice.
passages.vernacular: 「我聽過類似嘅,」愛麗絲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我聽過類似的,」愛麗絲說。

passages.original: “It goes on, you know,” the Hatter continued, “in this way:—
passages.vernacular: 「佢仲有下文,你知道,」帽匠繼續講,「係咁樣嘅:——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「它還有下文,你知道,」帽匠繼續說,「是這樣的:——

passages.original: ‘Up above the world you fly, Like a tea-tray in the sky. Twinkle, twinkle—’”
passages.vernacular: 『你在世界上空飛翔,像天上一個茶盤。一閃一閃——』」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 『你在世界上空飛翔,像天上一個茶盤。一閃一閃——』」

passages.original: Here the Dormouse shook itself, and began singing in its sleep “Twinkle, twinkle, twinkle, twinkle—” and went on so long that they had to pinch it to make it stop.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣瞓鼠抖咗抖身子,喺瞓夢中唱起嚟:「一閃一閃,一閃一閃——」一直唱咗咁久,佢哋唔得不掐佢才讓佢停下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時睡鼠抖了抖身子,在睡夢中唱起來:「一閃一閃,一閃一閃——」一直唱了那麼久,他們不得不掐它才讓它停下。

passages.original: “Well, I’d hardly finished the first verse,” said the Hatter, “when the Queen jumped up and bawled out, ‘He’s murdering the time! Off with his head!’”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我剛唱完第一段,」帽匠講,「王后就跳起嚟吼道:『佢喺謀殺時間!砍掉佢嘅頭!』」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我剛唱完第一段,」帽匠說,「王后就跳起來吼道:『他在謀殺時間!砍掉他的頭!』」

passages.original: “How dreadfully savage!” exclaimed Alice.
passages.vernacular: 「幾咁可怕嘅野蠻啊!」愛麗絲驚呼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「多麼可怕的野蠻啊!」愛麗絲驚呼。

passages.original: “And ever since that,” the Hatter went on in a mournful tone, “he won’t do a thing I ask! It’s always six o’clock now.”
passages.vernacular: 「從嗰以後,」帽匠用悲傷嘅語調繼續講,「我要求佢做乜嘢佢都唔肯做!而家永遠係六點鐘。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「從那以後,」帽匠用悲傷的語調繼續說,「我要求他做什麼他都不肯做!現在永遠是六點鐘。」

passages.original: A bright idea came into Alice’s head. “Is that the reason so many tea-things are put out here?” she asked.
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲腦子裡閃過一個好主意。「呢個就係呢兒擺出咁多茶具嘅原因嗎?」佢問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲腦子裡閃過一個好主意。「這就是這兒擺出這麼多茶具的原因嗎?」她問。

passages.original: “Yes, that’s it,” said the Hatter with a sigh: “it’s always tea-time, and we’ve no time to wash the things between whiles.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,就係咁樣,」帽匠嘆咗口氣講:「永遠係飲茶嘅時間,我哋冇時間喺兩次之間洗茶具。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,就是這樣,」帽匠嘆了口氣說:「永遠是喝茶的時間,我們沒有時間在兩次之間洗茶具。」

passages.original: “Then you keep moving round, I suppose?” said Alice.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰你哋就一直換座位吧,我想?」愛麗絲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那你們就一直換座位吧,我想?」愛麗絲說。

passages.original: “Exactly so,” said the Hatter: “as the things get used up.”
passages.vernacular: 「正是,」帽匠講:「隨住嘢用完。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「正是,」帽匠說:「隨著東西用完。」

passages.original: “But what happens when you come to the beginning again?” Alice ventured to ask.
passages.vernacular: 「但係等你哋轉回到開頭嘅時候會點樣呢?」愛麗絲冒昧地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但是等你們轉回到開頭的時候會怎麼樣呢?」愛麗絲冒昧地問。

passages.original: “Suppose we change the subject,” the March Hare interrupted, yawning. “I’m getting tired of this. I vote the young lady tells us a story.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋換個話題吧,」三月兔打住哈欠打斷道。「我對呢個厭倦喇。我提議呢位年輕小姐畀我哋講個故事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們換個話題吧,」三月兔打著哈欠打斷道。「我對這個厭倦了。我提議這位年輕小姐給我們講個故事。」

passages.original: “I’m afraid I don’t know one,” said Alice, rather alarmed at the proposal.
passages.vernacular: 「恐怕我唔會講,」愛麗絲講,對呢個提議相當驚慌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「恐怕我不會講,」愛麗絲說,對這個提議相當驚慌。

passages.original: “Then the Dormouse shall!” they both cried. “Wake up, Dormouse!” And they pinched it on both sides at once.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰就讓瞓鼠講!」佢哋倆都喊。「醒醒,瞓鼠!」佢哋同時從兩邊掐佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那就讓睡鼠講!」他們倆都喊。「醒醒,睡鼠!」他們同時從兩邊掐它。

passages.original: The Dormouse slowly opened his eyes. “I wasn’t asleep,” he said in a hoarse, feeble voice: “I heard every word you fellows were saying.”
passages.vernacular: 瞓鼠慢慢睜開眼睛。「我冇瞓住,」佢用嘶啞虛弱嘅聲音講:「你哋呢啲傢伙講嘅每個字我都聽見喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 睡鼠慢慢睜開眼睛。「我沒睡著,」他用嘶啞虛弱的聲音說:「你們這些傢伙說的每個字我都聽見了。」

passages.original: “Tell us a story!” said the March Hare.
passages.vernacular: 「畀我哋講個故事!」三月兔講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「給我們講個故事!」三月兔說。

passages.original: “Yes, please do!” pleaded Alice.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,請講吧!」愛麗絲懇求。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,請講吧!」愛麗絲懇求。

passages.original: “And be quick about it,” added the Hatter, “or you’ll be asleep again before it’s done.”
passages.vernacular: 「而且要快,」帽匠補充,「否則你講完之前又瞓住喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「而且要快,」帽匠補充,「否則你講完之前又睡著了。」

passages.original: “Once upon a time there were three little sisters,” the Dormouse began in a great hurry; “and their names were Elsie, Lacie, and Tillie; and they lived at the bottom of a well—”
passages.vernacular: 「從前有三個小姐妹,」瞓鼠急匆匆地開始;「佢哋嘅名字叫埃爾西、萊西同蒂莉;佢哋住喺一口井底——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「從前有三個小姐妹,」睡鼠急匆匆地開始;「她們的名字叫埃爾西、萊西和蒂莉;她們住在一口井底——」

passages.original: “What did they live on?” said Alice, who always took a great interest in questions of eating and drinking.
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋靠乜嘢生活?」愛麗絲講,佢總是對食飲問題好感興趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她們靠什麼生活?」愛麗絲說,她總是對吃喝問題很感興趣。

passages.original: “They lived on treacle,” said the Dormouse, after thinking a minute or two.
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋靠糖漿生活,」瞓鼠想咗一兩分鐘後講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她們靠糖漿生活,」睡鼠想了一兩分鐘後說。

passages.original: “They couldn’t have done that, you know,” Alice gently remarked; “they’d have been ill.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋唔可能嗰樣,你知道,」愛麗絲溫和地講;「佢哋會生病嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她們不可能那樣,你知道,」愛麗絲溫和地說;「她們會生病的。」

passages.original: “So they were,” said the Dormouse; “very ill.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋就係生病喇,」瞓鼠講;「病得好重。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她們就是生病了,」睡鼠說;「病得很重。」

passages.original: Alice tried to fancy to herself what such an extraordinary way of living would be like, but it puzzled her too much, so she went on: “But why did they live at the bottom of a well?”
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲試著想像呢種非同尋常嘅生活方式係乜嘢樣子,但呢令佢太困惑喇,所以佢接住問:「但佢哋點解住喺井底?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲試著想像這種非同尋常的生活方式是什麼樣子,但這令她太困惑了,所以她接著問:「但她們為什麼住在井底?」

passages.original: “Take some more tea,” the March Hare said to Alice, very earnestly.
passages.vernacular: 「再飲點茶,」三月兔好認真地對愛麗絲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「再喝點茶,」三月兔非常認真地對愛麗絲說。

passages.original: “I’ve had nothing yet,” Alice replied in an offended tone, “so I can’t take more.”
passages.vernacular: 「我仲啲冇飲呢,」愛麗絲用被冒犯嘅語調回答,「所以唔能夠再多飲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我還一點沒喝呢,」愛麗絲用被冒犯的語調回答,「所以不能再多喝。」

passages.original: “You mean you can’t take less,” said the Hatter: “it’s very easy to take more than nothing.”
passages.vernacular: 「你係講你唔能夠再少飲,」帽匠講:「比乜嘢都冇多飲點係好容易嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你是說你不能再少喝,」帽匠說:「比什麼都沒有多喝點是很容易的。」

passages.original: “Nobody asked your opinion,” said Alice.
passages.vernacular: 「冇人問你嘅意見,」愛麗絲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒人問你的意見,」愛麗絲說。

passages.original: “Who’s making personal remarks now?” the Hatter asked triumphantly.
passages.vernacular: 「而家係邊個喺發表針對個人嘅言論?」帽匠得意地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在是誰在發表針對個人的言論?」帽匠得意地問。

passages.original: Alice did not quite know what to say to this: so she helped herself to some tea and bread-and-butter, and then turned to the Dormouse, and repeated her question. “Why did they live at the bottom of a well?”
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲不太知道對此講乜嘢:所以佢自己倒咗些茶,攞咗麵包同黃油,然後轉向瞓鼠,重複佢嘅問題。「佢哋點解住喺井底?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲不太知道對此說什麼:所以她自己倒了些茶,拿了麵包和黃油,然後轉向睡鼠,重複她的問題。「她們為什麼住在井底?」

passages.original: The Dormouse again took a minute or two to think about it, and then said, “It was a treacle-well.”
passages.vernacular: 瞓鼠又花咗一兩分鐘思考,然後講:「嗰個係一口糖漿井。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 睡鼠又花了一兩分鐘思考,然後說:「那是一口糖漿井。」

passages.original: “There’s no such thing!” Alice was beginning very angrily, but the Hatter and the March Hare went “Sh! sh!” and the Dormouse sulkily remarked, “If you can’t be civil, you’d better finish the story for yourself.”
passages.vernacular: 「冇呢種嘢!」愛麗絲憤怒地開口,但帽匠同三月兔發出「噓!噓!」聲,瞓鼠慍怒地講:「如果你唔能夠有禮貌,你最好自己把故事講完。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有這種東西!」愛麗絲憤怒地開口,但帽匠和三月兔發出「噓!噓!」聲,睡鼠慍怒地說:「如果你不能有禮貌,你最好自己把故事講完。」

passages.original: “No, please go on!” Alice said very humbly; “I won’t interrupt again. I dare say there may be one.”
passages.vernacular: 「不,請繼續講!」愛麗絲好謙卑地講;「我唔會再打斷喇。我敢講或者有一口。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,請繼續講!」愛麗絲非常謙卑地說;「我不會再打斷了。我敢說也許有一口。」

passages.original: “One, indeed!” said the Dormouse indignantly. However, he consented to go on. “And so these three little sisters—they were learning to draw, you know—”
passages.vernacular: 「一口,真嘅!」瞓鼠憤憤地講。不過,佢同意繼續。「所以呢三個小姐妹——佢哋喺學畫畫,你知道——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一口,真的!」睡鼠憤憤地說。不過,他同意繼續。「所以這三個小姐妹——她們在學畫畫,你知道——」

passages.original: “What did they draw?” said Alice, quite forgetting her promise.
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋畫乜嘢?」愛麗絲講,完全忘咗自己嘅諾言。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她們畫什麼?」愛麗絲說,完全忘了自己的諾言。

passages.original: “Treacle,” said the Dormouse, without considering at all this time.
passages.vernacular: 「糖漿,」瞓鼠講,呢次根本冇考慮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「糖漿,」睡鼠說,這次根本沒考慮。

passages.original: “I want a clean cup,” interrupted the Hatter: “let’s all move one place on.”
passages.vernacular: 「我要一個乾淨嘅杯子,」帽匠打斷:「我哋都往前挪一個位置。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我要一個乾淨的杯子,」帽匠打斷:「我們都往前挪一個位置。」

passages.original: He moved on as he spoke, and the Dormouse followed him: the March Hare moved into the Dormouse’s place, and Alice rather unwillingly took the place of the March Hare. The Hatter was the only one who got any advantage from the change: and Alice was a good deal worse off than before, as the March Hare had just upset the milk-jug into his plate.
passages.vernacular: 佢講住挪動喇,瞓鼠跟住佢:三月兔移到瞓鼠嘅位置,愛麗絲相當不情願地坐到咗三月兔嘅位置。帽匠係唯一從呢次變動中得到好處嘅:愛麗絲比以前糟多喇,因為三月兔剛把牛奶壺打翻喺佢嘅盤子裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說著挪動了,睡鼠跟著他:三月兔移到睡鼠的位置,愛麗絲相當不情願地坐到了三月兔的位置。帽匠是唯一從這次變動中得到好處的:愛麗絲比以前糟多了,因為三月兔剛把牛奶壺打翻在他的盤子裡。

passages.original: Alice did not wish to offend the Dormouse again, so she began very cautiously: “But I don’t understand. Where did they draw the treacle from?”
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲唔想再冒犯瞓鼠,所以佢好謹慎地開口:「但我不明白。佢哋從邊兒汲取糖漿?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲不想再冒犯睡鼠,所以她非常謹慎地開口:「但我不明白。她們從哪兒汲取糖漿?」

passages.original: “You can draw water out of a water-well,” said the Hatter; “so I should think you could draw treacle out of a treacle-well—eh, stupid?”
passages.vernacular: 「你可以從水井裡汲水,」帽匠講;「所以我想你可以從糖漿井裡汲糖漿——嗯,傻瓜?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你可以從水井裡汲水,」帽匠說;「所以我想你可以從糖漿井裡汲糖漿——嗯,傻瓜?」

passages.original: “But they were in the well,” Alice said to the Dormouse, not choosing to notice this last remark.
passages.vernacular: 「但佢哋係喺井裡面,」愛麗絲對瞓鼠講,不打算理會呢個最後一句話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但她們是在井裡面,」愛麗絲對睡鼠說,不打算理會這最後一句話。

passages.original: “Of course they were,” said the Dormouse; “—well in.”
passages.vernacular: 「當然喺,」瞓鼠講;「——喺得好深(well in)。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然在,」睡鼠說;「——在得很深(well in)。」

passages.original: This answer so confused poor Alice, that she let the Dormouse go on for some time without interrupting it.
passages.vernacular: 呢個回答把可憐嘅愛麗絲弄糊塗喇,佢讓瞓鼠講咗一會兒,冇打斷佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個回答把可憐的愛麗絲弄糊塗了,她讓睡鼠說了一會兒,沒有打斷它。

passages.original: “They were learning to draw,” the Dormouse went on, yawning and rubbing its eyes, for it was getting very sleepy; “and they drew all manner of things—everything that begins with an M—”
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋喺學畫畫,」瞓鼠繼續講,打住哈欠,揉住眼睛,因為佢越嚟越困喇;「佢哋畫各種嘢——一切以M開頭嘅嘢——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她們在學畫畫,」睡鼠繼續說,打著哈欠,揉著眼睛,因為它越來越困了;「她們畫各種東西——一切以M開頭的東西——」

passages.original: “Why with an M?” said Alice.
passages.vernacular: 「點解以M開頭?」愛麗絲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為什麼以M開頭?」愛麗絲說。

passages.original: “Why not?” said the March Hare.
passages.vernacular: 「點解不?」三月兔講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為什麼不?」三月兔說。

passages.original: Alice was silent.
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲沉默喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲沉默了。
