passages.original: The Dormouse had closed its eyes by this time, and was going off into a doze; but, on being pinched by the Hatter, it woke up again with a little shriek, and went on: “—that begins with an M, such as mouse-traps, and the moon, and memory, and muchness—you know you say things are “much of a muchness”—did you ever see such a thing as a drawing of a muchness?”
passages.vernacular: 呢陣瞓鼠已經閉上咗眼睛,正要打瞌瞓;但被帽匠掐咗一下,佢又尖叫一聲醒過嚟,繼續講:「——以M開頭嘅,比如老鼠夾(mouse-traps)、月亮(moon)、記憶(memory)同許許多多(muchness)——你知道你哋講嘢『許許多多』(much of a muchness)——你見過畫『許許多多』嘅畫嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時睡鼠已經閉上了眼睛,正要打瞌睡;但被帽匠掐了一下,它又尖叫一聲醒過來,繼續說:「——以M開頭的,比如老鼠夾(mouse-traps)、月亮(moon)、記憶(memory)和許許多多(muchness)——你知道你們說東西『許許多多』(much of a muchness)——你見過畫『許許多多』的畫嗎?」

passages.original: “Really, now you ask me,” said Alice, very much confused, “I don’t think—”
passages.vernacular: 「真嘅,既然你問我,」愛麗絲講,好困惑,「我不覺得——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真的,既然你問我,」愛麗絲說,非常困惑,「我不覺得——」

passages.original: “Then you shouldn’t talk,” said the Hatter.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰你就不該講話,」帽匠講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那你就不該說話,」帽匠說。

passages.original: This piece of rudeness was more than Alice could bear: she got up in great disgust, and walked off; the Dormouse fell asleep instantly, and neither of the others took the least notice of her going, though she looked back once or twice, half hoping that they would call after her: the last time she saw them, they were trying to put the Dormouse into the teapot.
passages.vernacular: 呢種無禮係愛麗絲無法忍受嘅:佢好厭惡地站起嚟走開喇;瞓鼠即刻瞓住喇,另外兩個邊個都冇注意佢走,雖然佢回頭睇咗一兩次,半希望佢哋會喊佢:佢最後一次睇到佢哋時,佢哋正試圖把瞓鼠放進茶壺裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這種無禮是愛麗絲無法忍受的:她非常厭惡地站起來走開了;睡鼠立刻睡著了,另外兩個誰也沒注意她走,雖然她回頭看了一兩次,半希望他們會喊她:她最後一次看到他們時,他們正試圖把睡鼠放進茶壺裡。

passages.original: “At any rate I’ll never go there again!” said Alice as she picked her way through the wood. “It’s the stupidest tea-party I ever was at in all my life!”
passages.vernacular: 「不管點樣我再都不去嗰兒喇!」愛麗絲講,一邊喺樹林中摸索住走。「呢個係我一生中參加過嘅最愚蠢嘅茶會!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不管怎樣我再也不去那兒了!」愛麗絲說,一邊在樹林中摸索著走。「這是我一生中參加過的最愚蠢的茶會!」

passages.original: Just as she said this, she noticed that one of the trees had a door leading right into it. “That’s very curious!” she thought. “But everything’s curious today. I think I may as well go in at once.” And in she went.
passages.vernacular: 佢剛講完呢話,就注意到一棵樹上有一扇門直通樹裡面。「真稀奇!」佢想。「不過今日一切都稀奇。我想我不妨即刻進去。」佢進去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她剛說完這話,就注意到一棵樹上有一扇門直通樹裡面。「真稀奇!」她想。「不過今天一切都稀奇。我想我不妨馬上進去。」她進去了。

passages.original: Once more she found herself in the long hall, and close to the little glass table. “Now, I’ll manage better this time,” she said to herself, and began by taking the little golden key, and unlocking the door that led into the garden. Then she went to work nibbling at the mushroom (she had kept a piece of it in her pocket) till she was about a foot high: then she walked down the little passage: and then—she found herself at last in the beautiful garden, among the bright flower-beds and the cool fountains.
passages.vernacular: 佢再一次發現自己喺嗰個長長嘅大廳裡,靠近小玻璃桌。「呢次我要做得更好,」佢對自己講,先攞起嗰把小金鑰匙,打開咗通往花園嘅門。然後佢動手啃蘑菇(佢口袋裡留咗一塊),直到佢大約一英尺高:然後佢走下小通道:然後——佢終於發現自己喺美麗嘅花園裡,喺明亮嘅花壇同清涼嘅噴泉中間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她再一次發現自己在那個長長的大廳裡,靠近小玻璃桌。「這次我要做得更好,」她對自己說,先拿起那把小金鑰匙,打開了通往花園的門。然後她動手啃蘑菇(她口袋裡留了一塊),直到她大約一英尺高:然後她走下小通道:然後——她終於發現自己在美麗的花園裡,在明亮的花壇和清涼的噴泉中間。

chapters.title: Ch. VIII The Queen's Croquet-Ground 第八章:王后的槌球場

passages.original: A large rose-tree stood near the entrance of the garden: the roses growing on it were white, but there were three gardeners at it, busily painting them red. Alice thought this a very curious thing, and she went nearer to watch them, and just as she came up to them she heard one of them say, “Look out now, Five! Don’t go splashing paint over me like that!”
passages.vernacular: 花園入口附近立住一棵大玫瑰樹:長喺上面嘅玫瑰係白色嘅,但有三個園丁正在嗰兒忙住把佢哋漆成紅色。愛麗絲覺得呢個好稀奇,便走近去睇佢哋,佢剛走到佢哋跟前,就聽見其中一個講:「小心點,五號!別嗰樣把顏料濺到我身上!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 花園入口附近立著一棵大玫瑰樹:長在上面的玫瑰是白色的,但有三個園丁正在那兒忙著把它們漆成紅色。愛麗絲覺得這很稀奇,便走近去看他們,她剛走到他們跟前,就聽見其中一個說:「小心點,五號!別那樣把顏料濺到我身上!」

passages.original: “I couldn’t help it,” said Five, in a sulky tone; “Seven jogged my elbow.”
passages.vernacular: 「我冇辦法,」五號用慍怒嘅語調講;「七號碰咗我嘅胳膊肘。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我沒辦法,」五號用慍怒的語調說;「七號碰了我的胳膊肘。」

passages.original: On which Seven looked up and said, “That’s right, Five! Always lay the blame on others!”
passages.vernacular: 七號抬起頭講:「講得對,五號!總是把責任推畀別人!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 七號抬起頭說:「說得對,五號!總是把責任推給別人!」

passages.original: “You’d better not talk!” said Five. “I heard the Queen say only yesterday you deserved to be beheaded!”
passages.vernacular: 「你最好唔好講話!」五號講。「我尋日才聽王后講你該砍頭!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你最好別說話!」五號說。「我昨天才聽王后說你該砍頭!」

passages.original: “What for?” said the one who had spoken first.
passages.vernacular: 「點解?」最先講話嘅嗰個講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為什麼?」最先說話的那個說。

passages.original: “That’s none of your business, Two!” said Seven.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰不關你嘅事,二號!」七號講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那不關你的事,二號!」七號說。

passages.original: “Yes, it is his business!” said Five, “and I’ll tell him—it was for bringing the cook tulip-roots instead of onions.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,係佢嘅事!」五號講,「我告訴佢——係因為畀廚子帶咗鬱金香球根而唔係洋蔥。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,是他的事!」五號說,「我告訴他——是因為給廚子帶了鬱金香球根而不是洋蔥。」

passages.original: Seven flung down his brush, and had just begun “Well, of all the unjust things—” when his eye chanced to fall upon Alice, as she stood watching them, and he checked himself suddenly: the others looked round also, and all of them bowed low.
passages.vernacular: 七號扔下刷子,剛開口講「嗯,所有不公正嘅事裡——」,佢嘅目光碰巧落喺站住睇佢哋嘅愛麗絲身上,佢突然止住喇:其他人都轉過頭嚟,佢哋全都深深鞠咗一躬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 七號扔下刷子,剛開口說「嗯,所有不公正的事裡——」,他的目光碰巧落在站著看他們的愛麗絲身上,他突然止住了:其他人也轉過頭來,他們全都深深鞠了一躬。

passages.original: “Would you tell me,” said Alice, a little timidly, “why you are painting those roses?”
passages.vernacular: 「請問你哋,」愛麗絲有點膽怯地講,「點解要漆呢啲玫瑰?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請問你們,」愛麗絲有點膽怯地說,「為什麼要漆這些玫瑰?」

passages.original: Five and Seven said nothing, but looked at Two. Two began in a low voice, “Why the fact is, you see, Miss, this here ought to have been a red rose-tree, and we put a white one in by mistake; and if the Queen was to find it out, we should all have our heads cut off, you know. So you see, Miss, we’re doing our best, afore she comes, to—” At this moment Five, who had been anxiously looking across the garden, called out “The Queen! The Queen!” and the three gardeners instantly threw themselves flat upon their faces. There was a sound of many footsteps, and Alice looked round, eager to see the Queen.
passages.vernacular: 五號同七號冇講話,只係睇住二號。二號低聲開口:「嗯,事實係,你瞧,小姐,呢度本該係一棵紅玫瑰樹,我哋錯種咗一棵白嘅;如果王后發現喇,我哋都要被砍頭,你知道。所以你瞧,小姐,我哋正在盡力,趁佢嚟之前,把——」呢陣一直焦急地望住花園對面嘅五號喊道:「王后!王后!」三個園丁即刻趴到地上,臉朝下。傳嚟許多腳步聲,愛麗絲回頭睇,急切地想睇見王后。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 五號和七號沒說話,只是看著二號。二號低聲開口:「嗯,事實是,你瞧,小姐,這裡本該是一棵紅玫瑰樹,我們錯種了一棵白的;如果王后發現了,我們都要被砍頭,你知道。所以你瞧,小姐,我們正在盡力,趁她來之前,把——」這時一直焦急地望著花園對面的五號喊道:「王后!王后!」三個園丁立刻趴到地上,臉朝下。傳來許多腳步聲,愛麗絲回頭看,急切地想看見王后。

passages.original: First came ten soldiers carrying clubs; these were all shaped like the three gardeners, oblong and flat, with their hands and feet at the corners: next the ten courtiers; these were ornamented all over with diamonds, and walked two and two, as the soldiers did. After these came the royal children; there were ten of them, and the little dears came jumping merrily along hand in hand, in couples: they were all ornamented with hearts. Next came the guests, mostly Kings and Queens, and among them Alice recognised the White Rabbit: it was talking in a hurried nervous manner, smiling at everything that was said, and went by without noticing her. Then followed the Knave of Hearts, carrying the King’s crown on a crimson velvet cushion; and, last of all this grand procession, came THE KING AND QUEEN OF HEARTS.
passages.vernacular: 首先嚟咗十個攞棍棒嘅士兵;佢哋都同三個園丁嘅形狀一樣,長方形而扁平,手腳長喺四個角上:接住係十個朝臣;佢哋全身用方塊裝飾,同士兵一樣兩個兩個地走。喺呢啲之後來咗王室嘅細路哋;共有十個,可愛嘅小傢伙哋手拉手,成雙成對地蹦蹦跳跳地走嚟:佢哋全都用紅心裝飾。接下嚟係客人哋,大多數係國王同王后,愛麗絲喺佢哋中間認出咗白兔:佢正以匆忙緊張嘅方式講話,對講嘅每句話都微笑,從佢身邊經過,冇注意到佢。接住係紅心傑克,用深紅色天鵝絨墊子捧住國王嘅王冠;喺呢盛大遊行嘅最後,嚟咗紅心國王同紅心王后。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 首先來了十個拿棍棒的士兵;他們都和三個園丁的形狀一樣,長方形而扁平,手腳長在四個角上:接著是十個朝臣;他們全身用方塊裝飾,和士兵一樣兩個兩個地走。在這些之後來了王室的孩子們;共有十個,可愛的小傢伙們手拉手,成雙成對地蹦蹦跳跳地走來:他們全都用紅心裝飾。接下來是客人們,大多數是國王和王后,愛麗絲在他們中間認出了白兔:它正以匆忙緊張的方式說話,對說的每句話都微笑,從她身邊經過,沒有注意到她。接著是紅心傑克,用深紅色天鵝絨墊子捧著國王的王冠;在這盛大遊行的最後,來了紅心國王和紅心王后。

passages.original: Alice was rather doubtful whether she ought not to lie down on her face like the three gardeners, but she could not remember ever having heard of such a rule at processions; “and besides, what would be the use of a procession,” thought she, “if people had all to lie down upon their faces, so that they couldn’t see it?” So she stood still where she was, and waited.
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲相當猶豫,係唔係該像三個園丁嗰樣臉朝下趴下,但佢不記得聽講過遊行有咁樣嘅規矩;「而且,」佢想,「如果人人都得趴喺地上,睇唔到遊行,嗰遊行有乜嘢用?」所以佢站喺原地等住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲相當猶豫,是不是該像三個園丁那樣臉朝下趴下,但她不記得聽說過遊行有這樣的規矩;「而且,」她想,「如果人人都得趴在地上,看不到遊行,那遊行有什麼用?」所以她站在原地等著。

passages.original: When the procession came opposite to Alice, they all stopped and looked at her, and the Queen said severely “Who is this?” She said it to the Knave of Hearts, who only bowed and smiled in reply.
passages.vernacular: 遊行隊伍嚟到愛麗絲對面時,都停下嚟睇住佢,王后嚴厲地講:「呢個係邊個?」佢係對紅心傑克講嘅,傑克只係鞠躬微笑作為回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 遊行隊伍來到愛麗絲對面時,都停下來看著她,王后嚴厲地說:「這是誰?」她是對紅心傑克說的,傑克只是鞠躬微笑作為回答。

passages.original: “Idiot!” said the Queen, tossing her head impatiently; and, turning to Alice, she went on, “What’s your name, child?”
passages.vernacular: 「白痴!」王后講,不耐煩地甩住頭;佢轉向愛麗絲,接住講:「你叫乜嘢名字,細路?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「白痴!」王后說,不耐煩地甩著頭;她轉向愛麗絲,接著說:「你叫什麼名字,孩子?」

passages.original: “My name is Alice, so please your Majesty,” said Alice very politely; but she added, to herself, “Why, they’re only a pack of cards, after all. I needn’t be afraid of them!”
passages.vernacular: 「我嘅名字叫愛麗絲,陛下,」愛麗絲好有禮貌地講;但佢又對自己補充道:「哎呀,佢哋終究只係一副撲克牌。我唔使怕佢哋!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我的名字叫愛麗絲,陛下,」愛麗絲非常有禮貌地說;但她又對自己補充道:「哎呀,他們終究只是一副撲克牌。我不用怕他們!」

passages.original: “And who are these?” said the Queen, pointing to the three gardeners who were lying round the rose-tree; for, you see, as they were lying on their faces, and the pattern on their backs was the same as the rest of the pack, she could not tell whether they were gardeners, or soldiers, or courtiers, or three of her own children.
passages.vernacular: 「呢啲係邊個?」王后指住躺喺玫瑰樹周圍嘅三個園丁講;因為,你瞧,佢哋臉朝下躺住,背上嘅圖案同其餘嘅牌一樣,佢無法分辨佢哋係園丁、士兵、朝臣,定係佢自己嘅三個細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這些是誰?」王后指著躺在玫瑰樹周圍的三個園丁說;因為,你瞧,他們臉朝下躺著,背上的圖案和其餘的牌一樣,她無法分辨他們是園丁、士兵、朝臣,還是她自己的三個孩子。

passages.original: “How should I know?” said Alice, surprised at her own courage. “It’s no business of mine.”
passages.vernacular: 「我點知道?」愛麗絲講,對自己嘅勇氣感到驚訝。「呢不關我嘅事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我怎麼知道?」愛麗絲說,對自己的勇氣感到驚訝。「這不關我的事。」

passages.original: The Queen turned crimson with fury, and, after glaring at her for a moment like a wild beast, screamed “Off with her head! Off—”
passages.vernacular: 王后氣得臉色通紅,像野獸一樣瞪咗佢一會兒,尖叫道:「砍掉佢嘅頭!砍——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 王后氣得臉色通紅,像野獸一樣瞪了她一會兒,尖叫道:「砍掉她的頭!砍——」

passages.original: “Nonsense!” said Alice, very loudly and decidedly, and the Queen was silent.
passages.vernacular: 「胡講!」愛麗絲好大聲而堅決地講,王后沉默喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「胡說!」愛麗絲非常大聲而堅決地說,王后沉默了。

passages.original: The King laid his hand upon her arm, and timidly said “Consider, my dear: she is only a child!”
passages.vernacular: 國王把手放喺佢嘅胳膊上,膽怯地講:「考慮一下,我親愛嘅:佢只係個細路!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 國王把手放在她的胳膊上,膽怯地說:「考慮一下,我親愛的:她只是個孩子!」

passages.original: The Queen turned angrily away from him, and said to the Knave “Turn them over!”
passages.vernacular: 王后氣憤地從佢身邊轉開,對傑克講:「把佢哋翻過嚟!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 王后氣憤地從他身邊轉開,對傑克說:「把他們翻過來!」

passages.original: The Knave did so, very carefully, with one foot.
passages.vernacular: 傑克好小心地用一隻腳咁樣做喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑克非常小心地用一隻腳這樣做了。

passages.original: “Get up!” said the Queen, in a shrill, loud voice, and the three gardeners instantly jumped up, and began bowing to the King, the Queen, the royal children, and everybody else.
passages.vernacular: 「起嚟!」王后用尖銳響亮嘅聲音講,三個園丁即刻跳起嚟,開始向國王、王后、王室嘅細路哋,同其他所有人鞠躬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「起來!」王后用尖銳響亮的聲音說,三個園丁立刻跳起來,開始向國王、王后、王室的孩子們,和其他所有人鞠躬。

passages.original: “Leave off that!” screamed the Queen. “You make me giddy.” And then, turning to the rose-tree, she went on, “What have you been doing here?”
passages.vernacular: 「別鞠喇!」王后尖叫。「你哋讓我頭暈。」然後,轉向玫瑰樹,佢接住講:「你哋喺呢兒幹乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別鞠了!」王后尖叫。「你們讓我頭暈。」然後,轉向玫瑰樹,她接著說:「你們在這兒幹什麼?」

passages.original: “May it please your Majesty,” said Two, in a very humble tone, going down on one knee as he spoke, “we were trying—”
passages.vernacular: 「陛下恩准,」二號用好謙卑嘅語調講,講住單膝跪下,「我哋喺試住——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「陛下恩准,」二號用非常謙卑的語調說,說著單膝跪下,「我們在試著——」

passages.original: “I see!” said the Queen, who had meanwhile been examining the roses. “Off with their heads!” and the procession moved on, three of the soldiers remaining behind to execute the unfortunate gardeners, who ran to Alice for protection.
passages.vernacular: 「我明白喇!」王后講,佢呢陣一直喺檢查玫瑰。「砍掉佢哋嘅頭!」隊伍繼續前進,三個士兵留下嚟處決呢啲不幸嘅園丁,園丁哋跑向愛麗絲求保護。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我明白了!」王后說,她這時一直在檢查玫瑰。「砍掉他們的頭!」隊伍繼續前進,三個士兵留下來處決這些不幸的園丁,園丁們跑向愛麗絲求保護。

passages.original: “You shan’t be beheaded!” said Alice, and she put them into a large flower-pot that stood near. The three soldiers wandered about for a minute or two, looking for them, and then quietly marched off after the others.
passages.vernacular: 「你哋唔會被砍頭!」愛麗絲講,把佢哋放進附近一個大花盆裡。三個士兵四處走咗一兩分鐘找佢哋,然後悄悄地列隊去追趕其他人喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你們不會被砍頭!」愛麗絲說,把他們放進附近一個大花盆裡。三個士兵四處走了一兩分鐘找他們,然後悄悄地列隊去追趕其他人了。

passages.original: “Are their heads off?” shouted the Queen.
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋嘅頭砍掉咗嗎?」王后喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們的頭砍掉了嗎?」王后喊道。

passages.original: “Their heads are gone, if it please your Majesty!” the soldiers shouted in reply.
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋嘅頭冇喇,陛下!」士兵哋喊住回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們的頭沒了,陛下!」士兵們喊著回答。

passages.original: “That’s right!” shouted the Queen. “Can you play croquet?”
passages.vernacular: 「好好!」王后喊道。「你會玩槌球嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很好!」王后喊道。「你會玩槌球嗎?」

passages.original: The soldiers were silent, and looked at Alice, as the question was evidently meant for her.
passages.vernacular: 士兵哋沉默住,睇住愛麗絲,因為呢個問題顯然係對佢問嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 士兵們沉默著,看著愛麗絲,因為這個問題顯然是對她問的。

passages.original: “Yes!” shouted Alice.
passages.vernacular: 「會!」愛麗絲喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「會!」愛麗絲喊道。

passages.original: “Come on, then!” roared the Queen, and Alice joined the procession, wondering very much what would happen next.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰就嚟吧!」王后吼道,愛麗絲加入咗遊行隊伍,好想知道接下嚟會發生乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那就來吧!」王后吼道,愛麗絲加入了遊行隊伍,非常想知道接下來會發生什麼。

passages.original: “It’s—it’s a very fine day!” said a timid voice at her side. She was walking by the White Rabbit, who was peeping anxiously into her face.
passages.vernacular: 「今——今日天氣好好!」佢身旁一個膽怯嘅聲音講。佢正走喺白兔旁邊,佢焦急地偷睇佢嘅臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「今——今天天氣很好!」她身旁一個膽怯的聲音說。她正走在白兔旁邊,它焦急地偷看她的臉。

passages.original: “Very,” said Alice: “—where’s the Duchess?”
passages.vernacular: 「好好,」愛麗絲講:「——公爵夫人喺邊兒?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很好,」愛麗絲說:「——公爵夫人在哪兒?」

passages.original: “Hush! Hush!” said the Rabbit in a low, hurried tone. He looked anxiously over his shoulder as he spoke, and then raised himself upon tiptoe, put his mouth close to her ear, and whispered “She’s under sentence of execution.”
passages.vernacular: 「噓!噓!」兔子低聲急促地講。佢講話時焦慮地回頭睇咗一眼,然後踮起腳尖,嘴湊近佢嘅耳朵,低聲講:「佢被判咗死刑。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「噓!噓!」兔子低聲急促地說。它說話時焦慮地回頭看了一眼,然後踮起腳尖,嘴湊近她的耳朵,低聲說:「她被判了死刑。」

passages.original: “What for?” said Alice.
passages.vernacular: 「點解?」愛麗絲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為什麼?」愛麗絲說。

passages.original: “Did you say ‘What a pity!’?” the Rabbit asked.
passages.vernacular: 「你講咗『多可惜!』嗎?」兔子問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你說了『多可惜!』嗎?」兔子問。

passages.original: “No, I didn’t,” said Alice: “I don’t think it’s at all a pity. I said ‘What for?’”
passages.vernacular: 「冇,」愛麗絲講:「我根本不覺得可惜。我講嘅係『點解?』」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有,」愛麗絲說:「我根本不覺得可惜。我說的是『為什麼?』」

passages.original: “She boxed the Queen’s ears—” the Rabbit began. Alice gave a little scream of laughter. “Oh, hush!” the Rabbit whispered in a frightened tone. “The Queen will hear you! You see, she came rather late, and the Queen said—”
passages.vernacular: 「佢打咗王后嘅耳光——」兔子開始講。愛麗絲發出一聲小小嘅笑叫。「哦,噓!」兔子用驚恐嘅語調低聲講。「王后會聽見嘅!你瞧,佢嚟得相當晚,王后講——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她打了王后的耳光——」兔子開始說。愛麗絲發出一聲小小的笑叫。「哦,噓!」兔子用驚恐的語調低聲說。「王后會聽見的!你瞧,她來得相當晚,王后說——」

passages.original: “Get to your places!” shouted the Queen in a voice of thunder, and people began running about in all directions, tumbling up against each other; however, they got settled down in a minute or two, and the game began. Alice thought she had never seen such a curious croquet-ground in her life; it was all ridges and furrows; the balls were live hedgehogs, the mallets live flamingoes, and the soldiers had to double themselves up and to stand on their hands and feet, to make the arches.
passages.vernacular: 「各就各位!」王后用雷鳴般嘅聲音喊,人哋開始朝各個方向跑,互相撞喺一起;不過,一兩分鐘後佢哋就安頓好喇,比賽開始喇。愛麗絲覺得佢呢輩子冇見過咁古怪嘅槌球場;全係壟溝:球係活刺蝟,槌子係活火烈鳥,士兵哋得把自己彎成雙層,用手腳撐住,嚟做球門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「各就各位!」王后用雷鳴般的聲音喊,人們開始朝各個方向跑,互相撞在一起;不過,一兩分鐘後他們就安頓好了,比賽開始了。愛麗絲覺得她這輩子沒見過這麼古怪的槌球場;全是壟溝:球是活刺蝟,槌子是活火烈鳥,士兵們得把自己彎成雙層,用手腳撐著,來做球門。

passages.original: The chief difficulty Alice found at first was in managing her flamingo: she succeeded in getting its body tucked away, comfortably enough, under her arm, with its legs hanging down, but generally, just as she had got its neck nicely straightened out, and was going to give the hedgehog a blow with its head, it would twist itself round and look up in her face, with such a puzzled expression that she could not help bursting out laughing: and when she had got its head down, and was going to begin again, it was very provoking to find that the hedgehog had unrolled itself, and was in the act of crawling away: besides all this, there was generally a ridge or furrow in the way wherever she wanted to send the hedgehog to, and, as the doubled-up soldiers were always getting up and walking off to other parts of the ground, Alice soon came to the conclusion that it was a very difficult game indeed.
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲起初發現嘅主要困難係操縱佢嘅火烈鳥:佢成功地把佢嘅身體舒適地夾喺胳膊下,雙腿垂下嚟,但通常,就喺佢剛把佢嘅脖子理直,正要用佢嘅頭去擊刺蝟時,佢就會扭轉身子抬頭睇住佢嘅臉,帶住咁困惑嘅表情,佢忍不住大笑起嚟:當佢把佢嘅頭弄低,又要開始時,發現刺蝟已經展開身子,正在爬走,好惱人:此外,不管佢想把刺蝟打向邊兒,通常路上都有壟或溝,而且彎成雙層嘅士兵總是站起嚟走到場地嘅別處去,愛麗絲好快得出結論,呢確實係個好困難嘅遊戲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲起初發現的主要困難是操縱她的火烈鳥:她成功地把它的身體舒適地夾在胳膊下,雙腿垂下來,但通常,就在她剛把它的脖子理直,正要用它的頭去擊刺蝟時,它就會扭轉身子抬頭看著她的臉,帶著那麼困惑的表情,她忍不住大笑起來:當她把它的頭弄低,又要開始時,發現刺蝟已經展開身子,正在爬走,非常惱人:此外,不管她想把刺蝟打向哪兒,通常路上都有壟或溝,而且彎成雙層的士兵總是站起來走到場地的別處去,愛麗絲很快得出結論,這確實是個非常困難的遊戲。

passages.original: The players all played at once without waiting for turns, quarrelling all the while, and fighting for the hedgehogs; and in a very short time the Queen was in a furious passion, and went stamping about, and shouting “Off with his head!” or “Off with her head!” about once in a minute.
passages.vernacular: 選手哋都同時玩,不等輪流,一直吵架,爭奪刺蝟;好快王后就狂怒起嚟,跺住腳走嚟走去,大約每分鐘喊一次「砍掉佢嘅頭!」或「砍掉佢嘅頭!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 選手們都同時玩,不等輪流,一直吵架,爭奪刺蝟;很快王后就狂怒起來,跺著腳走來走去,大約每分鐘喊一次「砍掉他的頭!」或「砍掉她的頭!」

passages.original: Alice began to feel very uneasy: to be sure, she had not as yet had any dispute with the Queen, but she knew that it might happen any minute, “and then,” thought she, “what would become of me? They’re dreadfully fond of beheading people here; the great wonder is, that there’s any one left alive!”
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲開始覺得好不安:誠然,佢迄今仲冇同王后爭執過,但佢知道呢隨時可能發生,「嗰時,」佢想,「我會點樣?佢哋呢度可怕地愛砍人頭;最大嘅奇蹟係,仲有人活住!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲開始覺得很不安:誠然,她迄今還沒有和王后爭執過,但她知道這隨時可能發生,「那時,」她想,「我會怎麼樣?他們這裡可怕地愛砍人頭;最大的奇蹟是,還有人活著!」

passages.original: She was looking about for some way of escape, and wondering whether she could get away without being seen, when she noticed a curious appearance in the air: it puzzled her very much at first, but, after watching it a minute or two, she made it out to be a grin, and she said to herself “It’s the Cheshire Cat: now I shall have somebody to talk to.”
passages.vernacular: 佢四處尋找逃跑嘅辦法,並琢磨係咪能不被睇見地逃走,呢陣佢注意到空中有個奇怪嘅景象:起初讓佢好困惑,但睇咗一兩分鐘後,佢睇出嗰個係一個咧嘴嘅笑,佢對自己講:「呢個係柴郡貓:而家我有講話嘅對象喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她四處尋找逃跑的辦法,並琢磨是否能不被看見地逃走,這時她注意到空中有個奇怪的景象:起初讓她非常困惑,但看了一兩分鐘後,她看出那是一個咧嘴的笑,她對自己說:「這是柴郡貓:現在我有說話的對象了。」

passages.original: “How are you getting on?” said the Cat, as soon as there was mouth enough for it to speak with.
passages.vernacular: 「你點樣?」貓講,一有足夠嘅嘴能講話佢就講喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你怎麼樣?」貓說,一有足夠的嘴能說話它就說了。

passages.original: Alice waited till the eyes appeared, and then nodded. “It’s no use speaking to it,” she thought, “till its ears have come, or at least one of them.” In another minute the whole head appeared, and then Alice put down her flamingo, and began an account of the game, feeling very glad she had someone to listen to her. The Cat seemed to think that there was enough of it now in sight, and no more of it appeared.
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲等到眼睛出現,然後點咗點頭。「對佢講話冇用,」佢想,「等佢嘅耳朵嚟喇,至少嚟一隻。」又過咗一分鐘,整個頭出現喇,然後愛麗絲放下佢嘅火烈鳥,開始講述遊戲嘅情況,好高興有人聽佢講。貓似乎覺得佢而家露出嚟嘅已經夠多喇,冇再出現更多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲等到眼睛出現,然後點了點頭。「對它說話沒用,」她想,「等它的耳朵來了,至少來一隻。」又過了一分鐘,整個頭出現了,然後愛麗絲放下她的火烈鳥,開始講述遊戲的情況,非常高興有人聽她說。貓似乎覺得它現在露出來的已經夠多了,沒有再出現更多。

passages.original: “I don’t think they play at all fairly,” Alice began, in rather a complaining tone, “and they all quarrel so dreadfully one can’t hear oneself speak—and they don’t seem to have any rules in particular; at least, if there are, nobody attends to them—and you’ve no idea how confusing it is all the things being alive; for instance, there’s the arch I’ve got to go through next walking about at the other end of the ground—and I should have croqueted the Queen’s hedgehog just now, only it ran away when it saw mine coming!”
passages.vernacular: 「我覺得佢哋玩得啲都不公平,」愛麗絲開始,用相當抱怨嘅語調講,「而且佢哋吵得咁厲害,人聽唔見自己講話——佢哋似乎冇任何特別嘅規則;至少,即使有,都冇人理會——你想唔到所有嘢都係活嘅有多亂;比如,我接下嚟要穿過嘅球門,正在場地嘅另一頭走嚟走去——我頭先本來可以擊中王后嘅刺蝟,只係佢睇見我嘅過嚟就跑掉喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我覺得他們玩得一點也不公平,」愛麗絲開始,用相當抱怨的語調說,「而且他們吵得這麼厲害,人聽不見自己說話——他們似乎沒有任何特別的規則;至少,即使有,也沒人理會——你想不到所有東西都是活的有多亂;比如,我接下來要穿過的球門,正在場地的另一頭走來走去——我剛才本來可以擊中王后的刺蝟,只是它看見我的過來就跑掉了!」

passages.original: “How do you like the Queen?” said the Cat in a low voice.
passages.vernacular: 「你鍾意王后嗎?」貓低聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你喜歡王后嗎?」貓低聲說。

passages.original: “Not at all,” said Alice: “she’s so extremely—” Just then she noticed that the Queen was close behind her, listening: so she went on, “—likely to win, that it’s hardly worth while finishing the game.”
passages.vernacular: 「啲都不,」愛麗絲講:「佢係咁極其——」呢陣佢注意到王后就緊貼喺佢身後聽住:所以佢接住講,「——好可能會贏,所以幾乎不值得把遊戲結束。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一點也不,」愛麗絲說:「她是那麼極其——」這時她注意到王后就緊貼在她身後聽著:所以她接著說,「——很可能會贏,所以幾乎不值得把遊戲結束。」

passages.original: The Queen smiled and passed on.
passages.vernacular: 王后笑咗笑,走開喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 王后笑了笑,走開了。

passages.original: “Who are you talking to?” said the King, going up to Alice, and looking at the Cat’s head with great curiosity.
passages.vernacular: 「你喺跟邊個講話?」國王走向愛麗絲講,好奇地睇住貓嘅頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你在跟誰說話?」國王走向愛麗絲說,好奇地看著貓的頭。

passages.original: “It’s a friend of mine—a Cheshire Cat,” said Alice: “allow me to introduce it.”
passages.vernacular: 「係我嘅一位朋友——一隻柴郡貓,」愛麗絲講:「請允許我介紹一下。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是我的一位朋友——一隻柴郡貓,」愛麗絲說:「請允許我介紹一下。」

passages.original: “I don’t like the look of it at all,” said the King: “however, it may kiss my hand if it likes.”
passages.vernacular: 「我啲都不鍾意佢嘅樣子,」國王講:「不過,佢要係願意,可以吻我嘅手。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我一點也不喜歡它的樣子,」國王說:「不過,它要是願意,可以吻我的手。」

passages.original: “I’d rather not,” the Cat remarked.
passages.vernacular: 「我寧可不,」貓講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我寧可不,」貓說。

passages.original: “Don’t be impertinent,” said the King, “and don’t look at me like that!” He got behind Alice as he spoke.
passages.vernacular: 「別無禮,」國王講,「都別嗰樣睇住我!」佢講住躲到咗愛麗絲身後。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別無禮,」國王說,「也別那樣看著我!」他說著躲到了愛麗絲身後。

passages.original: “A cat may look at a king,” said Alice. “I’ve read that in some book, but I don’t remember where.”
passages.vernacular: 「貓可以睇國王,」愛麗絲講。「我喺乜嘢書裡讀到過,但不記得喺邊兒喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「貓可以看國王,」愛麗絲說。「我在什麼書裡讀到過,但不記得在哪兒了。」

passages.original: “Well, it must be removed,” said the King very decidedly, and he called the Queen, who was passing at the moment, “My dear! I wish you would have this cat removed!”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,佢必須被移走,」國王好堅決地講,佢叫咗正好經過嘅王后:「我嘅親愛嘅!我希望你把呢隻貓弄走!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,它必須被移走,」國王非常堅決地說,他叫了正好經過的王后:「我的親愛的!我希望你把這隻貓弄走!」

passages.original: The Queen had only one way of settling all difficulties, great or small. “Off with his head!” she said, without even looking round.
passages.vernacular: 王后解決所有困難,無論大小,只有一個辦法。「砍掉佢嘅頭!」佢講,甚至冇回頭睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 王后解決所有困難,無論大小,只有一個辦法。「砍掉他的頭!」她說,甚至沒有回頭看。

passages.original: “I’ll fetch the executioner myself,” said the King eagerly, and he hurried off.
passages.vernacular: 「我親自去叫劊子手,」國王急切地講,匆匆走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我親自去叫劊子手,」國王急切地說,匆匆走了。

passages.original: Alice thought she might as well go back, and see how the game was going on, as she heard the Queen’s voice in the distance, screaming with passion. She had already heard her sentence three of the players to be executed for having missed their turns, and she did not like the look of things at all, as the game was in such confusion that she never knew whether it was her turn or not. So she went in search of her hedgehog.
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲想佢不妨回去睇睇遊戲進行得點樣,因為佢聽到遠處王后嘅聲音,憤怒地尖叫。佢已經聽到佢判決三個選手處死,因為佢哋錯過咗自己嘅輪次,佢啲都不鍾意呢情形,因為遊戲咁混亂,佢永遠唔知道係唔係輪到佢。於是佢去找自己嘅刺蝟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲想她不妨回去看看遊戲進行得怎麼樣,因為她聽到遠處王后的聲音,憤怒地尖叫。她已經聽到她判決三個選手處死,因為他們錯過了自己的輪次,她一點也不喜歡這情形,因為遊戲那麼混亂,她永遠不知道是不是輪到她。於是她去找自己的刺蝟。

passages.original: The hedgehog was engaged in a fight with another hedgehog, which seemed to Alice an excellent opportunity for croqueting one of them with the other: the only difficulty was, that her flamingo was gone across to the other side of the garden, where Alice could see it trying in a helpless sort of way to fly up into a tree.
passages.vernacular: 刺蝟正在同另一隻刺蝟打架,呢喺愛麗絲睇來係用其中一隻擊另一隻嘅絕好機會:唯一嘅困難係,佢嘅火烈鳥跑到咗花園嘅另一邊,愛麗絲睇見佢正以一種無助嘅方式試圖飛上一棵樹。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 刺蝟正在和另一隻刺蝟打架,這在愛麗絲看來是用其中一隻擊另一隻的絕好機會:唯一的困難是,她的火烈鳥跑到了花園的另一邊,愛麗絲看見它正以一種無助的方式試圖飛上一棵樹。

passages.original: By the time she had caught the flamingo and brought it back, the fight was over, and both the hedgehogs were out of sight: “but it doesn’t matter much,” thought Alice, “as all the arches are gone from this side of the ground.” So she tucked it away under her arm, that it might not escape again, and went back for a little more conversation with her friend.
passages.vernacular: 佢抓住火烈鳥帶回嚟時,架已經打完喇,兩隻刺蝟都唔見喇:「不過冇多大關係,」愛麗絲想,「因為場地呢一邊所有嘅球門都走喇。」所以佢把佢夾喺胳膊下,免得佢再跑掉,回去同佢嘅朋友再聊一聊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她抓住火烈鳥帶回來時,架已經打完了,兩隻刺蝟都不見了:「不過沒多大關係,」愛麗絲想,「因為場地這一邊所有的球門都走了。」所以她把它夾在胳膊下,免得它再跑掉,回去和她的朋友再聊一聊。

passages.original: When she got back to the Cheshire Cat, she was surprised to find quite a large crowd collected round it: there was a dispute going on between the executioner, the King, and the Queen, who were all talking at once, while all the rest were quite silent, and looked very uncomfortable.
passages.vernacular: 佢回到柴郡貓嗰兒時,驚訝地發現周圍聚集咗相當一大群人:劊子手、國王同王后之間喺爭論,佢哋同時講話,而其餘嘅人都靜靜地睇住,好不自在。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她回到柴郡貓那兒時,驚訝地發現周圍聚集了相當一大群人:劊子手、國王和王后之間在爭論,他們同時說話,而其餘的人都靜靜地看著,非常不自在。

passages.original: The moment Alice appeared, she was appealed to by all three to settle the question, and they repeated their arguments to her, though, as they all spoke at once, she found it very hard indeed to make out exactly what they said.
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲一出現,佢哋三個就都向佢求助嚟解決呢個問題,佢哋向佢重複自己嘅論點,不過,因為佢哋同時講話,佢好難聽清佢哋究竟講咗乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲一出現,他們三個就都向她求助來解決這個問題,他們向她重複自己的論點,不過,因為他們同時說話,她很難聽清他們究竟說了什麼。

passages.original: The executioner’s argument was, that you couldn’t cut off a head unless there was a body to cut it off from: that he had never had to do such a thing before, and he wasn’t going to begin at his time of life.
passages.vernacular: 劊子手嘅論點係,冇身體就唔能夠砍下頭嚟:佢以前從冇做過呢種事,佢到咗呢把年紀都不打算開始。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 劊子手的論點是,沒有身體就不能砍下頭來:他以前從沒有做過這種事,他到了這把年紀也不打算開始。

passages.original: The King’s argument was, that anything that had a head could be beheaded, and that you weren’t to talk nonsense.
passages.vernacular: 國王嘅論點係,凡是有頭嘅嘢都可以被砍頭,唔好胡講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 國王的論點是,凡是有頭的東西都可以被砍頭,不要胡說。

passages.original: The Queen’s argument was, that if something wasn’t done about it in less than no time she’d have everybody executed, all round. (It was this last remark that had made the whole party look so grave and anxious.)
passages.vernacular: 王后嘅論點係,如果不喺極短嘅時間裡對此採取措施,佢就要把所有人通通處決。(正是呢個最後一句話,讓整個一群人睇上去咁嚴肅而焦慮。)
passages.vernacularMandarin: 王后的論點是,如果不在極短的時間裡對此採取措施,她就要把所有人通通處決。(正是這最後一句話,讓整個一群人看上去那麼嚴肅而焦慮。)

passages.original: Alice could think of nothing else to say but “It belongs to the Duchess: you’d better ask her about it.”
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲想不出別嘅話可講,只講:「佢係公爵夫人嘅:你哋最好問問佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲想不出別的話可說,只說:「它是公爵夫人的:你們最好問問她。」

passages.original: “She’s in prison,” the Queen said to the executioner: “fetch her here.” And the executioner went off like an arrow.
passages.vernacular: 「佢喺監獄裡,」王后對劊子手講:「把佢帶到呢兒嚟。」劊子手像箭一樣去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她在監獄裡,」王后對劊子手說:「把她帶到這兒來。」劊子手像箭一樣去了。

passages.original: The Cat’s head began fading away the moment he was gone, and, by the time he had come back with the Duchess, it had entirely disappeared; so the King and the executioner ran wildly up and down looking for it, while the rest of the party went back to the game.
passages.vernacular: 佢一走,貓嘅頭就開始消失,等佢帶住公爵夫人回嚟時,佢已經完全消失喇;於是國王同劊子手瘋狂地上下奔跑尋找佢,而其餘嘅人回到咗遊戲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他一走,貓的頭就開始消失,等他帶著公爵夫人回來時,它已經完全消失了;於是國王和劊子手瘋狂地上下奔跑尋找它,而其餘的人回到了遊戲。

chapters.title: Ch. IX The Mock Turtle's Story 第九章:假海龜的故事

passages.original: “You can’t think how glad I am to see you again, you dear old thing!” said the Duchess, as she tucked her arm affectionately into Alice’s, and they walked off together.
passages.vernacular: 「你想唔到我再見到你有多高興,你呢個親愛嘅老嘢!」公爵夫人講,親熱地把胳膊挽進愛麗絲嘅胳膊,佢哋一起走開喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你想不到我再見到你有多高興,你這個親愛的老東西!」公爵夫人說,親熱地把胳膊挽進愛麗絲的胳膊,她們一起走開了。

passages.original: Alice was very glad to find her in such a pleasant temper, and thought to herself that perhaps it was only the pepper that had made her so savage when they met in the kitchen.
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲好高興發現佢脾氣咁好,心想或者只係胡椒讓佢喺廚房遇見時咁凶暴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲很高興發現她脾氣這麼好,心想也許只是胡椒讓她在廚房遇見時那麼凶暴。

passages.original: “When I’m a Duchess,” she said to herself, (not in a very hopeful tone though), “I won’t have any pepper in my kitchen at all. Soup does very well without—Maybe it’s always pepper that makes people hot-tempered,” she went on, very much pleased at having found out a new kind of rule, “and vinegar that makes them sour—and camomile that makes them bitter—and—and barley-sugar and such things that make children sweet-tempered. I only wish people knew that: then they wouldn’t be so stingy about it, you know—”
passages.vernacular: 「等我當咗公爵夫人,」佢對自己講,(不過語調不太有希望),「我嘅廚房裡根本不放胡椒。湯冇胡椒都好好——或者總是胡椒讓人脾氣暴躁,」佢接住講,為發現咗一種新規律而好高興,「醋讓人酸——甘菊讓人苦——仲有——仲有大麥糖之類嘅嘢讓細路脾氣甜。我只希望人哋都知道呢個:嗰樣佢哋就唔會對此咁吝嗇喇,你知道——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「等我當了公爵夫人,」她對自己說,(不過語調不太有希望),「我的廚房裡根本不放胡椒。湯沒有胡椒也很好——也許總是胡椒讓人脾氣暴躁,」她接著說,為發現了一種新規律而非常高興,「醋讓人酸——甘菊讓人苦——還有——還有大麥糖之類的東西讓孩子脾氣甜。我只希望人們都知道這個:那樣他們就不會對此這麼吝嗇了,你知道——」

passages.original: She had quite forgotten the Duchess by this time, and was a little startled when she heard her voice close to her ear. “You’re thinking about something, my dear, and that makes you forget to talk. I can’t tell you just now what the moral of that is, but I shall remember it in a bit.”
passages.vernacular: 呢陣佢完全忘咗公爵夫人,聽見佢嘅聲音貼近耳邊,不由得有點食驚。「你喺想事情,我嘅親愛嘅,呢讓你忘咗講話。我而家唔能夠告訴你呢件事嘅寓意係乜嘢,但我一會兒就會想起嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時她完全忘了公爵夫人,聽見她的聲音貼近耳邊,不由得有點吃驚。「你在想事情,我的親愛的,這讓你忘了說話。我現在不能告訴你這件事的寓意是什麼,但我一會兒就會想起來。」

passages.original: “Perhaps it hasn’t one,” Alice ventured to remark.
passages.vernacular: 「或者佢冇寓意,」愛麗絲冒昧地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「也許它沒有寓意,」愛麗絲冒昧地說。

passages.original: “Tut, tut, child!” said the Duchess. “Everything’s got a moral, if only you can find it.” And she squeezed herself up closer to Alice’s side as she spoke.
passages.vernacular: 「嘖,嘖,細路!」公爵夫人講。「萬物都有寓意,只要你能找到。」佢講住把身子更緊地擠到愛麗絲身邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嘖,嘖,孩子!」公爵夫人說。「萬物都有寓意,只要你能找到。」她說著把身子更緊地擠到愛麗絲身邊。

passages.original: Alice did not much like keeping so close to her: first, because the Duchess was very ugly; and secondly, because she was exactly the right height to rest her chin upon Alice’s shoulder, and it was an uncomfortably sharp chin. However, she did not like to be rude, so she bore it as well as she could.
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲不太鍾意靠佢咁近:首先,因為公爵夫人好醜;其次,因為佢嘅身高剛好可以把下巴擱喺愛麗絲嘅肩上,而嗰個係個令人不舒服嘅尖下巴。不過,佢唔願無禮,所以盡量忍受住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲不太喜歡靠她這麼近:首先,因為公爵夫人非常醜;其次,因為她的身高剛好可以把下巴擱在愛麗絲的肩上,而那是個令人不舒服的尖下巴。不過,她不願無禮,所以盡量忍受著。

passages.original: “The game’s going on rather better now,” she said, by way of keeping up the conversation a little.
passages.vernacular: 「遊戲而家進行得好啲喇,」佢講,為了維持啲對話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「遊戲現在進行得好一些了,」她說,為了維持一點對話。

passages.original: “’Tis so,” said the Duchess: “and the moral of that is—‘Oh, ’tis love, ’tis love, that makes the world go round!’”
passages.vernacular: 「係咁樣,」公爵夫人講:「呢件事嘅寓意係——『哦,係愛,係愛,讓世界轉動!』」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是這樣,」公爵夫人說:「這件事的寓意是——『哦,是愛,是愛,讓世界轉動!』」

passages.original: “Somebody said,” Alice whispered, “that it’s done by everybody minding their own business!”
passages.vernacular: 「有人講過,」愛麗絲低聲講,「係人人都管自己嘅事才讓世界轉動!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有人說過,」愛麗絲低聲說,「是人人都管自己的事才讓世界轉動!」

passages.original: “Ah, well! It means much the same thing,” said the Duchess, digging her sharp little chin into Alice’s shoulder as she added, “and the moral of that is—‘Take care of the sense, and the sounds will take care of themselves.’”
passages.vernacular: 「啊,好吧!意思差不多,」公爵夫人講,把佢尖尖嘅小下巴扎進愛麗絲嘅肩膀,補充講,「呢件事嘅寓意係——『照顧好意義,聲音自會照顧好自己。』」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「啊,好吧!意思差不多,」公爵夫人說,把她尖尖的小下巴扎進愛麗絲的肩膀,補充說,「這件事的寓意是——『照顧好意義,聲音自會照顧好自己。』」

passages.original: “How fond she is of finding morals in things!” Alice thought to herself.
passages.vernacular: 「佢幾咁愛喺事情裡找寓意啊!」愛麗絲心想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她多麼愛在事情裡找寓意啊!」愛麗絲心想。

passages.original: “I dare say you’re wondering why I don’t put my arm round your waist,” the Duchess said after a pause: “the reason is, that I’m doubtful about the temper of your flamingo. Shall I try the experiment?”
passages.vernacular: 「我敢講你喺奇怪我點解唔使胳膊摟你嘅腰,」公爵夫人停咗一下後講:「原因係,我對你嘅火烈鳥嘅脾氣有些懷疑。我要試試睇嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我敢說你在奇怪我為什麼不用胳膊摟你的腰,」公爵夫人停了一下後說:「原因是,我對你的火烈鳥的脾氣有些懷疑。我要試試看嗎?」

passages.original: “He might bite,” Alice cautiously replied, not feeling at all anxious to have the experiment tried.
passages.vernacular: 「佢可能會咬人,」愛麗絲謹慎地回答,啲都不急於讓佢試。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「它可能會咬人,」愛麗絲謹慎地回答,一點也不急於讓她試。

passages.original: “Very true,” said the Duchess: “flamingoes and mustard both bite. And the moral of that is—‘Birds of a feather flock together.’”
passages.vernacular: 「好對,」公爵夫人講:「火烈鳥同芥末都咬人。呢件事嘅寓意係——『物以類聚。』」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很對,」公爵夫人說:「火烈鳥和芥末都咬人。這件事的寓意是——『物以類聚。』」

passages.original: “Only mustard isn’t a bird,” Alice remarked.
passages.vernacular: 「只不過芥末唔係鳥,」愛麗絲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「只不過芥末不是鳥,」愛麗絲說。

passages.original: “Right, as usual,” said the Duchess: “what a clear way you have of putting things!”
passages.vernacular: 「講得對,同往常一樣,」公爵夫人講:「你講事情幾咁清楚!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「說得對,和往常一樣,」公爵夫人說:「你說事情多麼清楚!」

passages.original: “It’s a mineral, I think,” said Alice.
passages.vernacular: 「我想佢係礦物,」愛麗絲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想它是礦物,」愛麗絲說。

passages.original: “Of course it is,” said the Duchess, who seemed ready to agree to everything that Alice said; “there’s a large mustard-mine near here. And the moral of that is—‘The more there is of mine, the less there is of yours.’”
passages.vernacular: 「當然係,」公爵夫人講,佢似乎準備同意愛麗絲講嘅一切;「呢附近有一個大芥末礦。呢件事嘅寓意係——『我嘅越多,你嘅越少。』」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然是,」公爵夫人說,她似乎準備同意愛麗絲說的一切;「這附近有一個大芥末礦。這件事的寓意是——『我的越多,你的越少。』」

passages.original: “Oh, I know!” exclaimed Alice, who had not attended to this last remark, “it’s a vegetable. It doesn’t look like one, but it is.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我知道喇!」愛麗絲喊道,佢冇注意最後呢句話,「佢係蔬菜。佢睇上去不像,但確實係。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我知道了!」愛麗絲喊道,她沒有注意最後這句話,「它是蔬菜。它看上去不像,但確實是。」

passages.original: “I quite agree with you,” said the Duchess; “and the moral of that is—‘Be what you would seem to be’—or if you’d like it put more simply—‘Never imagine yourself not to be otherwise than what it might appear to others that what you were or might have been was not otherwise than what you had been would have appeared to them to be otherwise.’”
passages.vernacular: 「我完全同意你,」公爵夫人講;「呢件事嘅寓意係——『做你想顯得係嘅人』——或者如果你鍾意講得更簡單啲——『永遠唔好想像你自己唔係別人可能睇起嚟你曾係或可能曾係嘅樣子唔係別樣,而你曾係嘅樣子會喺佢哋睇來係別樣。』」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我完全同意你,」公爵夫人說;「這件事的寓意是——『做你想顯得是的人』——或者如果你喜歡說得更簡單一點——『永遠不要想像你自己不是別人可能看起來你曾是或可能曾是的樣子不是別樣,而你曾是的樣子會在他們看來是別樣。』」

passages.original: “I think I should understand that better,” Alice said very politely, “if I had it written down: but I can’t quite follow it as you say it.”
passages.vernacular: 「我想如果寫下嚟,我會更好地明白,」愛麗絲好有禮貌地講:「但係你咁講,我不太能跟上。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想如果寫下來,我會更好地明白,」愛麗絲非常有禮貌地說:「但是你這麼說,我不太能跟上。」

passages.original: “That’s nothing to what I could say if I chose,” the Duchess replied, in a pleased tone.
passages.vernacular: 「呢跟我如果願意能講嘅比起嚟不算乜嘢,」公爵夫人用高興嘅語調回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這跟我如果願意能說的比起來不算什麼,」公爵夫人用高興的語調回答。

passages.original: “Pray don’t trouble yourself to say it any longer than that,” said Alice.
passages.vernacular: 「請唔使費心講得比呢更長喇,」愛麗絲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請不必費心說得比這更長了,」愛麗絲說。

passages.original: “Oh, don’t talk about trouble!” said the Duchess. “I make you a present of everything I’ve said as yet.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,別提麻煩!」公爵夫人講。「我把到目前為止我講嘅一切都送畀你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,別提麻煩!」公爵夫人說。「我把到目前為止我說的一切都送給你。」

passages.original: “A cheap sort of present!” thought Alice. “I’m glad they don’t give birthday presents like that!” But she did not venture to say it out loud.
passages.vernacular: 「便宜嘅禮物!」愛麗絲想。「我好高興佢哋不送咁樣嘅生日禮物!」但佢唔敢大聲講出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「便宜的禮物!」愛麗絲想。「我很高興他們不送這樣的生日禮物!」但她不敢大聲說出來。

passages.original: “Thinking again?” the Duchess asked, with another dig of her sharp little chin.
passages.vernacular: 「又喺想?」公爵夫人又用佢尖尖嘅小下巴扎咗一下,問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「又在想?」公爵夫人又用她尖尖的小下巴扎了一下,問。

passages.original: “I’ve a right to think,” said Alice sharply, for she was beginning to feel a little worried.
passages.vernacular: 「我有權利想,」愛麗絲尖銳地講,因為佢開始有點擔心喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我有權利想,」愛麗絲尖銳地說,因為她開始有點擔心了。

passages.original: “Just about as much right,” said the Duchess, “as pigs have to fly; and the m—”
passages.vernacular: 「權利差不多就同豬有權利飛一樣,」公爵夫人講;「而寓——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「權利差不多就和豬有權利飛一樣,」公爵夫人說;「而寓——」

passages.original: But here, to Alice’s great surprise, the Duchess’s voice died away, even in the middle of her favourite word ‘moral,’ and the arm that was linked into hers began to tremble. Alice looked up, and there stood the Queen in front of them, with her arms folded, frowning like a thunderstorm.
passages.vernacular: 但呢陣,令愛麗絲大食一驚嘅係,公爵夫人嘅聲音消失喇,甚至喺佢最鍾意嘅詞「寓意」中間,而挽住佢胳膊嘅嗰隻胳膊開始顫抖。愛麗絲抬頭一睇,王后站喺佢哋面前,抱住雙臂,像雷雨一樣皺住眉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但這時,令愛麗絲大吃一驚的是,公爵夫人的聲音消失了,甚至在她最喜歡的詞「寓意」中間,而挽著她胳膊的那隻胳膊開始顫抖。愛麗絲抬頭一看,王后站在她們面前,抱著雙臂,像雷雨一樣皺著眉。

passages.original: “A fine day, your Majesty!” the Duchess began in a low, weak voice.
passages.vernacular: 「天氣真好,陛下!」公爵夫人用低而微弱嘅聲音開口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天氣真好,陛下!」公爵夫人用低而微弱的聲音開口。

passages.original: “Now, I give you fair warning,” shouted the Queen, stamping on the ground as she spoke; “either you or your head must be off, and that in about half no time! Take your choice!”
passages.vernacular: 「而家,我畀你公平嘅警告,」王后喊道,講住跺地;「要麼你要麼你嘅頭必須走,而且喺唔到半瞬間之內!做出你嘅選擇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在,我給你公平的警告,」王后喊道,說著跺地;「要麼你要麼你的頭必須走,而且在不到半瞬間之內!做出你的選擇!」

passages.original: The Duchess took her choice, and was gone in a moment.
passages.vernacular: 公爵夫人做咗選擇,轉眼間就唔見喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 公爵夫人做了選擇,轉眼間就不見了。

passages.original: “Let’s go on with the game,” the Queen said to Alice; and Alice was too much frightened to say a word, but slowly followed her back to the croquet-ground.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋繼續遊戲吧,」王后對愛麗絲講;愛麗絲嚇得一個字都講不出嚟,慢慢跟住佢回到槌球場。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們繼續遊戲吧,」王后對愛麗絲說;愛麗絲嚇得一個字也說不出來,慢慢跟著她回到槌球場。

passages.original: The other guests had taken advantage of the Queen’s absence, and were resting in the shade: however, the moment they saw her, they hurried back to the game, the Queen merely remarking that a moment’s delay would cost them their lives.
passages.vernacular: 其他客人趁王后不喺,正在樹蔭下休息:不過,佢哋一睇見佢,就趕緊回到遊戲中,王后只係講,片刻嘅耽擱就會要佢哋嘅命。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其他客人趁王后不在,正在樹蔭下休息:不過,他們一看見她,就趕緊回到遊戲中,王后只是說,片刻的耽擱就會要他們的命。

passages.original: All the time they were playing the Queen never left off quarrelling with the other players, and shouting “Off with his head!” or “Off with her head!” Those whom she sentenced were taken into custody by the soldiers, who of course had to leave off being arches to do this, so that by the end of half an hour or so there were no arches left, and all the players, except the King, the Queen, and Alice, were in custody and under sentence of execution.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋玩嘅整個時間裡,王后一直喺同其他選手吵架,並喊住「砍掉佢嘅頭!」或「砍掉佢嘅頭!」被佢判刑嘅人由士兵睇管,士兵當然得離開去做球門才能做到呢個,所以半個鐘頭左右後就冇球門喇,除咗國王、王后同愛麗絲,所有選手都被拘押並判處死刑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們玩的整個時間裡,王后一直在和其他選手吵架,並喊著「砍掉他的頭!」或「砍掉她的頭!」被她判刑的人由士兵看管,士兵當然得離開去做球門才能做到這個,所以半個鐘頭左右後就沒有球門了,除了國王、王后和愛麗絲,所有選手都被拘押並判處死刑。

passages.original: Then the Queen left off, quite out of breath, and said to Alice, “Have you seen the Mock Turtle yet?”
passages.vernacular: 然後王后停下嚟,氣喘吁吁,對愛麗絲講:「你見過假海龜咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後王后停下來,氣喘吁吁,對愛麗絲說:「你見過假海龜了嗎?」

passages.original: “No,” said Alice. “I don’t even know what a Mock Turtle is.”
passages.vernacular: 「冇,」愛麗絲講。「我甚至唔知道假海龜係乜嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有,」愛麗絲說。「我甚至不知道假海龜是什麼。」

passages.original: “It’s the thing Mock Turtle Soup is made from,” said the Queen.
passages.vernacular: 「就係做假海龜湯嘅嘢,」王后講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就是做假海龜湯的東西,」王后說。

passages.original: “I never saw one, or heard of one,” said Alice.
passages.vernacular: 「我從冇見過,都冇聽講過,」愛麗絲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我從沒見過,也沒聽說過,」愛麗絲說。

passages.original: “Come on, then,” said the Queen, “and he shall tell you his history.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰就嚟吧,」王后講,「佢會告訴你佢嘅身世。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那就來吧,」王后說,「他會告訴你他的身世。」

passages.original: As they walked off together, Alice heard the King say in a low voice, to the company generally, “You are all pardoned.” “Come, that’s a good thing!” she said to herself, for she had felt quite unhappy at the number of executions the Queen had ordered.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋一起走開時,愛麗絲聽見國王低聲對在場所有人講:「你哋都被赦免喇。」「好,呢個係件好事!」佢對自己講,因為佢對王后下令處決嘅人數感到好不快。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們一起走開時,愛麗絲聽見國王低聲對在場所有人說:「你們都被赦免了。」「好,這是件好事!」她對自己說,因為她對王后下令處決的人數感到很不快。

passages.original: They very soon came upon a Gryphon, lying fast asleep in the sun. (If you don’t know what a Gryphon is, look at the picture.) “Up, lazy thing!” said the Queen, “and take this young lady to see the Mock Turtle, and to hear his history. I must go back and see after some executions I have ordered;” and she walked off, leaving Alice alone with the Gryphon. Alice did not quite like the look of the creature, but on the whole she thought it would be quite as safe to stay with it as to go after that savage Queen: so she waited.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋好快遇見一頭獅鷲,喺太陽下瞓得正香。(如果你唔知道獅鷲係乜嘢,睇睇圖。)「起嚟,懶嘢!」王后講,「帶呢位年輕小姐去睇假海龜,聽佢嘅身世。我得回去睇睇我下令嘅啲處決;」佢走喇,留下愛麗絲同獅鷲單獨喺一起。愛麗絲不太鍾意呢生物嘅樣子,但總嘅來講佢覺得同佢待喺一起,跟追住嗰個凶暴嘅王后一樣安全:所以佢等住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們很快遇見一頭獅鷲,在太陽下睡得正香。(如果你不知道獅鷲是什麼,看看圖。)「起來,懶東西!」王后說,「帶這位年輕小姐去看假海龜,聽他的身世。我得回去看看我下令的一些處決;」她走了,留下愛麗絲和獅鷲單獨在一起。愛麗絲不太喜歡這生物的樣子,但總的來說她覺得和它待在一起,跟追著那個凶暴的王后一樣安全:所以她等著。

passages.original: The Gryphon sat up and rubbed its eyes: then it watched the Queen till she was out of sight: then it chuckled. “What fun!” said the Gryphon, half to itself, half to Alice.
passages.vernacular: 獅鷲坐起嚟揉揉眼睛:然後睇住王后,直到佢走出視線:然後食食地笑。「多好玩!」獅鷲講,一半對自己,一半對愛麗絲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 獅鷲坐起來揉揉眼睛:然後看著王后,直到她走出視線:然後吃吃地笑。「多好玩!」獅鷲說,一半對自己,一半對愛麗絲。

passages.original: “What is the fun?” said Alice.
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢好玩?」愛麗絲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼好玩?」愛麗絲說。

passages.original: “Why, she,” said the Gryphon. “It’s all her fancy, that: they never executes nobody, you know. Come on!”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,佢,」獅鷲講。「嗰全係佢嘅幻想:佢哋從不處決邊個,你知道。嚟吧!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,她,」獅鷲說。「那全是她的幻想:他們從不處決誰,你知道。來吧!」

passages.original: “Everybody says ‘come on!’ here,” thought Alice, as she went slowly after it: “I never was so ordered about in all my life, never!”
passages.vernacular: 「呢度人人都講『嚟吧!』」愛麗絲想,慢慢跟喺佢後面:「我呢輩子從冇被咁樣支使過,從來冇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這裡人人都說『來吧!』」愛麗絲想,慢慢跟在它後面:「我這輩子從沒被這樣支使過,從來沒有!」

passages.original: They had not gone far before they saw the Mock Turtle in the distance, sitting sad and lonely on a little ledge of rock, and, as they came nearer, Alice could hear him sighing as if his heart would break. She pitied him deeply. “What is his sorrow?” she asked the Gryphon, and the Gryphon answered, very nearly in the same words as before, “It’s all his fancy, that: he hasn’t got no sorrow, you know. Come on!”
passages.vernacular: 佢哋冇走多遠,就遠遠睇見假海龜,悲傷孤獨地坐喺一小塊岩石壁架上,走近時,愛麗絲能聽見佢嘆息,好像心要碎喇。佢深深地同情佢。「佢有乜嘢悲傷?」佢問獅鷲,獅鷲幾乎用同以前相同嘅話回答:「嗰全係佢嘅幻想:佢冇悲傷,你知道。嚟吧!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們沒走多遠,就遠遠看見假海龜,悲傷孤獨地坐在一小塊岩石壁架上,走近時,愛麗絲能聽見他嘆息,好像心要碎了。她深深地同情他。「他有什麼悲傷?」她問獅鷲,獅鷲幾乎用和以前相同的話回答:「那全是他的幻想:他沒有悲傷,你知道。來吧!」

passages.original: So they went up to the Mock Turtle, who looked at them with large eyes full of tears, but said nothing.
passages.vernacular: 於是佢哋走向假海龜,佢用滿含淚水嘅大眼睛睇住佢哋,但乜嘢都冇講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是他們走向假海龜,它用滿含淚水的大眼睛看著他們,但什麼也沒說。

passages.original: “This here young lady,” said the Gryphon, “she wants for to know your history, she do.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢位年輕小姐,」獅鷲講,「佢想知道你嘅身世,佢想。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這位年輕小姐,」獅鷲說,「她想知道你的身世,她想。」

passages.original: “I’ll tell it her,” said the Mock Turtle in a deep, hollow tone: “sit down, both of you, and don’t speak a word till I’ve finished.”
passages.vernacular: 「我告訴佢,」假海龜用深沉空洞嘅語調講:「你哋倆坐下,等我講完之前唔好講一個字。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我告訴她,」假海龜用深沉空洞的語調說:「你們倆坐下,等我說完之前別說一個字。」

passages.original: So they sat down, and nobody spoke for some minutes. Alice thought to herself, “I don’t see how he can ever finish, if he doesn’t begin.” But she waited patiently.
passages.vernacular: 於是佢哋坐下喇,幾分鐘冇人講話。愛麗絲心想:「我不明白佢不開始點能結束。」但佢耐心地等住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是他們坐下了,幾分鐘沒人說話。愛麗絲心想:「我不明白他不開始怎麼能結束。」但她耐心地等著。

passages.original: “Once,” said the Mock Turtle at last, with a deep sigh, “I was a real Turtle.”
passages.vernacular: 「從前,」假海龜終於深深嘆咗口氣講,「我係一隻真正嘅海龜。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「從前,」假海龜終於深深嘆了口氣說,「我是一隻真正的海龜。」

passages.original: These words were followed by a very long silence, broken only by an occasional exclamation of “Hjckrrh!” from the Gryphon, and the constant heavy sobbing of the Mock Turtle. Alice was very nearly getting up and saying, “Thank you, sir, for your interesting story,” but she could not help thinking there must be more to come, so she sat still and said nothing.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲話之後係好長一段沉默,只被獅鷲偶爾嘅一聲「呃咳嗝!」同假海龜持續沉重嘅啜泣打破。愛麗絲差點站起來講「謝謝你,先生,謝謝你有趣嘅故事」,但佢忍不住想一定仲有下文,所以佢坐住冇動,乜嘢都冇講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些話之後是很長一段沉默,只被獅鷲偶爾的一聲「呃咳嗝!」和假海龜持續沉重的啜泣打破。愛麗絲差點站起來說「謝謝你,先生,謝謝你有趣的故事」,但她忍不住想一定還有下文,所以她坐著沒動,什麼也沒說。

passages.original: “When we were little,” the Mock Turtle went on at last, more calmly, though still sobbing a little now and then, “we went to school in the sea. The master was an old Turtle—we used to call him Tortoise—”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋小嘅時候,」假海龜終於比較平靜地繼續講,雖然偶爾仲有點抽泣,「我哋喺海裡上學。老師係一隻老海龜——我哋常叫佢陸龜(Tortoise)——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們小的時候,」假海龜終於比較平靜地繼續說,雖然偶爾還有點抽泣,「我們在海裡上學。老師是一隻老海龜——我們常叫他陸龜(Tortoise)——」

passages.original: “Why did you call him Tortoise, if he wasn’t one?” Alice asked.
passages.vernacular: 「如果佢唔係陸龜,你哋點解叫佢陸龜?」愛麗絲問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果他不是陸龜,你們為什麼叫他陸龜?」愛麗絲問。

passages.original: “We called him Tortoise because he taught us,” said the Mock Turtle angrily: “really you are very dull!”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋叫佢陸龜(Tortoise),因為佢教我哋(taught us),」假海龜生氣地講:「你真係太笨喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們叫他陸龜(Tortoise),因為他教我們(taught us),」假海龜生氣地說:「你真是太笨了!」

passages.original: “You ought to be ashamed of yourself for asking such a simple question,” added the Gryphon; and then they both sat silent and looked at poor Alice, who felt ready to sink into the earth. At last the Gryphon said to the Mock Turtle, “Drive on, old fellow! Don’t be all day about it!” and he went on in these words:
passages.vernacular: 「你問咁簡單嘅問題,應該為自己感到羞愧,」獅鷲補充;然後佢哋倆都沉默地坐住,睇住可憐嘅愛麗絲,佢覺得恨唔得鑽進地裡。最後獅鷲對假海龜講:「接住講,老夥計!別拖一整天!」佢接住用呢啲話講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你問這麼簡單的問題,應該為自己感到羞愧,」獅鷲補充;然後他們倆都沉默地坐著,看著可憐的愛麗絲,她覺得恨不得鑽進地裡。最後獅鷲對假海龜說:「接著說,老夥計!別拖一整天!」他接著用這些話說:

passages.original: “Yes, we went to school in the sea, though you mayn’t believe it—”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,我哋喺海裡上學,雖然你可能不信——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,我們在海裡上學,雖然你可能不信——」

passages.original: “I never said I didn’t!” interrupted Alice.
passages.vernacular: 「我從冇講我不信!」愛麗絲打斷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我從沒說我不信!」愛麗絲打斷。

passages.original: “You did,” said the Mock Turtle.
passages.vernacular: 「你講喇,」假海龜講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你說了,」假海龜說。

passages.original: “Hold your tongue!” added the Gryphon, before Alice could speak again. The Mock Turtle went on.
passages.vernacular: 「閉嘴!」獅鷲喺愛麗絲能再講話之前補充。假海龜繼續講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「閉嘴!」獅鷲在愛麗絲能再說話之前補充。假海龜繼續說。

passages.original: “We had the best of educations—in fact, we went to school every day—”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋受到咗最好嘅教育——事實上,我哋每天都上學——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們受到了最好的教育——事實上,我們每天都上學——」

passages.original: “I’ve been to a day-school, too,” said Alice; “you needn’t be so proud as all that.”
passages.vernacular: 「我都上過日校,」愛麗絲講;「你唔使咁驕傲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我也上過日校,」愛麗絲說;「你不必那麼驕傲。」

passages.original: “With extras?” asked the Mock Turtle a little anxiously.
passages.vernacular: 「有額外科目嗎?」假海龜有點焦急地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有額外科目嗎?」假海龜有點焦急地問。

passages.original: “Yes,” said Alice, “we learned French and music.”
passages.vernacular: 「有,」愛麗絲講,「我哋學法語同音樂。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有,」愛麗絲說,「我們學法語和音樂。」

passages.original: “And washing?” said the Mock Turtle.
passages.vernacular: 「仲有洗衣?」假海龜講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「還有洗衣?」假海龜說。

passages.original: “Certainly not!” said Alice indignantly.
passages.vernacular: 「當然冇!」愛麗絲憤慨地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然沒有!」愛麗絲憤慨地說。

passages.original: “Ah! then yours wasn’t a really good school,” said the Mock Turtle in a tone of great relief. “Now at ours they had at the end of the bill, ‘French, music, and washing—extra.’”
passages.vernacular: 「啊!嗰你哋嘅唔係真正好嘅學校,」假海龜用大大鬆咗口氣嘅語調講。「我哋學校賬單末尾有:『法語、音樂同洗衣——額外收費。』」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「啊!那你們的不是真正好的學校,」假海龜用大大鬆了口氣的語調說。「我們學校賬單末尾有:『法語、音樂和洗衣——額外收費。』」

passages.original: “You couldn’t have wanted it much,” said Alice; “living at the bottom of the sea.”
passages.vernacular: 「你哋唔會好需要佢,」愛麗絲講;「住喺海底。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你們不會很需要它,」愛麗絲說;「住在海底。」

passages.original: “I couldn’t afford to learn it.” said the Mock Turtle with a sigh. “I only took the regular course.”
passages.vernacular: 「我學不起,」假海龜嘆氣講。「我只上咗常規課程。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我學不起,」假海龜嘆氣說。「我只上了常規課程。」

passages.original: “What was that?” inquired Alice.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係乜嘢?」愛麗絲問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是什麼?」愛麗絲問。

passages.original: “Reeling and Writhing, of course, to begin with,” the Mock Turtle replied; “and then the different branches of Arithmetic—Ambition, Distraction, Uglification, and Derision.”
passages.vernacular: 「當然,首先係捲繞同扭動(Reeling and Writhing),」假海龜回答;「然後係算術嘅不同分支——野心、分心、醜化同嘲笑(Ambition, Distraction, Uglification, and Derision)。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然,首先是捲繞和扭動(Reeling and Writhing),」假海龜回答;「然後是算術的不同分支——野心、分心、醜化和嘲笑(Ambition, Distraction, Uglification, and Derision)。」

passages.original: “I never heard of ‘Uglification,’” Alice ventured to say. “What is it?”
passages.vernacular: 「我從冇聽講過『醜化』,」愛麗絲冒昧地講。「嗰個係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我從沒聽說過『醜化』,」愛麗絲冒昧地說。「那是什麼?」

passages.original: The Gryphon lifted up both its paws in surprise. “What! Never heard of uglifying!” it exclaimed. “You know what to beautify is, I suppose?”
passages.vernacular: 獅鷲驚訝地舉起兩隻爪子。「乜嘢!冇聽講過醜化!」佢驚呼。「我想你知道美化係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 獅鷲驚訝地舉起兩隻爪子。「什麼!沒聽說過醜化!」它驚呼。「我想你知道美化是什麼?」

passages.original: “Yes,” said Alice doubtfully: “it means—to—make—anything—prettier.”
passages.vernacular: 「知道,」愛麗絲懷疑地講:「就係——把——任何嘢——弄得——更漂亮。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「知道,」愛麗絲懷疑地說:「就是——把——任何東西——弄得——更漂亮。」

passages.original: “Well, then,” the Gryphon went on, “if you don’t know what to uglify is, you are a simpleton.”
passages.vernacular: 「咁,」獅鷲接住講,「如果你唔知道醜化係乜嘢,你就係個傻瓜。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼,」獅鷲接著說,「如果你不知道醜化是什麼,你就是個傻瓜。」

passages.original: Alice did not feel encouraged to ask any more questions about it, so she turned to the Mock Turtle, and said “What else had you to learn?”
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲冇被鼓勵再問更多關於佢嘅問題,所以佢轉向假海龜,講:「你仲要學乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲沒有被鼓勵再問更多關於它的問題,所以她轉向假海龜,說:「你還要學什麼?」

passages.original: “Well, there was Mystery,” the Mock Turtle replied, counting off the subjects on his flappers, “—Mystery, ancient and modern, with Seaography: then Drawling—the Drawling-master was an old conger-eel, that used to come once a week: he taught us Drawling, Stretching, and Fainting in Coils.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,仲有神祕學(Mystery),」假海龜回答,用鰭掰著手指數科目,「——古代同現代嘅神祕學,仲有海洋學(Seaography):然後係拖腔(Drawling)——拖腔老師係一條老康吉鰻,每週嚟一次:佢教我哋拖腔、拉伸同盤繞中昏厥(Drawling, Stretching, and Fainting in Coils)。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,還有神祕學(Mystery),」假海龜回答,用鰭掰著手指數科目,「——古代和現代的神祕學,還有海洋學(Seaography):然後是拖腔(Drawling)——拖腔老師是一條老康吉鰻,每週來一次:他教我們拖腔、拉伸和盤繞中昏厥(Drawling, Stretching, and Fainting in Coils)。」

passages.original: “What was that like?” said Alice.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係乜嘢樣嘅?」愛麗絲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是什麼樣的?」愛麗絲說。

passages.original: “Well, I can’t show it you myself,” the Mock Turtle said: “I’m too stiff. And the Gryphon never learnt it.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我自己唔能夠畀你演示,」假海龜講:「我太僵硬喇。而獅鷲從冇學過。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我自己不能給你演示,」假海龜說:「我太僵硬了。而獅鷲從沒學過。」

passages.original: “Hadn’t time,” said the Gryphon: “I went to the Classics master, though. He was an old crab, he was.”
passages.vernacular: 「冇時間,」獅鷲講:「不過我去上咗古典課老師嘅課。佢係一隻老螃蟹,係嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒時間,」獅鷲說:「不過我去上了古典課老師的課。他是一隻老螃蟹,是的。」

passages.original: “I never went to him,” the Mock Turtle said with a sigh: “he taught Laughing and Grief, they used to say.”
passages.vernacular: 「我從冇去過佢嗰兒,」假海龜嘆氣講:「佢哋講佢教笑同悲(Laughing and Grief)。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我從沒去過他那兒,」假海龜嘆氣說:「他們說他教笑與悲(Laughing and Grief)。」

passages.original: “So he did, so he did,” said the Gryphon, sighing in his turn; and both creatures hid their faces in their paws.
passages.vernacular: 「佢確實教,佢確實教,」獅鷲講,輪到佢嘆息喇;兩個生物都把臉埋喺爪子裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他確實教,他確實教,」獅鷲說,輪到它嘆息了;兩個生物都把臉埋在爪子裡。

passages.original: “And how many hours a day did you do lessons?” said Alice, in a hurry to change the subject.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰你哋一天上幾個鐘頭嘅課?」愛麗絲講,急忙想轉換話題。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那你們一天上幾個鐘頭的課?」愛麗絲說,急忙想轉換話題。

passages.original: “Ten hours the first day,” said the Mock Turtle: “nine the next, and so on.”
passages.vernacular: 「第一天十個鐘頭,」假海龜講:「第二天九個鐘頭,依此類推。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「第一天十個鐘頭,」假海龜說:「第二天九個鐘頭,依此類推。」

passages.original: “What a curious plan!” exclaimed Alice.
passages.vernacular: 「多奇怪嘅安排!」愛麗絲驚呼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「多奇怪的安排!」愛麗絲驚呼。

passages.original: “That’s the reason they’re called lessons,” the Gryphon remarked: “because they lessen from day to day.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢個就係佢哋被叫做課(lessons)嘅原因,」獅鷲講:「因為佢哋一天比一天減少(lessen)。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這就是它們被叫做課(lessons)的原因,」獅鷲說:「因為它們一天比一天減少(lessen)。」

passages.original: This was quite a new idea to Alice, and she thought it over a little before she made her next remark. “Then the eleventh day must have been a holiday?”
passages.vernacular: 呢對愛麗絲來講係個全新嘅想法,佢想咗一會兒才講下一句話。「咁第十一天一定係假日?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這對愛麗絲來說是個全新的想法,她想了一會兒才說下一句話。「那麼第十一天一定是假日?」

passages.original: “Of course it was,” said the Mock Turtle.
passages.vernacular: 「當然係,」假海龜講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然是,」假海龜說。

passages.original: “And how did you manage on the twelfth?” Alice went on eagerly.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰第十二天你哋點算?」愛麗絲急切地接住問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那第十二天你們怎麼辦?」愛麗絲急切地接著問。

passages.original: “That’s enough about lessons,” the Gryphon interrupted in a very decided tone: “tell her something about the games now.”
passages.vernacular: 「關於課夠喇,」獅鷲用好堅決嘅語調打斷:「而家跟佢講講遊戲吧。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「關於課夠了,」獅鷲用非常堅決的語調打斷:「現在跟她說說遊戲吧。」

chapters.title: Ch. X The Lobster Quadrille 第十章:龍蝦方塊舞

passages.original: The Mock Turtle sighed deeply, and drew the back of one flapper across his eyes. He looked at Alice, and tried to speak, but for a minute or two sobs choked his voice. “Same as if he had a bone in his throat,” said the Gryphon: and it set to work shaking him and punching him in the back. At last the Mock Turtle recovered his voice, and, with tears running down his cheeks, he went on again:—
passages.vernacular: 假海龜深深嘆咗口氣,用一隻鰭嘅背面抹過眼睛。佢睇住愛麗絲,試住講話,但有一兩分鐘啜泣哽住咗佢嘅聲音。「就像喉嚨裡卡咗一根骨頭,」獅鷲講:佢動手搖晃佢,捶佢嘅背。最後假海龜恢復咗聲音,臉頰上淌住淚,又接住講:——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 假海龜深深嘆了口氣,用一隻鰭的背面抹過眼睛。他看著愛麗絲,試著說話,但有一兩分鐘啜泣哽住了他的聲音。「就像喉嚨裡卡了一根骨頭,」獅鷲說:它動手搖晃他,捶他的背。最後假海龜恢復了聲音,臉頰上淌著淚,又接著說:——

passages.original: “You may not have lived much under the sea—” (“I haven’t,” said Alice)—“and perhaps you were never even introduced to a lobster—” (Alice began to say “I once tasted—” but checked herself hastily, and said “No, never”) “—so you can have no idea what a delightful thing a Lobster Quadrille is!”
passages.vernacular: 「你或者喺海底下冇住過多久——」(「我冇,」愛麗絲講)——「或者你甚至從冇被介紹畀龍蝦——」(愛麗絲開始講「我曾經嘗過——」但急忙止住,講「不,從冇」)「——所以你肯定唔知道龍蝦方塊舞係幾咁令人愉快嘅事!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你也許在海底下沒住過多久——」(「我沒有,」愛麗絲說)——「也許你甚至從沒被介紹給龍蝦——」(愛麗絲開始說「我曾經嘗過——」但急忙止住,說「不,從沒有」)「——所以你肯定不知道龍蝦方塊舞是多麼令人愉快的事!」

passages.original: “No, indeed,” said Alice. “What sort of a dance is it?”
passages.vernacular: 「確實唔知道,」愛麗絲講。「嗰個係一種乜嘢舞?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「確實不知道,」愛麗絲說。「那是一種什麼舞?」

passages.original: “Why,” said the Gryphon, “you first form into a line along the sea-shore—”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,」獅鷲講,「你哋首先沿住海岸排成一行——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,」獅鷲說,「你們首先沿著海岸排成一行——」

passages.original: “Two lines!” cried the Mock Turtle. “Seals, turtles, salmon, and so on; then, when you’ve cleared all the jelly-fish out of the way—”
passages.vernacular: 「兩行!」假海龜喊道。「海豹、海龜、鮭魚,等等;然後,等你把所有水母都清出路之後——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「兩行!」假海龜喊道。「海豹、海龜、鮭魚,等等;然後,等你把所有水母都清出路之後——」

passages.original: “That generally takes some time,” interrupted the Gryphon.
passages.vernacular: 「呢通常要花啲時間,」獅鷲打斷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這通常要花一些時間,」獅鷲打斷。

passages.original: “—you advance twice—”
passages.vernacular: 「——你哋前進兩步——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「——你們前進兩步——」

passages.original: “Each with a lobster as a partner!” cried the Gryphon.
passages.vernacular: 「每個都帶一隻龍蝦做舞伴!」獅鷲喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「每個都帶一隻龍蝦做舞伴!」獅鷲喊道。

passages.original: “Of course,” the Mock Turtle said: “advance twice, set to partners—”
passages.vernacular: 「當然,」假海龜講:「前進兩步,各就舞伴——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然,」假海龜說:「前進兩步,各就舞伴——」

passages.original: “—change lobsters, and retire in same order,” continued the Gryphon.
passages.vernacular: 「——換龍蝦,按同樣順序後退,」獅鷲接住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「——換龍蝦,按同樣順序後退,」獅鷲接著說。

passages.original: “Then, you know,” the Mock Turtle went on, “you throw the—”
passages.vernacular: 「然後,你知道,」假海龜接住講,「你把嗰——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「然後,你知道,」假海龜接著說,「你把那——」

passages.original: “The lobsters!” shouted the Gryphon, with a bound into the air.
passages.vernacular: 「龍蝦!」獅鷲喊道,猛地躍到空中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「龍蝦!」獅鷲喊道,猛地躍到空中。

passages.original: “—as far out to sea as you can—”
passages.vernacular: 「——儘可能遠地扔到海裡去——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「——儘可能遠地扔到海裡去——」

passages.original: “Swim after them!” screamed the Gryphon.
passages.vernacular: 「游住追佢哋!」獅鷲尖叫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「游著追它們!」獅鷲尖叫。

passages.original: “Turn a somersault in the sea!” cried the Mock Turtle, capering wildly about.
passages.vernacular: 「喺海裡翻個跟頭!」假海龜喊道,瘋狂地蹦跳住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在海裡翻個跟頭!」假海龜喊道,瘋狂地蹦跳著。

passages.original: “Change lobsters again!” yelled the Gryphon at the top of its voice.
passages.vernacular: 「再換龍蝦!」獅鷲用盡全力大聲喊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「再換龍蝦!」獅鷲用盡全力大聲喊。

passages.original: “Back to land again, and that’s all the first figure,” said the Mock Turtle, suddenly dropping his voice; and the two creatures, who had been jumping about like mad things all this time, sat down again very sadly and quietly, and looked at Alice.
passages.vernacular: 「回到岸上,呢個就係第一式全部喇,」假海龜講,突然壓低聲音;兩個一直像瘋子一樣蹦跳嘅生物,又好悲傷、安靜地坐下嚟,睇住愛麗絲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「回到岸上,這就是第一式全部了,」假海龜說,突然壓低聲音;兩個一直像瘋子一樣蹦跳的生物,又非常悲傷、安靜地坐下來,看著愛麗絲。

passages.original: “It must be a very pretty dance,” said Alice timidly.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰一定係一支好漂亮嘅舞,」愛麗絲膽怯地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那一定是一支非常漂亮的舞,」愛麗絲膽怯地說。

passages.original: “Would you like to see a little of it?” said the Mock Turtle.
passages.vernacular: 「你想睇啲嗎?」假海龜講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你想看一點嗎?」假海龜說。

passages.original: “Very much indeed,” said Alice.
passages.vernacular: 「好想,」愛麗絲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「非常想,」愛麗絲說。

passages.original: “Come, let’s try the first figure!” said the Mock Turtle to the Gryphon. “We can do without lobsters, you know. Which shall sing?”
passages.vernacular: 「嚟,我哋試試第一式!」假海龜對獅鷲講。「我哋可以唔使龍蝦,你知道。邊個嚟唱?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「來,我們試試第一式!」假海龜對獅鷲說。「我們可以不用龍蝦,你知道。誰來唱?」

passages.original: “Oh, you sing,” said the Gryphon. “I’ve forgotten the words.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,你唱,」獅鷲講。「我把詞忘喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,你唱,」獅鷲說。「我把詞忘了。」

passages.original: So they began solemnly dancing round and round Alice, every now and then treading on her toes when they passed too close, and waving their forepaws to mark the time, while the Mock Turtle sang this, very slowly and sadly:—
passages.vernacular: 於是佢哋開始莊重地繞住愛麗絲一圈又一圈地跳舞,時不時經過太近時踩到佢嘅腳趾,並揮動前爪打拍子,假海龜好緩慢而悲傷地唱起呢首:——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是他們開始莊重地繞著愛麗絲一圈又一圈地跳舞,時不時經過太近時踩到她的腳趾,並揮動前爪打拍子,假海龜非常緩慢而悲傷地唱起這首:——

passages.original: “Will you walk a little faster?” said a whiting to a snail. “There’s a porpoise close behind us, and he’s treading on my tail. See how eagerly the lobsters and the turtles all advance! They are waiting on the shingle—will you come and join the dance? Will you, won’t you, will you, won’t you, will you join the dance? Will you, won’t you, will you, won’t you, won’t you join the dance?
passages.vernacular: 「『你能走快啲嗎?』鱈魚對蝸牛講。『有一隻海豚緊跟喺我哋後面,佢喺踩我嘅尾巴。睇龍蝦同海龜都幾咁熱切地前進!佢哋喺鵝卵石灘上等住——你要嚟加入舞蹈嗎?你願意,你唔願意,你願意,你唔願意,你願意加入舞蹈嗎?你願意,你唔願意,你願意,你唔願意,你唔願意加入舞蹈嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『你能走快一點嗎?』鱈魚對蝸牛說。『有一隻海豚緊跟在我們後面,他在踩我的尾巴。看龍蝦和海龜都多麼熱切地前進!他們在鵝卵石灘上等著——你要來加入舞蹈嗎?你願意,你不願意,你願意,你不願意,你願意加入舞蹈嗎?你願意,你不願意,你願意,你不願意,你不願意加入舞蹈嗎?

passages.original: “You can really have no notion how delightful it will be When they take us up and throw us, with the lobsters, out to sea!” But the snail replied “Too far, too far!” and gave a look askance— Said he thanked the whiting kindly, but he would not join the dance. Would not, could not, would not, could not, would not join the dance. Would not, could not, would not, could not, could not join the dance.
passages.vernacular: 「『你真嘅想像不出會有幾咁美妙,當佢哋把我哋抓起嚟,連同龍蝦,扔到海裡去嘅時候!』可蝸牛回答『太遠喇,太遠喇!』並斜睨一眼——講佢誠懇地謝謝鱈魚,但佢唔會加入舞蹈。唔會,唔能夠,唔會,唔能夠,唔會加入舞蹈。唔會,唔能夠,唔會,唔能夠,唔能夠加入舞蹈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『你真的想像不出會有多麼美妙,當他們把我們抓起來,連同龍蝦,扔到海裡去的時候!』可蝸牛回答『太遠了,太遠了!』並斜睨一眼——說他誠懇地謝謝鱈魚,但他不會加入舞蹈。不會,不能,不會,不能,不會加入舞蹈。不會,不能,不會,不能,不能加入舞蹈。

passages.original: “What matters it how far we go?” his scaly friend replied. “There is another shore, you know, upon the other side. The further off from England the nearer is to France— Then turn not pale, beloved snail, but come and join the dance. Will you, won’t you, will you, won’t you, will you join the dance? Will you, won’t you, will you, won’t you, won’t you join the dance?”
passages.vernacular: 『走多遠有乜嘢關係?』佢有鱗嘅朋友回答。『你知道,另一邊仲有另一個海岸。離英格蘭越遠,離法國就越近——所以別發白,親愛嘅蝸牛,嚟加入舞蹈吧。你願意,你唔願意,你願意,你唔願意,你願意加入舞蹈嗎?你願意,你唔願意,你願意,你唔願意,你唔願意加入舞蹈嗎?』」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 『走多遠有什麼關係?』他有鱗的朋友回答。『你知道,另一邊還有另一個海岸。離英格蘭越遠,離法國就越近——所以別發白,親愛的蝸牛,來加入舞蹈吧。你願意,你不願意,你願意,你不願意,你願意加入舞蹈嗎?你願意,你不願意,你願意,你不願意,你不願意加入舞蹈嗎?』」

passages.original: “Thank you, it’s a very interesting dance to watch,” said Alice, feeling very glad that it was over at last: “and I do so like that curious song about the whiting!”
passages.vernacular: 「謝謝,呢個係一支睇起嚟好有趣嘅舞,」愛麗絲講,好高興佢終於結束喇:「我真鍾意嗰首關於鱈魚嘅奇怪嘅歌!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「謝謝,這是一支看起來非常有趣的舞,」愛麗絲說,很高興它終於結束了:「我真喜歡那首關於鱈魚的奇怪的歌!」

passages.original: “Oh, as to the whiting,” said the Mock Turtle, “they—you’ve seen them, of course?”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,講到鱈魚,」假海龜講,「佢哋——你當然見過佢哋?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,說到鱈魚,」假海龜說,「它們——你當然見過它們?」

passages.original: “Yes,” said Alice, “I’ve often seen them at dinn—” she checked herself hastily.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,」愛麗絲講,「我常喺晚飯(dinn)——」佢急忙止住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,」愛麗絲說,「我常在晚飯(dinn)——」她急忙止住了。

passages.original: “I don’t know where Dinn may be,” said the Mock Turtle, “but if you’ve seen them so often, of course you know what they’re like.”
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道晚飯(Dinn)喺邊兒,」假海龜講,「但如果你見過佢哋咁多次,你當然知道佢哋係乜嘢樣子嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道晚飯(Dinn)在哪兒,」假海龜說,「但如果你見過它們那麼多次,你當然知道它們是什麼樣子的。」

passages.original: “I believe so,” Alice replied thoughtfully. “They have their tails in their mouths—and they’re all over crumbs.”
passages.vernacular: 「我想係嘅,」愛麗絲若有所思地回答。「佢哋把尾巴含喺嘴裡——而且滿身都係麵包屑。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想是的,」愛麗絲若有所思地回答。「它們把尾巴含在嘴裡——而且滿身都是麵包屑。」

passages.original: “You’re wrong about the crumbs,” said the Mock Turtle: “crumbs would all wash off in the sea. But they have their tails in their mouths; and the reason is—” here the Mock Turtle yawned and shut his eyes.—“Tell her about the reason and all that,” he said to the Gryphon.
passages.vernacular: 「麵包屑你講錯喇,」假海龜講:「麵包屑喺海裡都會被沖掉。但係佢哋確實把尾巴含喺嘴裡;原因係——」呢陣假海龜打咗個哈欠,閉上咗眼睛。——「把原因同嗰一切都告訴佢,」佢對獅鷲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「麵包屑你說錯了,」假海龜說:「麵包屑在海裡都會被沖掉。但是它們確實把尾巴含在嘴裡;原因是——」這時假海龜打了個哈欠,閉上了眼睛。——「把原因和那一切都告訴她,」他對獅鷲說。

passages.original: “The reason is,” said the Gryphon, “that they would go with the lobsters to the dance. So they got thrown out to sea. So they had to fall a long way. So they got their tails fast in their mouths. So they couldn’t get them out again. That’s all.”
passages.vernacular: 「原因係,」獅鷲講,「佢哋要同龍蝦一起去跳舞。所以佢哋被扔到海裡。所以佢哋唔得不掉咗好遠。所以佢哋把尾巴牢牢含喺咗嘴裡。所以佢哋再都拔不出嚟喇。就呢啲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「原因是,」獅鷲說,「它們要和龍蝦一起去跳舞。所以它們被扔到海裡。所以它們不得不掉了很遠。所以它們把尾巴牢牢含在了嘴裡。所以它們再也拔不出來了。就這些。」

passages.original: “Thank you,” said Alice, “it’s very interesting. I never knew so much about a whiting before.”
passages.vernacular: 「謝謝,」愛麗絲講,「呢個好有趣。我以前從唔知道關於鱈魚咁多。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「謝謝,」愛麗絲說,「這非常有趣。我以前從不知道關於鱈魚這麼多。」

passages.original: “I can tell you more than that, if you like,” said the Gryphon. “Do you know why it’s called a whiting?”
passages.vernacular: 「我仲能告訴你更多,如果你願意,」獅鷲講。「你知道佢點解叫鱈魚(whiting,都指白粉)嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我還能告訴你更多,如果你願意,」獅鷲說。「你知道它為什麼叫鱈魚(whiting,也指白粉)嗎?」

passages.original: “I never thought about it,” said Alice. “Why?”
passages.vernacular: 「我從冇想過,」愛麗絲講。「點解?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我從沒想過,」愛麗絲說。「為什麼?」

passages.original: “It does the boots and shoes,” the Gryphon replied very solemnly.
passages.vernacular: 「佢擦靴子同鞋子,」獅鷲好莊重地回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「它擦靴子和鞋子,」獅鷲非常莊重地回答。

passages.original: Alice was thoroughly puzzled. “Does the boots and shoes!” she repeated in a wondering tone.
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲徹底糊塗喇。「擦靴子同鞋子!」佢用驚奇嘅語調重複。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲徹底糊塗了。「擦靴子和鞋子!」她用驚奇的語調重複。

passages.original: “Why, what are your shoes done with?” said the Gryphon. “I mean, what makes them so shiny?”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,你嘅鞋子係用乜嘢擦嘅?」獅鷲講。「我係講,係乜嘢讓佢哋咁亮?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,你的鞋子是用什麼擦的?」獅鷲說。「我是說,是什麼讓它們這麼亮?」

passages.original: Alice looked down at them, and considered a little before she gave her answer. “They’re done with blacking, I believe.”
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲低頭睇睇佢哋,想咗想才回答。「係用鞋油擦嘅,我想。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲低頭看看它們,想了想才回答。「是用鞋油擦的,我想。」

passages.original: “Boots and shoes under the sea,” the Gryphon went on in a deep voice, “are done with a whiting. Now you know.”
passages.vernacular: 「海底嘅靴子同鞋子,」獅鷲用低沉嘅聲音接住講,「係用鱈魚(白粉)擦嘅。而家你知道喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「海底的靴子和鞋子,」獅鷲用低沉的聲音接著說,「是用鱈魚(白粉)擦的。現在你知道了。」

passages.original: “And what are they made of?” Alice asked in a tone of great curiosity.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰佢哋係用乜嘢做嘅?」愛麗絲用好好奇嘅語調問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那它們是用什麼做的?」愛麗絲用非常好奇的語調問。

passages.original: “Soles and eels, of course,” the Gryphon replied rather impatiently: “any shrimp could have told you that.”
passages.vernacular: 「鰨魚底同鰻魚,當然,」獅鷲相當不耐煩地回答:「任何一隻蝦都能告訴你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「鰨魚底和鰻魚,當然,」獅鷲相當不耐煩地回答:「任何一隻蝦都能告訴你。」

passages.original: “If I’d been the whiting,” said Alice, whose thoughts were still running on the song, “I’d have said to the porpoise, ‘Keep back, please: we don’t want you with us!’”
passages.vernacular: 「如果我係鱈魚,」愛麗絲講,佢嘅思緒仍然停留喺嗰首歌上,「我會對海豚講:『請走開:我哋唔好你跟住!』」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果我是鱈魚,」愛麗絲說,她的思緒仍然停留在那首歌上,「我會對海豚說:『請走開:我們不要你跟著!』」

passages.original: “They were obliged to have him with them,” the Mock Turtle said: “no wise fish would go anywhere without a porpoise.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋唔得不讓佢跟住,」假海龜講:「聰明嘅魚邊兒都唔會不帶海豚就去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們不得不讓他跟著,」假海龜說:「聰明的魚哪兒都不會不帶海豚就去。」

passages.original: “Wouldn’t it really?” said Alice in a tone of great surprise.
passages.vernacular: 「真嘅唔會嗎?」愛麗絲用好驚訝嘅語調講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真的不會嗎?」愛麗絲用非常驚訝的語調說。

passages.original: “Of course not,” said the Mock Turtle: “why, if a fish came to me, and told me he was going a journey, I should say ‘With what porpoise?’”
passages.vernacular: 「當然唔會,」假海龜講:「哎呀,如果一條魚嚟找我,告訴我佢要出遠門,我會講『帶乜嘢海豚(porpoise)?』」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然不會,」假海龜說:「哎呀,如果一條魚來找我,告訴我他要出遠門,我會說『帶什麼海豚(porpoise)?』」

passages.original: “Don’t you mean ‘purpose’?” said Alice.
passages.vernacular: 「你唔係講『目的』(purpose)嗎?」愛麗絲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你不是說『目的』(purpose)嗎?」愛麗絲說。

passages.original: “I mean what I say,” the Mock Turtle replied in an offended tone. And the Gryphon added “Come, let’s hear some of your adventures.”
passages.vernacular: 「我講嘅就係我講嘅,」假海龜用被冒犯嘅語調回答。獅鷲補充:「嚟,讓我哋聽聽你嘅啲冒險。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我說的就是我說的,」假海龜用被冒犯的語調回答。獅鷲補充:「來,讓我們聽聽你的一些冒險。」

passages.original: “I could tell you my adventures—beginning from this morning,” said Alice a little timidly: “but it’s no use going back to yesterday, because I was a different person then.”
passages.vernacular: 「我可以告訴你哋我嘅冒險——從今日早晨開始,」愛麗絲有點膽怯地講:「但回到尋日冇用,因為嗰時我係另一個人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我可以告訴你們我的冒險——從今天早晨開始,」愛麗絲有點膽怯地說:「但回到昨天沒用,因為那時我是另一個人。」

passages.original: “Explain all that,” said the Mock Turtle.
passages.vernacular: 「把呢一切解釋一下,」假海龜講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「把這一切解釋一下,」假海龜說。

passages.original: “No, no! The adventures first,” said the Gryphon in an impatient tone: “explanations take such a dreadful time.”
passages.vernacular: 「不,不!先講冒險,」獅鷲用不耐煩嘅語調講:「解釋要花太多時間。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,不!先說冒險,」獅鷲用不耐煩的語調說:「解釋要花太多時間。」

passages.original: So Alice began telling them her adventures from the time when she first saw the White Rabbit. She was a little nervous about it just at first, the two creatures got so close to her, one on each side, and opened their eyes and mouths so very wide, but she gained courage as she went on. Her listeners were perfectly quiet till she got to the part about her repeating “You are old, Father William,” to the Caterpillar, and the words all coming different, and then the Mock Turtle drew a long breath, and said “That’s very curious.”
passages.vernacular: 於是愛麗絲開始畀佢哋講佢嘅冒險,從佢第一次睇見白兔嘅時候講起。起初佢有點緊張,兩個生物挨得佢咁近,一邊一個,把眼睛同嘴張得咁大,但隨住講述佢鼓起咗勇氣。佢嘅聽眾完全安靜,直到佢講到對毛毛蟲背誦「你老喇,威廉爹爹」,而詞全都變喇,呢陣假海龜長長地吸咗口氣,講:「呢個好奇怪。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是愛麗絲開始給他們講她的冒險,從她第一次看見白兔的時候講起。起初她有點緊張,兩個生物挨得她那麼近,一邊一個,把眼睛和嘴張得那麼大,但隨著講述她鼓起了勇氣。她的聽眾完全安靜,直到她講到對毛毛蟲背誦「你老了,威廉爹爹」,而詞全都變了,這時假海龜長長地吸了口氣,說:「這非常奇怪。」

passages.original: “It’s all about as curious as it can be,” said the Gryphon.
passages.vernacular: 「奇怪得唔能夠再奇怪喇,」獅鷲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「奇怪得不能再奇怪了,」獅鷲說。

passages.original: “It all came different!” the Mock Turtle repeated thoughtfully. “I should like to hear her try and repeat something now. Tell her to begin.” He looked at the Gryphon as if he thought it had some kind of authority over Alice.
passages.vernacular: 「全都變喇!」假海龜若有所思地重複。「我想聽佢而家試住背誦點乜嘢。叫佢開始。」佢睇住獅鷲,好像認為佢對愛麗絲有某種權威。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「全都變了!」假海龜若有所思地重複。「我想聽她現在試著背誦點什麼。叫她開始。」他看著獅鷲,好像認為它對愛麗絲有某種權威。

passages.original: “Stand up and repeat ‘’Tis the voice of the sluggard,’” said the Gryphon.
passages.vernacular: 「站起嚟背『呢個係懶漢嘅聲音』,」獅鷲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「站起來背『這是懶漢的聲音』,」獅鷲說。

passages.original: “How the creatures order one about, and make one repeat lessons!” thought Alice; “I might as well be at school at once.” However, she got up, and began to repeat it, but her head was so full of the Lobster Quadrille, that she hardly knew what she was saying, and the words came very queer indeed:—
passages.vernacular: 「呢啲生物點咁樣支使人,仲讓人背功課!」愛麗絲想:「我仲不如即刻就喺學校裡。」不過,佢站起嚟,開始背,但佢嘅腦子裡滿係龍蝦方塊舞,佢幾乎唔知道自己喺講乜嘢,詞句確實出得好古怪:——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這些生物怎麼這樣支使人,還讓人背功課!」愛麗絲想:「我還不如馬上就在學校裡。」不過,她站起來,開始背,但她的腦子裡滿是龍蝦方塊舞,她幾乎不知道自己在說什麼,詞句確實出得非常古怪:——

passages.original: “’Tis the voice of the Lobster; I heard him declare, “You have baked me too brown, I must sugar my hair.” As a duck with its eyelids, so he with his nose Trims his belt and his buttons, and turns out his toes.”
passages.vernacular: 「『呢個係龍蝦嘅聲音;我聽見佢宣布,「你把我烤得太棕喇,我得畀頭髮撒點糖。」就像鴨子用眼皮,佢用佢嘅鼻子,修整佢嘅腰帶同紐扣,把腳趾向外翻。』」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『這是龍蝦的聲音;我聽見他宣布,「你把我烤得太棕了,我得給頭髮撒點糖。」就像鴨子用眼皮,他用他的鼻子,修整他的腰帶和紐扣,把腳趾向外翻。』」

passages.original: [later editions continued as follows When the sands are all dry, he is gay as a lark, And will talk in contemptuous tones of the Shark, But, when the tide rises and sharks are around, His voice has a timid and tremulous sound.]
passages.vernacular: [後來嘅版本接下嚟係咁樣嘅:沙子都乾咗時,佢快活得像雲雀,並會用輕蔑嘅語調談論鯊魚,但係,潮水漲起、鯊魚喺周圍時,佢嘅聲音就有一種膽怯而顫抖嘅聲響。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [後來的版本接下來是這樣的:沙子都乾了時,他快活得像雲雀,並會用輕蔑的語調談論鯊魚,但是,潮水漲起、鯊魚在周圍時,他的聲音就有一種膽怯而顫抖的聲響。]

passages.original: “That’s different from what I used to say when I was a child,” said the Gryphon.
passages.vernacular: 「呢同我小時候念嘅不一樣,」獅鷲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這和我小時候念的不一樣,」獅鷲說。

passages.original: “Well, I never heard it before,” said the Mock Turtle; “but it sounds uncommon nonsense.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我以前從冇聽過,」假海龜講;「但聽起嚟係不尋常嘅胡講。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我以前從沒聽過,」假海龜說;「但聽起來是不尋常的胡說。」

passages.original: Alice said nothing; she had sat down with her face in her hands, wondering if anything would ever happen in a natural way again.
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲冇講話;佢坐咗下嚟,雙手捧住臉,唔知仲有冇乜嘢事會再以自然嘅方式發生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲沒說話;她坐了下來,雙手捧著臉,不知還有沒有什麼事會再以自然的方式發生。

passages.original: “I should like to have it explained,” said the Mock Turtle.
passages.vernacular: 「我想要把佢解釋一下,」假海龜講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想要把它解釋一下,」假海龜說。

passages.original: “She can’t explain it,” said the Gryphon hastily. “Go on with the next verse.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢解釋不喇,」獅鷲急忙講。「接住背下一節。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她解釋不了,」獅鷲急忙說。「接著背下一節。」

passages.original: “But about his toes?” the Mock Turtle persisted. “How could he turn them out with his nose, you know?”
passages.vernacular: 「但係講到佢嘅腳趾?」假海龜堅持。「佢點能用鼻子把佢哋翻向外邊呢,你知道?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但是說到他的腳趾?」假海龜堅持。「他怎麼能用鼻子把它們翻向外邊呢,你知道?」

passages.original: “It’s the first position in dancing.” Alice said; but was dreadfully puzzled by the whole thing, and longed to change the subject.
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係舞蹈中嘅第一位置。」愛麗絲講;但被整件事弄得糊塗極喇,渴望轉換話題。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是舞蹈中的第一位置。」愛麗絲說;但被整件事弄得糊塗極了,渴望轉換話題。

passages.original: “Go on with the next verse,” the Gryphon repeated impatiently: “it begins ‘I passed by his garden.’”
passages.vernacular: 「接住背下一節,」獅鷲不耐煩地重複:「佢開頭係『我經過佢嘅花園』。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「接著背下一節,」獅鷲不耐煩地重複:「它開頭是『我經過他的花園』。」

passages.original: Alice did not dare to disobey, though she felt sure it would all come wrong, and she went on in a trembling voice:—
passages.vernacular: 愛麗絲唔敢違抗,雖然佢確信一切都會出錯,佢用顫抖嘅聲音接住背:——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛麗絲不敢違抗,雖然她確信一切都會出錯,她用顫抖的聲音接著背:——

passages.original: “I passed by his garden, and marked, with one eye, How the Owl and the Panther were sharing a pie—”
passages.vernacular: 「『我經過佢嘅花園,用一隻眼注意到,貓頭鷹同豹正在分享一個餡餅——』」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『我經過他的花園,用一隻眼注意到,貓頭鷹和豹正在分享一個餡餅——』」

passages.original: [later editions continued as follows The Panther took pie-crust, and gravy, and meat, While the Owl had the dish as its share of the treat. When the pie was all finished, the Owl, as a boon, Was kindly permitted to pocket the spoon: While the Panther received knife and fork with a growl, And concluded the banquet—]
passages.vernacular: [後來嘅版本接下嚟係咁樣嘅:豹攞咗餡餅皮、肉汁同肉,而貓頭鷹分到嘅係盤子,作為享受嘅份額。餡餅食完,貓頭鷹作為恩惠,被好心允許把勺子裝進口袋:而豹得到刀叉,伴住一聲咆哮,結束咗盛宴——]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [後來的版本接下來是這樣的:豹拿了餡餅皮、肉汁和肉,而貓頭鷹分到的是盤子,作為享受的份額。餡餅吃完,貓頭鷹作為恩惠,被好心允許把勺子裝進口袋:而豹得到刀叉,伴著一聲咆哮,結束了盛宴——]

passages.original: “What is the use of repeating all that stuff,” the Mock Turtle interrupted, “if you don’t explain it as you go on? It’s by far the most confusing thing I ever heard!”
passages.vernacular: 「重複所有呢啲廢話有乜嘢用,」假海龜打斷,「如果你一邊背一邊不解釋?呢個係我聽過最令人困惑嘅嘢!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「重複所有這些廢話有什麼用,」假海龜打斷,「如果你一邊背一邊不解釋?這是我聽過最令人困惑的東西!」

passages.original: “Yes, I think you’d better leave off,” said the Gryphon: and Alice was only too glad to do so.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,我想你最好停下,」獅鷲講:愛麗絲求之唔得。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,我想你最好停下,」獅鷲說:愛麗絲求之不得。

passages.original: “Shall we try another figure of the Lobster Quadrille?” the Gryphon went on. “Or would you like the Mock Turtle to sing you a song?”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋要唔好試試龍蝦方塊舞嘅另一個舞式?」獅鷲接住講。「定係你想讓假海龜畀你唱首歌?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們要不要試試龍蝦方塊舞的另一個舞式?」獅鷲接著說。「還是你想讓假海龜給你唱首歌?」

passages.original: “Oh, a song, please, if the Mock Turtle would be so kind,” Alice replied, so eagerly that the Gryphon said, in a rather offended tone, “Hm! No accounting for tastes! Sing her ‘Turtle Soup,’ will you, old fellow?”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,唱歌吧,請,如果假海龜肯咁好心嘅話,」愛麗絲講,咁急切,以至於獅鷲用相當被冒犯嘅語調講:「哼!真係眾口難調!畀佢唱《海龜湯》吧,老夥計?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,唱歌吧,請,如果假海龜肯那麼好心的話,」愛麗絲說,那麼急切,以至於獅鷲用相當被冒犯的語調說:「哼!真是眾口難調!給她唱《海龜湯》吧,老夥計?」

passages.original: The Mock Turtle sighed deeply, and began, in a voice sometimes choked with sobs, to sing this:—
passages.vernacular: 假海龜深深嘆咗口氣,開始用一個時而被啜泣哽住嘅聲音唱起呢首:——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 假海龜深深嘆了口氣,開始用一個時而被啜泣哽住的聲音唱起這首:——

passages.original: “Beautiful Soup, so rich and green, Waiting in a hot tureen! Who for such dainties would not stoop? Soup of the evening, beautiful Soup! Soup of the evening, beautiful Soup! Beau—ootiful Soo—oop! Beau—ootiful Soo—oop! Soo—oop of the e—e—evening, Beautiful, beautiful Soup!
passages.vernacular: 「美麗嘅湯,咁濃咁綠,喺熱湯碗中等候!為咁樣嘅美味邊個唔願屈身?晚餐嘅湯,美麗嘅湯!晚餐嘅湯,美麗嘅湯!美——麗嘅湯——!美——麗嘅湯——!晚——餐嘅湯——,美麗,美麗嘅湯!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「美麗的湯,那麼濃那麼綠,在熱湯碗中等候!為這樣的美味誰不願屈身?晚餐的湯,美麗的湯!晚餐的湯,美麗的湯!美——麗的湯——!美——麗的湯——!晚——餐的湯——,美麗,美麗的湯!

passages.original: “Beautiful Soup! Who cares for fish, Game, or any other dish? Who would not give all else for two p ennyworth only of beautiful Soup? Pennyworth only of beautiful Soup? Beau—ootiful Soo—oop! Beau—ootiful Soo—oop! Soo—oop of the e—e—evening, Beautiful, beauti—FUL SOUP!”
passages.vernacular: 「美麗嘅湯!邊個在乎魚、野味,或任何別嘅菜?邊個唔願放棄其餘嘅一切,只為兩便士嘅美麗嘅湯?只要一便士嘅美麗嘅湯?美——麗嘅湯——!美——麗嘅湯——!晚——餐嘅湯——,美麗,美麗——嘅湯!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「美麗的湯!誰在乎魚、野味,或任何別的菜?誰不願放棄其餘的一切,只為兩便士的美麗的湯?只要一便士的美麗的湯?美——麗的湯——!美——麗的湯——!晚——餐的湯——,美麗,美麗——的湯!」
